chapters.title: Chapter 1951: A Week of Time!
paragraphs: After Max agreed to represent her in the Bloodline Legacy Battle, Rose didn’t keep him in the ancestral hall for long.

She looked once more at the statue of the First Progenitor, and for a brief moment her expression turned complicated again. There was longing in her eyes, but also frustration, restraint, and a faint trace of resentment that had clearly been buried for years.
To the true heirs of the Four Sacred Clans, this statue represented origin, pride, and inheritance. To Rose, it represented everything she’d been denied since birth.
Then she turned away.
"Come with me," she said. "I’ll take you to the place prepared for you."

Max gave the statue one last glance before following her out of the sealed hall. The moment he stepped away from the chamber, the strange reaction inside his blood eased a little, though it didn’t vanish completely.
It stayed deep inside him like a disturbed echo, quiet for now but not settled. He couldn’t make sense of it, and since Rose was still beside him, he kept it to himself.

The gate closed behind them. The silver spatial chains around the hall tightened again, and the entrance disappeared beneath layers of folded space as if it had never existed. Rose led him through several hidden corridors that didn’t seem tied to normal distance.

Each corridor twisted gently and changed direction in ways that should have been impossible, yet Max’s Dimensional Sovereign Body could still follow the spatial logic behind them. The Evercrest Clan hadn’t just built a residence inside space. It had turned space itself into architecture.
Soon, they arrived at a quiet courtyard.
The courtyard sat on one of the higher branches of an enormous ancient tree. Its walls were made of pale green jade and living wood, and silver spatial runes flowed across the entrance like water.
A small magical pond lay at the center, surrounded by soft grass, flowering vines, and a few stone paths leading toward several rooms.
Above the courtyard, a faint dome of hidden space separated it from the outside world, giving the whole place a peaceful, isolated feel.
Rose stopped in front of the main room and looked at Max.
"This will be your residence until the Bloodline Legacy Battle begins."
Max looked around once. The place was quiet but not simple. The energy density here was extremely high, and the spatial runes hidden inside the walls were strong enough to block most forms of spying.
There was also a separate training chamber attached to the residence, and from the faint pressure coming off it, Max could tell it was built to withstand attacks from powerful geniuses.

Rose noticed him looking and explained, "Your room has its own training chamber. It can adjust pressure, simulate different spatial environments, and block most energy leakage. You can cultivate, stabilize your power, or train there without disturbing anyone."
Max nodded. "Good."

"The Bloodline Legacy Battle starts in one week," Rose continued. "Until then, you can rest here. I still need to sort out some things related to registering you as my representative, so I might not come around much these next few days."
"That’s fine."

Rose looked at him for a moment, then said, "Max, the Bloodline Legacy Battle isn’t like the Cosmic Ascension Conference. The conference was watched by the whole Divine Realm, so the rules had to look fair. The Four Sacred Clans have rules too, but theirs are older, harsher, and full of hidden meaning. Some people won’t be happy that I brought you here."
Max smiled faintly. "Then they can dislike me all they want. I’m here to fulfill a promise, not to entertain them."
Rose’s lips curved slightly. "I figured you’d say something like that."
She turned to leave, then paused at the entrance of the courtyard.
"Rest for now. I’ll send you information about the battle once I confirm the final list of participants."
Max nodded. "Go."
Rose looked at him one last time before stepping into a silver spatial ripple and disappearing from the courtyard.
The courtyard went quiet.

Max stood alone in the room prepared for him. For a while, he didn’t move. His gaze slowly drifted toward the direction of the ancestral hall, even though it was no longer visible from here. The image of the statue stayed clear in his mind.
The tall man with closed eyes. The calm face. The hand resting near his side. That indescribable presence that didn’t feel like tyranny, divinity, or ordinary supremacy, but something even stranger.
And more importantly, the reaction inside Max’s blood.

The moment he’d seen that statue, several powers inside him had stirred violently. His Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline had reacted. His Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline had trembled. His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline had pulsed. Even the deeper parts of his foundation had shown signs of movement.
That shouldn’t have happened.
Max frowned slightly.
’Why did my blood react like that?’

He couldn’t think of any clear reason. He didn’t know the First Progenitor of the Four Sacred Clans. He’d never heard his name, never seen his face, and never received any inheritance connected to him. Max’s major bloodlines and powers all had known sources.

The Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline came from the Black Dragon side. The Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline came from his mother’s lineage. The Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline had just been granted by the Primordial Race. His Dimensional Sovereign Body came from his Dimensional Keeper’s legacy.
None of them should have reacted so strongly to that statue. Unless there was a deeper connection he didn’t know about.
Max stayed silent for a long time. Then he shook his head. There was no point guessing without information.
The Bloodline Legacy Battle would start in a week. Rose had said the forbidden bloodline could only be properly shown inside the clan, and the ancestral statue had already caused a reaction.
As long as he stayed here, there would likely be more chances to uncover the truth.
For now, there was something more practical to handle.

chapters.title: Chapter 1952: A new attack!
paragraphs: Max walked toward the training chamber. The doors opened automatically, revealing a wide circular space reinforced with countless spatial runes.

The floor was black stone, the walls were layered with silver patterns, and the ceiling held several floating crystals that seemed able to adjust gravity, space pressure, and energy density. It was a solid chamber, especially for a guest room.
But Max didn’t plan to use only this chamber.
He raised his hand. Space rippled. A moment later, Max entered his Dimension of Time.

The world around him changed. The quiet Evercrest room disappeared, replaced by the familiar space where time flowed according to his will. Here, he could think, train, refine, and analyze far more deeply than in the outside world.
The week before the Bloodline Legacy Battle wasn’t long, but for Max, with the Dimension of Time at his disposal, it was enough to prepare a great deal.
He sat cross-legged at the center of the dimension. Soon, his thoughts turned to one battle in particular.
His battle with Revona.

Among all the fights in the Cosmic Ascension Conference, Revona had pushed him into the toughest spot. Damian’s sword had been terrifying. Ervin’s abyss had been dangerous. Orion’s stars had been powerful. Kaiden’s space path had run deep.
But Revona had been different.

Her Void Origin Eyes hadn’t just attacked him. They’d stripped him bare. They’d shut down his powers one after another. Return To Nothing had already been dangerous enough on its own, but Null Origin Tide had been the real problem.

The moment that pale gray tide spread out, Max’s draconic essences, Dragon Scales Transformation, Divine Veins, Divine King Punishment, Devouring Flames Domain, and even his clone’s time concept had all gotten stripped away or suppressed.
His Emotion Severing Path had barely held on, and even that had been weakened to a dangerous degree.

In the end, Max had turned to the Dimensional Keeper legacy. That power had let him stand beyond Revona’s level of nullification, cut through Null Origin Tide, and beat her. But Max didn’t like relying on a power he couldn’t fully control.

The Dimensional Keeper legacy was strong, but it wasn’t something he could call on as naturally as his own sword, bloodline, or Pseudo Cosmic Paths yet. In a real life-or-death fight, leaning on a power that might not answer at the right moment was foolish.
He needed another way. A way to beat Revona’s abilities without leaning on the Dimensional Keeper legacy.
Max closed his eyes. The battle replayed in his mind.

Revona standing calmly in the arena. The Void Origin Eyes opening fully. The Void Origin Realm spreading out. His attacks being traced, hollowed, delayed, and erased. His black flames devouring but never fully consuming Return To Nothing.
His Emotion Severing Path cutting connections, but struggling once her nullification spread out in every direction.
Then the Null Origin Tide. A wave that didn’t target one attack or one technique but flooded the whole battlefield with origin-level nullification. Dodging it wasn’t enough.
Overpowering it with raw force wasn’t enough either. It attacked the very existence of his powers before they could properly take shape.
Max’s thoughts sharpened.
’The problem wasn’t only strength. It was structure.’
Revona’s ability worked because her Void Origin Eyes could identify, trace, and nullify the foundation of whatever they touched.

If Max threw a normal attack, she could hollow it out. If he released a domain, she could weaken its source. If he used bloodline power, she could drag it toward emptiness. Even the Devouring Flames Domain, built for consuming things, still had a definable structure she could target.
In other words, anything clear enough to be understood could be nullified.
That was terrifying. But not unbeatable.
Max started thinking through possible counters.

The first was speed. If he attacked faster than Revona could properly trace, he might land a hit before her nullification finished forming. But against her fully awakened Void Origin Eyes, that wasn’t reliable.
Her perception was too sharp, and her past-life experience made her reactions almost inhuman.
The second was overwhelming force. If his attack went beyond what her current realm could nullify, it would break through.

That was essentially what the Dimensional Keeper legacy had done. But without relying on that legacy, Max needed another source of overwhelming authority. His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline might eventually help, but it was too newly integrated and not yet awake enough to work as a stable counter.

The third was concealment. If Revona couldn’t identify the true source of an attack, her nullification might lose precision. Max had already used the Devouring Flames Domain and a time clone to throw off her Void Origin Eyes, but that had only delayed her. It hadn’t solved the root problem.

The fourth was layering. If one attack carried multiple false structures, false sources, and shifting cores, Revona might end up nullifying the wrong layer first. While she stripped away one part, the true killing intent could slip through along another path. This one had potential.
Max opened his eyes slightly.
’An attack with no fixed origin. A sword strike whose source keeps shifting between bloodline, law, domain, body, emotion, and space.’
His gaze deepened. Revona’s Void Origin Eyes were terrifying because they could trace an attack back to its foundation.

So what if the foundation kept changing every instant? What if the attack carried several foundations at once? What if the visible source was fake, the second source was bait, and the true source only existed at the moment of impact?

Max raised one hand. A faint sword light appeared above his palm. The Emotion Severing Path flowed into it first. Then Divine King Punishment flickered around it as seven-colored lightning. Then the Devouring Flames Domain formed a thin black flame along the edge. Space folded faintly around the sword light.
The first attempt collapsed almost instantly.
Max frowned slightly. The powers rejected each other because their structures were too different. Emotion Severing wanted to cut connection.

Divine King Punishment wanted to judge and punish. Devouring Flames wanted to consume. Space wanted to shift and fold. If he forced them together carelessly, the result would be unstable and easy to read.
That wouldn’t work against Revona.
He let the sword light disperse and tried again. This time, he didn’t combine the powers from the outside. He started from the intent itself.

A sword meant to keep the enemy from locating its true source. A sword meant to keep changing its foundation. A sword meant to survive nullification by never staying one thing long enough to be fully erased.
Max’s expression settled into calm. He had one week outside. Inside the Dimension of Time, that could stretch into much longer.

He didn’t need to finish a perfect counter in one session. He just needed to start forming a path. The next time he faced Revona’s Null Origin Tide, he didn’t want to rely only on the Dimensional Keeper legacy.
He wanted an answer of his own.
Max lifted Dragonheart. His white hair moved slightly in the silent space.
"Let’s begin."
The Dimension of Time filled with sword light.

chapters.title: Chapter 1953: A Week Passed By!
paragraphs: A week wasn’t much time.
For ordinary people, seven days might feel like enough to rest, think, prepare, and slowly settle into a new environment.

But for someone like Max, who’d just stepped into the heart of the Evercrest Clan, learned the deeper secret behind the Four Sacred Clans, sensed a mysterious reaction from the statue of the First Progenitor, and was about to represent Rose in the Bloodline Legacy Battle, one week went by almost too fast.
Inside the Dimension of Time, though, that week stretched out much longer.
Max spent most of it cultivating, stabilizing, and training.
The Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline had fully settled into his body during this stretch.

At first, its presence had felt like a sleeping ancient ocean inside his blood, calm on the surface but unbelievably heavy underneath. Whenever he circulated his power, the bloodline responded with quiet authority, shaping his body, soul, laws, and even his Pseudo Cosmic Paths.
It didn’t clash with his other bloodlines as much as he’d expected. Instead, it seemed to settle at the very top of his foundation, like a supreme framework that could hold everything else together.
By the end of the week, Max had grown fully used to it. His body no longer felt strange when the Primordial Bloodline stirred. His laws no longer trembled when primordial energy flowed through them.
Even his Emotion Severing Path, Divine King Punishment, and Devouring Flames Domain had adapted to the new foundation.

They were still Pseudo Cosmic Paths, still unable to become true Cosmic Paths before the Divine Lord Realm, but they now carried a faint primordial quality that made them deeper and harder to shake loose.

His cultivation rose again too. The breakthrough didn’t come as violently as the jump from the 1st to the 5th level of the Law Refinement Realm, which had been forced along by the leftover integration energy of the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline.

This time, Max advanced through steady accumulation. He used the Dimension of Time to refine his laws, stabilize the new bloodline, digest the energy still sitting in his body, and keep polishing his foundation until the next small barrier loosened on its own.
On the sixth day by the outer world’s count, that barrier broke.
[Breakthrough Achieved.]
[Law Refinement Realm 6th Level.]

Max opened his eyes inside the Dimension of Time and felt the change settle in quietly. His aura hadn’t turned wildly unstable. It had simply grown deeper. The laws flowing around him were more condensed than before, and every movement of his power felt smoother.
The Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline circulated more naturally too, no longer like something newly acquired, but like something that had always belonged inside him.
Max didn’t spend the whole week only on cultivation, though. He kept thinking through his battle with Revona too.

Again and again, he replayed the moment Null Origin Tide had stripped his powers away. Again and again, he tested sword structures built to shift their source, hide their foundation, and survive nullification by refusing to stay fixed.
Many attempts failed. Some collapsed instantly. Some turned unstable. Some worked for a moment but lacked real power. Still, every failure taught him something.
By the time the seventh day came, Max hadn’t built a perfect counter to Revona’s Void Origin Eyes, but he’d taken the first real step.

A new sword concept was starting to take shape in his mind. A sword with a layered source. A sword with a shifting foundation. A sword that didn’t fight nullification through raw power alone, but through deception, shifting origin, and momentary truth.
It wasn’t finished yet. But it existed. That was enough for now.
On the seventh day, Max stepped out of the Dimension of Time.
The quiet room prepared for him inside the Evercrest Clan came back into view. The silver spatial runes on the walls glowed faintly, and the training chamber behind him slowly closed.
The magical pond outside rippled beneath the morning wind, while emerald light filtered through the leaves of the massive ancient tree holding up the courtyard.
Rose was already waiting for him. She stood near the entrance of the courtyard, wearing a formal green and silver robe, different from the pale dress she’d worn before.

Her long hair was tied back with an emerald ribbon, and a thin jade ornament hung at her waist, marked with the Evercrest Clan’s insignia. She looked more elegant and dignified than before, but Max could sense the tension hidden beneath her calm face.
The moment she saw him, her eyes sharpened slightly.
"You got stronger again."
Max walked toward her. "A little."
Rose stared at him for a breath. Then she smiled faintly.
"Only you would call reaching the 6th level of the Law Refinement Realm in one week ’a little.’"
Max didn’t deny it.
Rose looked at him more closely, and her expression turned a bit more serious. "Your aura’s different too. The Primordial Bloodline has fully settled?"
"Yes."
"Good," Rose said. "The Bloodline Legacy Battle starts today. The people from the Four Sacred Clans have already gathered."
Max nodded. "Then let’s go."
Rose turned without wasting any more words. The space at the edge of the courtyard opened, forming a path of emerald and silver light. She stepped into it first, and Max followed.

This time, Rose didn’t lead him deeper into the Evercrest Clan. Instead, she took him away from the main sacred territory. The two of them passed through several folded spatial layers, crossed hidden bridges of light, and moved through passages that seemed to curve around the outside of the clan’s core world.
Gradually, the elegant palaces and enormous ancient trees faded behind them. The atmosphere shifted from peaceful and sacred to solemn and ancient.
After a while, the spatial passage opened. Max and Rose stepped out.

Before them stood an arena. It was enormous. Calling it an arena almost felt like an understatement, since it was large enough to hold several cities. The whole structure floated inside a separate spatial field, surrounded by six vast platforms arranged in a grand hexagon.

Each platform was built like its own world facing the central battlefield below. The ground of the battlefield was carved with countless old runes, many so ancient that even Max couldn’t immediately tell what they were for.

They were still Pseudo Cosmic Paths, still unable to become true Cosmic Paths before the Divine Lord Realm, but they now carried a faint primordial quality that made them deeper and harder to shake loose.
His cultivation rose again too.

The breakthrough didn’t come as violently as the jump from the 1st to the 5th level of the Law Refinement Realm, which had been forced along by the leftover integration energy of the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline.
This time, Max advanced through steady accumulation.

He used the Dimension of Time to refine his laws, stabilize the new bloodline, digest the energy still sitting in his body, and keep polishing his foundation until the next small barrier loosened on its own.
On the sixth day by the outer world’s count, that barrier broke.
[Breakthrough Achieved.]
[Law Refinement Realm 6th Level.]
Max opened his eyes inside the Dimension of Time and felt the change settle in quietly.
His aura hadn’t turned wildly unstable.
It had simply grown deeper.
The laws flowing around him were more condensed than before, and every movement of his power felt smoother.
The Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline circulated more naturally too, no longer like something newly acquired, but like something that had always belonged inside him.
Max didn’t spend the whole week only on cultivation, though.
He kept thinking through his battle with Revona too.
Again and again, he replayed the moment Null Origin Tide had stripped his powers away.
Again and again, he tested sword structures built to shift their source, hide their foundation, and survive nullification by refusing to stay fixed.
Many attempts failed.
Some collapsed instantly.
Some turned unstable.
Some worked for a moment but lacked real power.
Still, every failure taught him something.
By the time the seventh day came, Max hadn’t built a perfect counter to Revona’s Void Origin Eyes, but he’d taken the first real step.
A new sword concept was starting to take shape in his mind.
A sword with a layered source.
A sword with a shifting foundation.
A sword that didn’t fight nullification through raw power alone, but through deception, shifting origin, and momentary truth.
It wasn’t finished yet.
But it existed.
That was enough for now.
On the seventh day, Max stepped out of the Dimension of Time.
The quiet room prepared for him inside the Evercrest Clan came back into view.
The silver spatial runes on the walls glowed faintly, and the training chamber behind him slowly closed.
The magical pond outside rippled beneath the morning wind, while emerald light filtered through the leaves of the massive ancient tree holding up the courtyard.
Rose was already waiting for him.
She stood near the entrance of the courtyard, wearing a formal green and silver robe, different from the pale dress she’d worn before.
Her long hair was tied back with an emerald ribbon, and a thin jade ornament hung at her waist, marked with the Evercrest Clan’s insignia.
She looked more elegant and dignified than before, but Max could sense the tension hidden beneath her calm face.
The moment she saw him, her eyes sharpened slightly.
"You got stronger again."
Max walked toward her.
"A little."
Rose stared at him for a breath.
Then she smiled faintly.
"Only you would call reaching the 6th level of the Law Refinement Realm in one week ’a little.’"
Max didn’t deny it.
Rose looked at him more closely, and her expression turned a bit more serious.
"Your aura’s different too.
The Primordial Bloodline has fully settled?"
"Yes."
"Good," Rose said.
"The Bloodline Legacy Battle starts today.
The people from the Four Sacred Clans have already gathered."
Max nodded.
"Then let’s go."
Rose turned without wasting any more words.
The space at the edge of the courtyard opened, forming a path of emerald and silver light.
She stepped into it first, and Max followed.
This time, Rose didn’t lead him deeper into the Evercrest Clan.
Instead, she took him away from the main sacred territory.
The two of them passed through several folded spatial layers, crossed hidden bridges of light, and moved through passages that seemed to curve around the outside of the clan’s core world.
Gradually, the elegant palaces and enormous ancient trees faded behind them.
The atmosphere shifted from peaceful and sacred to solemn and ancient.
After a while, the spatial passage opened.
Max and Rose stepped out.
Before them stood an arena.
It was enormous.
Calling it an arena almost felt like an understatement, since it was large enough to hold several cities.
The whole structure floated inside a separate spatial field, surrounded by six vast platforms arranged in a grand hexagon.
Each platform was built like its own world facing the central battlefield below.
The ground of the battlefield was carved with countless old runes, many so ancient that even Max couldn’t immediately tell what they were for.

chapters.title: Chapter 1954: Start of the Bloodline Legacy Battle!
paragraphs: At one end of the arena stood the statue of the First Progenitor. It wasn’t the same statue Max had seen in the sealed hall, but it carried the same face, the same posture, and the same strange calmness.

This statue was far larger, standing above one whole end of the arena like a silent judge watching over every descendant of the Four Sacred Clans. Its eyes were closed, its robes carved from dark stone, and its presence made the whole battlefield feel like something more than just a competition ground.
The other four ends belonged to the Four Sacred Clans.
One end belonged to Valerius. It was built from white-gold stone, covered in sunlike patterns and sharp sacred banners.

The people seated there carried proud, brilliant auras, and many wore robes decorated with golden flame-like markings. Their presence was bright, domineering, and noble, as if they’d been born to stand beneath a higher light.

Another end belonged to Ashbourne. Their platform was darker, built from black stone and crimson metal. The aura there was heavy, fierce, and oppressive. Many Ashbourne descendants had sharp eyes and battle-hardened expressions, and even their silence felt like restrained violence.
The third end belonged to Ravenhart. That platform was elegant and mysterious, filled with deep purple banners, black-feathered motifs, and moonlike crystals hanging in the air.
The people there looked calm, strange, and hard to read. Some carried scholarly auras, while others seemed as dangerous as hidden blades.
The fourth end belonged to Evercrest. It was covered in green-gold light, living wood, jade stone, and layered spatial formations.

Max immediately recognized the same refined spatial style he’d seen throughout the Evercrest Clan. The people there wore robes of green, silver, and white, and their gazes turned toward Rose and Max almost instantly when the two of them arrived.
Then there was the sixth end.
It was abandoned. No banners hung there. No clan insignia marked it. The platform sat dark, empty, and silent, covered in broken stone seats and old cracks.
Compared to the other five ends, it looked forgotten, almost deliberately left untouched. Still, Max’s eyes lingered on it longer than he expected.
Something about that abandoned end felt strange. It wasn’t completely dead. It felt like a place kept reserved for something that no longer existed.
Rose noticed where he was looking and said quietly, "That’s the abandoned end."
Max glanced at her. "Who did it used to belong to?"
Rose stayed silent for a moment. Then she said, "That’s not something people talk about during the Bloodline Legacy Battle."
Max looked at her calmly and didn’t push it further. He looked around and didn’t see any crowd at that end either. It was suspiciously empty.
’Huh?’ It was then that Max noticed the sixth end wasn’t completely empty after all. There was an old man sitting alone at that end, his eyes closed. ’Very strange.’
There would be time to find out more later.

The arena was already overflowing with people from the Four Sacred Clans. Countless descendants, elders, guardians, representatives, servants, branch family members, and invited observers filled the four clan platforms.

Their voices blended into a deep roar that rolled across the arena like thunder. This battle wasn’t open to the whole Divine Realm the way the Cosmic Ascension Conference had been, but the pressure here was no weaker. In some ways it felt even heavier, since everyone present carried blood ties to one of the oldest, most mysterious human forces in existence.
The moment Rose and Max appeared, plenty of eyes shifted toward them.
At first, some people only looked at Rose. Then they recognized Max. A wave of whispers spread quickly across the Evercrest platform first, then across the other sacred clan ends.
"That’s Rose."
"She actually came."
"So the castaway descendant dared to use the old rule?"
"Who’s the man beside her?"
"Are you blind? That’s Max Morgan."
"The champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference?"
"The one who beat Revona?"
"He got the Primordial Race’s reward, didn’t he?"
"Why would someone like him represent Rose?"
The whispers grew louder. Some people looked shocked. Some looked curious. Some looked unhappy. Some looked openly hostile.
Max ignored all of it.
Rose felt those stares more deeply, though. She kept her back straight and her expression calm, but Max could sense the tension in her breathing. This was the place that had rejected her.

These were the people who’d looked down on her since birth just because she’d been born without the forbidden bloodline. Coming back here under all these eyes wasn’t easy for her, even if she didn’t let it show.
Max walked beside her without changing his pace. That alone made a fair number of people quiet down a little.

Rose led him toward a smaller waiting area beneath the Evercrest end. It wasn’t among the main Evercrest heirs, but on a lower platform set aside for special challengers and castaway descendants invoking old rules.
There weren’t many people there. In fact, Rose seemed to be the only one from Evercrest using that path this time.
The message was clear. She was allowed to take part. But she wasn’t welcome.
As they reached the waiting area, an elder from the Evercrest side looked down at them with cold eyes.
"Rose Evercrest," the elder said, his voice carrying across the lower platform. "You’ve come back to invoke the castaway challenge right."
Rose raised her head and answered calmly, "Yes."
The elder’s gaze moved to Max. "And this is your chosen representative?"
"Yes."
The elder narrowed his eyes slightly. Even with his cold expression, he couldn’t deny who Max was.

The young man in front of him wasn’t some ordinary outsider. He was the champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference, the genius personally rewarded by the Primordial Race, and someone whose name had already spread across the Divine Realm.
The elder stayed silent for a moment before saying, "The old rule allows it. But remember, Rose Evercrest, if your representative fails, you’ll bear the consequences yourself."
Rose’s hands tightened slightly at her sides. "I know."
The statue of the First Progenitor stood silently at one end. Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest each held their own sacred platforms. The abandoned sixth end stayed empty and dark.
Max looked across the packed arena, sensing the countless powerful auras, hidden bloodline pressures, and hostile stares gathering around them.
The Bloodline Legacy Battle hadn’t even started yet. But the stage was already alive.

chapters.title: Chapter 1955: Strongest Warriors of the Four Sacred Clans!
paragraphs: Max stood beside Rose on the lower waiting platform beneath the Evercrest end and looked out over the vast arena.

The Bloodline Legacy Battle hadn’t officially started yet, but the pressure from the gathered crowd was already heavy. The Four Sacred Clans didn’t carry the same public noise as the Cosmic Ascension Conference.

Their atmosphere felt different. There were fewer outsiders, fewer excited spectators, and no grand proclamations meant for the whole Divine Realm. Still, the feeling here ran sharper, older, and more suffocating, since everyone present came from bloodlines that had stood at the top of humanity since the earliest eras.
Valerius. Ashbourne. Ravenhart. Evercrest.
Each clan held one end of the arena, and each end carried a completely different aura.
The Valerius platform shone with white-gold brilliance, as if every disciple there had been born beneath a sacred sun.
The Ashbourne platform felt like a silent battlefield soaked in old blood and iron will.
The Ravenhart platform was mysterious and elegant, filled with shadowed gazes and faint purple light.
The Evercrest platform was layered with life, space, and sealed domains, beautiful on the surface but hard to see through.
Max’s gaze moved calmly across those platforms.
Then he asked, "Who are the strongest participants?"
Rose seemed to have expected the question. She stood beside him with her hands folded in front of her, her expression composed, though the tension in her eyes hadn’t fully faded.
This arena was full of people who’d once treated her like a discarded descendant. Even without showing weakness, coming back here clearly weighed on her.

"There are a few people you need to watch closely," Rose said. "The Bloodline Legacy Battle isn’t like an ordinary tournament where everyone fights randomly until one champion comes out on top. The structure changes depending on the number of challengers, representatives, and legacy claims. But the strongest geniuses of the Four Sacred Clans will definitely show up, and if you want to gather enough legacy merit for me, you’ll probably have to beat some of them."
Max nodded. "Tell me."
Rose looked toward the Valerius end first.
"The strongest genius of Valerius this generation is Cassian Valerius."
Max followed her gaze.

At the highest row of the Valerius platform, a young man sat with his eyes closed. He wore a white-gold robe embroidered with sun patterns, and even sitting still, he looked wrapped in a faint halo of sacred light.
His hair was golden-white, his posture straight, and the aura around him didn’t spread out wildly. It stayed condensed close to his body, which only made him seem more dangerous.

Rose’s voice turned serious. "Cassian is known as the Sun-Crowned Heir of Valerius. He awakened the Valerius branch of the forbidden bloodline very young, and his control over sacred solar law is terrifying. Among the younger generation of the Four Sacred Clans, he’s considered one of the most stable and complete fighters. He doesn’t have any obvious weaknesses, and his attacks only get stronger the longer a battle drags on."
"What cultivation level?" Max asked.
"Peak of the Law Manifestation Realm."
Max didn’t look surprised.

Rose continued, "Most of the strongest participants sit at that level. The Law Manifestation Realm is a special boundary among the younger generation. Before entering the Divine Lord Realm, a cultivator still counts as part of the younger generation in most supreme forces. But once someone steps into the Divine Lord Realm, their status changes. They stop being treated as a young genius. They get the authority and standing of an elder, or at least a quasi-elder, depending on the force."
Max understood right away. "So battle cultivation is capped at peak Law Manifestation Realm."

"Yes," Rose said. "The Bloodline Legacy Battle exists for descendants and representatives fighting for bloodline opportunities. It’s not built for elders. If Divine Lord Realm cultivators were allowed to join freely, the whole point of the battle would change. So most young genius battles stop at the peak of Law Manifestation Realm. Anyone who breaks through to the Divine Lord Realm usually steps away from this kind of competition and moves into the elder hierarchy."

Max looked at Cassian Valerius again. Peak Law Manifestation Realm. That sat several levels above Max’s current position at Law Refinement Realm 6th level. But Max had never cared much about ordinary realm gaps.
During the Cosmic Ascension Conference, he’d fought and beaten monsters standing at the very top of the younger generation while he himself was still only at the peak of the Law Awakening Realm.
Now he’d entered the Law Refinement Realm, gained a Tier 4 Primarch Bloodline, and strengthened every part of his foundation.
Rose knew that too. That was exactly why she’d brought him.
Her gaze moved toward the Ashbourne platform next.
"The strongest genius of Ashbourne is Draven Ashbourne."

Max looked over. On the black and crimson platform, a tall young man stood with his arms crossed. Unlike Cassian, he didn’t sit quietly like a noble heir. He stood out in plain view, wearing dark armor over a simple black battle robe.

His hair was dark red, and his eyes carried a cold brutality that made a lot of people instinctively look away after a moment. Several Ashbourne disciples kept a respectful distance from him, as if they didn’t dare stand too close unless called over.

Rose’s tone grew heavier. "Draven is called the Blood-Iron Demon of Ashbourne. The Ashbourne branch of the forbidden bloodline is famous for destructive physical power, blood refinement, and battle endurance.

Draven inherited all of that to a terrifying degree. He’s fought a lot of battles outside the public eye, and there are rumors that a few older peak Law Manifestation experts died at his hands even before he reached his current level."
"Peak Law Manifestation Realm?" Max asked.

"Yes. But even among peak Law Manifestation Realm geniuses, he’s one of the most dangerous in direct combat. If Rakan Thorne from the War God Palace is a battle maniac with an overwhelming physique, Draven is something darker. He fights to break his opponent, not just beat them."

Max’s eyes lingered on Draven for a moment. As if sensing the gaze, Draven Ashbourne turned slightly and looked straight at him. Their eyes met across the arena. Draven didn’t smile. Max didn’t look away.
After a few breaths, Draven’s lips curved faintly, but there was no warmth in it. It was the smile of someone who’d just found a target worth crushing.

chapters.title: Chapter 1956: Sharpening Me!
paragraphs: Rose noticed and said quietly, "He’s already noticed you."
"That’s fine," Max said.
Rose glanced at him. "You don’t look worried."
"Should I be?"
Rose stayed quiet for a moment. Then she sighed lightly. "I forgot who I was talking to."
She looked toward the Ravenhart end next.
"The strongest genius of Ravenhart is Seraphine Ravenhart."

Max’s gaze shifted. The Ravenhart platform was the quietest of the four clan ends, and the people seated there looked far more restrained than the rest. Near the center of the highest seating area sat a young woman in a deep violet dress, her black hair falling over one shoulder like silk.

A faint feather-shaped mark rested between her brows, and her eyes carried a strange shade of silver-purple. She looked gentle at first glance, almost scholarly, but the space around her felt off somehow. The shadows near her chair moved slightly even though there was no wind.

Rose’s expression turned even more cautious. "Seraphine is probably the hardest one to read. Ravenhart’s forbidden bloodline branch is tied to shadows, prophecy fragments, soul silence, and fate-like perception. No one really knows how much she can actually see. Some say she can predict where a battle is headed several moves before it happens. Some say she doesn’t predict at all, but instead listens to the hidden rhythm of her opponent’s soul."
Max raised an eyebrow slightly. "Soul and prediction abilities."

"Yes. And unlike Draven, who’s dangerous because of his direct brutality, Seraphine is dangerous because you might not even understand how you lost until the battle’s already over. She’s also at the peak of Law Manifestation Realm."

Max looked at Seraphine Ravenhart. As if sensing his attention, the young woman slowly turned toward him and smiled. It was a small, polite smile, but Max’s eyes narrowed slightly, because for one instant, it felt like her gaze hadn’t landed on his face at all, but somewhere deeper.
Not deep enough to see his real secrets, but enough to make his soul react faintly.
His Dimension of Soul stirred. The slight probing sensation disappeared right away.
Seraphine’s smile didn’t change, but her eyes flickered with interest.
Rose caught the brief exchange. "Don’t underestimate her."
"I won’t."
Rose then turned toward the Evercrest end.
"As for Evercrest, the strongest genius is Aelric Evercrest."

Max looked up. At the center of the Evercrest platform sat a young man in green and silver robes. Compared to Cassian’s sacred brilliance, Draven’s brutal pressure, and Seraphine’s mysterious calm, Aelric looked more refined and elegant.

His face was handsome, his posture relaxed, and his eyes carried the natural confidence of someone who’d been praised his whole life. A lot of Evercrest descendants sat around him with clear respect, and several elders glanced his way with obvious satisfaction.
Rose’s voice turned colder when she said his name.

"Aelric awakened the Evercrest forbidden bloodline at a very high purity. He’s considered the strongest Evercrest heir of the current generation. His mastery over space and life-sealing techniques goes way beyond mine. He can fold the battlefield, seal off movement routes, create hidden domains, and use life force itself as a binding tool."
Max looked at her. "You don’t like him."
Rose’s expression didn’t shift much, but her eyes turned colder. "He was one of the people who told me I should be grateful the clan even let me keep the Evercrest name."
Max looked at Aelric again.

Aelric had noticed them too. Unlike Draven, he didn’t show open hostility. He just looked down from the higher platform with a faint smile, as if Rose’s return amused him more than it bothered him. His gaze shifted to Max next, and that smile turned slightly more polite, though Max could still feel the pride running underneath it.

Rose continued, "Aelric is also at the peak of Law Manifestation Realm. Among Evercrest’s younger generation, he’s almost untouchable. Most people believe he’ll eventually inherit one of the clan’s highest positions once he enters the Divine Lord Realm."
"And if I beat him?" Max asked.
Rose paused, then looked at him.
"If you beat Aelric in the Bloodline Legacy Battle, the Evercrest Clan loses face, and I gain far more legacy merit than I would from beating an ordinary representative."
Max smiled faintly. "Then he’s useful."
Rose looked at him for a moment before shaking her head. "You really do treat them like stepping stones."
"Aren’t they?"
For a second, Rose didn’t know whether to laugh or sigh.

Then she went on, "Besides those four, there are other strong participants. Valerius has Lucara Valerius, known for her Sacred Flame Mandate. Ashbourne has Kaelric Ashbourne, Draven’s cousin, who specializes in bone-crushing martial arts and blood armor. Ravenhart has Nox Ravenhart, who’s extremely dangerous in assassination-style fights. Evercrest also has several high-level heirs, including Mirena Evercrest and Solan Evercrest. All of them are at peak Law Manifestation Realm or very close to it."
Max asked, "Are outsiders allowed to represent people too?"

"Yes," Rose said. "Several descendants from the Four Sacred Clans have brought in outsiders. Most of them are hidden monsters from ancient forces, supreme guilds, and forbidden training grounds. Some might not be as famous as the top geniuses from the Cosmic Ascension Conference, but don’t assume that means they’re weak. The Four Sacred Clans have enough influence to invite genuinely dangerous people."
Max nodded slowly.

Rose looked at him seriously. "Your fame from the Cosmic Ascension Conference cuts both ways here. On one hand, no one can dismiss you as some ordinary outsider. On the other hand, plenty of them will want to beat you just to prove themselves. Some will see you as the champion of the Divine Realm’s younger generation. Some will see you as the outsider who dared to step onto the sacred clans’ stage. Some will just hate you because you’re representing me."
Max’s expression stayed calm. "That makes things simple."
"How?"
"They’ll come to me."
Rose looked at him in silence.

Below them, the central battlefield began to glow as the ancient runes woke up one after another. The noise in the arena grew louder. Representatives from the four clans started entering their waiting zones.
Several powerful auras rose up across the platforms, each one belonging to a genius with no intention of staying unnoticed.
Rose took a slow breath.

"Max, remember this. Most of them are at the peak of Law Manifestation Realm. That’s the highest realm allowed in the true young genius battles. Once someone enters the Divine Lord Realm, they’re considered to have crossed the line between genius and elder. That’s why this battle has so many peak Law Manifestation Realm cultivators. They’re all standing right at the last step before becoming elder-level figures."
Max looked out at the arena. Peak Law Manifestation Realm geniuses from the Four Sacred Clans.

Forbidden bloodline inheritors. Ancient clan representatives. Outsider monsters. A battlefield tied to the bloodline legacy of the First Progenitor. And somewhere behind all of it, the mystery of why his own blood had reacted so violently to that statue.
Max’s smile deepened slightly. "Good."
Rose glanced at him. "You keep saying that."
Max kept his gaze fixed on the central battlefield as the runes finished lighting up.
"The stronger they are, the more useful they’ll be."
Rose’s eyes shifted slightly. "Useful for what?"
Max’s gaze stayed locked on the arena.
"For sharpening me."

chapters.title: Chapter 1957: Bloodline Legacy Battle Begins!
paragraphs: The central battlefield finished lighting up.
Ancient runes spread across the vast arena floor one after another, forming a web of golden, crimson, purple, green, silver, and black light.
Each color linked faintly to one of the powers gathered there, but the whole formation ultimately pointed toward the towering statue of the First Progenitor standing at one end of the arena.
The statue’s closed eyes stayed silent, yet once the runes fully woke up, the entire arena felt like it had come under that ancient ancestor’s watch.
The noise from the four sacred clan platforms slowly faded. Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest all turned their attention to the central battlefield.
Even the abandoned sixth end of the arena seemed darker and quieter than before, sitting apart from the other five like a forgotten wound in this grand sacred place.
Then space shimmered above the battlefield. A woman stepped out.

She wore a white-gold robe marked with the Valerius insignia, and her long golden hair fell behind her like flowing sunlight. Her face was beautiful, dignified, and familiar. The moment Max saw her, his eyes shifted slightly.
Angelina Valerius.

She had presided over the Cosmic Ascension Conference. Back then, she’d stood above the Eternal Hourglass as the announcer and judge, calmly watching the greatest geniuses of the Divine Realm clash one after another. Now she’d appeared here again, not as a representative of the conference, but as a member of the Valerius Clan, one of the Four Sacred Clans.
The moment Angelina arrived, many younger members of the Four Sacred Clans straightened up instinctively. Her status was clearly not low.

She descended slowly toward the center of the battlefield, her robe moving gently despite the absence of wind. The white-gold light around her wasn’t oppressive, but it carried a natural authority that made people listen.
When her feet touched the arena floor, the surrounding runes brightened once before settling back down.

Angelina looked around the whole arena. Her gaze passed over the Valerius platform, the Ashbourne platform, the Ravenhart platform, the Evercrest platform, the statue of the First Progenitor, and finally the lower challenger areas where Rose and Max stood.
For a brief instant, her eyes lingered on Max. A faint smile crossed her lips. Then she looked away and spoke.

"Descendants of Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest. Representatives chosen by bloodline claimants. Elders and witnesses of the Four Sacred Clans. Today, the Bloodline Legacy Battle begins."
Her voice was clear, steady, and carried through every corner of the arena. The already solemn atmosphere grew heavier.

"This battle is held under the authority of the First Progenitor’s legacy and witnessed by the Four Sacred Clans. Every descendant who seeks legacy merit, every representative who fights on behalf of a claimant, and every challenger who steps onto this battlefield must accept the ancient rules of the Bloodline Legacy Battle."
Angelina raised one hand. A massive circular projection appeared above the battlefield, showing the rules laid out through ancient script.
"The rules are simple." Her gaze swept over everyone. "Anyone may challenge anyone."
The arena stirred. Even though many people already knew the rules, hearing them announced officially still sent a wave of tension through the crowd.

Angelina continued, "There are no fixed brackets, no arranged order, and no protection from being challenged because of reputation, bloodline, clan, or status. If you stand as a participant in the Bloodline Legacy Battle, you may challenge another participant, and another participant may challenge you."

Her voice sharpened slightly. "If the challenged party refuses without a valid reason recognized by the battle formation, they’ll lose legacy merit and face a penalty based on their claim level. If they accept, both sides enter combat under the protection of the arena laws."
She then pointed toward the First Progenitor statue.
"The battle continues until no one dares challenge the standing victor, or until one participant remains undefeated after all others have either lost, withdrawn, or refused to continue."
The projection above the arena shifted, showing a single figure standing beneath the statue while everyone else stood below.
"That person will become the winner of the Bloodline Legacy Battle."

The arena went silent. It was a brutal rule, simple, direct, and merciless. There was no hiding behind brackets, no dodging powerful opponents through luck, and no waiting for others to eliminate the dangerous ones. Anyone who wanted merit had to fight.
Anyone who wanted to prove themselves had to step forward. Anyone who wanted the final victory had to stand where everyone could challenge them and still come out undefeated.
Rose quietly clenched her hands. This rule was exactly why the Bloodline Legacy Battle was so hard for someone like her.

A castaway descendant could only rely on a representative, and that representative had to be strong enough not just to win one battle, but to keep standing as stronger and stronger enemies kept showing up.
Max, on the other hand, smiled faintly. This kind of rule suited him.
Angelina lowered her hand.

"The use of killing techniques is allowed, but deliberate killing after victory has already been decided is forbidden. The arena formation will suppress fatal intent only after one side has lost the ability to continue or has admitted defeat. Before that point, every participant has to protect themselves with their own strength."
Several young geniuses narrowed their eyes. This meant the battles would be dangerous, not staged sparring or symbolic exchanges. Real battles.
Angelina’s gaze swept across the participant areas.
"The Bloodline Legacy Battle now begins."

The moment those words fell, the whole arena erupted. The crowd from the Four Sacred Clans released a wave of noise that rolled across the battlefield like thunder. Clan descendants started looking at one another.

Representatives straightened their backs. Several powerful auras rose from the waiting zones, each one carrying challenge, pride, and killing intent. Plenty of people had already picked their targets before the battle even started.
But before anyone else could move, Max stepped forward. He didn’t say anything at first. He just walked towards the arena.

chapters.title: Chapter 1958: Max’s First Challenge!
paragraphs: From the lower Evercrest challenger platform, Max moved toward the central battlefield with calm steps. His white hair shifted gently in the wind stirred up by the arena formation, and his black robe carried no sacred clan insignia.
Next to the clan heirs wearing robes marked by Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest, he looked like a total outsider.

Yet the moment he entered the arena, every eye turned toward him. The noise started to fade. It didn’t vanish all at once. It rolled down slowly, section by section, platform by platform, until the whole massive arena grew quieter than before.

Max Morgan. The champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference. The man who’d defeated Revona, Damian Voss, Ervin, Orion Starfall, Kaiden Voidmere, Rakan Thorne, Aurelian Lareth, and every other opponent placed before him.
The strongest genius of the Divine Realm’s younger generation. Even inside the Four Sacred Clans, his name had already spread everywhere.

Some looked curious. Some looked excited. Some looked displeased. Some looked hostile. The younger descendants of the Four Sacred Clans had pride carved into their bones. They didn’t easily accept an outsider being called the strongest genius of the Divine Realm, especially not on their own sacred stage.
But none of them could deny what Max had actually accomplished. The Cosmic Ascension Conference had been watched by countless forces, and his perfect record had already become impossible to ignore.

Angelina watched him approach with a smile that carried both familiarity and interest. When Max stopped at the center of the battlefield, she looked at him and asked, "Max Morgan. You’re the first to enter the arena. Who do you wish to challenge?"
The arena grew even quieter. Plenty of people leaned forward.

Rose stood beneath the Evercrest end, her chest tightening despite herself. She knew Max wouldn’t shy away from strong opponents, but she hadn’t expected him to step forward before anyone else. In this kind of battle, the first challenger naturally drew the most attention. It was bold, arrogant, and dangerous.
Max looked across the four sacred clan platforms. His gaze didn’t stop on Valerius. It didn’t stop on Ashbourne. It didn’t stop on Ravenhart. It moved straight to Evercrest.

Above the Evercrest platform, several expressions shifted. Aelric Evercrest sat calmly among the main heirs, his posture relaxed and his expression faintly amused. When Max’s gaze landed on him, his smile deepened slightly, as if he’d already guessed what might happen but still found it entertaining.
Then Max raised his hand and pointed directly at Aelric Evercrest.
"I challenge him."
The arena fell silent. For one breath, no one reacted. Then the entire Evercrest platform stirred violently.
"What?"
"He challenged Aelric directly?"
"Is he insane?"
"He’s Rose’s representative, and the first person he challenges is the strongest heir of Evercrest?"
"He didn’t pick a weaker opponent to build up merit first?"
"He went straight for Aelric?"

The shock spread beyond Evercrest. Valerius descendants looked surprised. Ashbourne descendants grinned with interest. Ravenhart descendants narrowed their eyes, sensing the battle had turned interesting far sooner than they’d expected. Even some elders traded glances.

Rose stared at Max from below, her eyes widening slightly. She’d expected him to target Aelric eventually, since beating him would bring huge legacy merit. She’d even hoped it would happen after Max won a few smaller battles and built up some momentum.
But Max hadn’t waited. He’d chosen Aelric as his very first challenge.
On the Evercrest platform, the elder who’d warned Rose earlier frowned deeply. "Audacious."
Another Evercrest elder’s expression turned cold. "An outsider steps onto our sacred stage and challenges Aelric directly?"
Some younger Evercrest descendants looked furious, but others looked uneasy. After all, the challenger wasn’t some unknown fool. It was Max Morgan.
Aelric himself didn’t stand up right away. He looked down at Max from the higher platform with that same refined smile.
"Max Morgan," he said, his voice carrying smoothly across the arena, "I didn’t expect you to pick me so quickly."
Max looked at him calmly. "Rose needs merit."
Aelric’s eyes drifted toward Rose for a moment. His smile turned slightly colder. "So this is for her."
"Yes."
The simplicity of Max’s answer made the mood even heavier.

Aelric slowly stood. The moment he rose, the Evercrest platform quieted down. The green-gold light around him stirred, and faint spatial ripples appeared beneath his feet. His aura didn’t burst out violently, but the space around him folded gently, as if the world itself were clearing a path for him.
Rose’s expression turned tense. "Aelric," she whispered.
Max had already heard everything she’d told him about him. The strongest genius of the Evercrest Clan’s current generation.

A direct heir who’d awakened the Evercrest forbidden bloodline at high purity. A master of space, life-sealing techniques, hidden domains, and battlefield control. A peak Law Manifestation Realm cultivator.

Aelric stepped down from the Evercrest platform. He didn’t fly in the normal sense. He walked through folded space, appearing closer with each step until he stood inside the central battlefield across from Max. His robes moved softly, and his refined face carried calm pride.
Angelina looked between them. "Aelric Evercrest," she said. "You’ve been challenged by Max Morgan, representative of Rose Evercrest. Do you accept?"
Aelric smiled. "How could I refuse?"
The formation beneath the battlefield brightened instantly. A circular boundary rose around the arena, cutting Max and Aelric off from the outside world.
The runes on the floor began rotating slowly, and the statue of the First Progenitor at the far end seemed to grow more solemn under the shifting light.
Angelina stepped back. "Then the first battle of the Bloodline Legacy Battle shall begin."
Aelric looked at Max with calm eyes.
"Champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference," he said softly. "You may have dominated the conference, but this isn’t the Eternal Hourglass. This is the sacred stage of the Four Sacred Clans."
Max held out his hand. Dragonheart appeared. The black sword let out a low hum, and the moment it settled into his grip, Max’s aura changed.
He looked at Aelric and smiled faintly. "Then show me what makes this stage different."

Rose stood beneath the Evercrest end, her chest tightening despite herself.
She knew Max wouldn’t shy away from strong opponents, but she hadn’t expected him to step forward before anyone else.
In this kind of battle, the first challenger naturally drew the most attention.
It was bold, arrogant, and dangerous.
Max looked across the four sacred clan platforms.
His gaze didn’t stop on Valerius.
It didn’t stop on Ashbourne.
It didn’t stop on Ravenhart.
It moved straight to Evercrest.
Above the Evercrest platform, several expressions shifted.
Aelric Evercrest sat calmly among the main heirs, his posture relaxed and his expression faintly amused.
When Max’s gaze landed on him, his smile deepened slightly, as if he’d already guessed what might happen but still found it entertaining.
Then Max raised his hand and pointed directly at Aelric Evercrest.
"I challenge him."
The arena fell silent.
For one breath, no one reacted.
Then the entire Evercrest platform stirred violently.
"What?"
"He challenged Aelric directly?"
"Is he insane?"
"He’s Rose’s representative, and the first person he challenges is the strongest heir of Evercrest?"
"He didn’t pick a weaker opponent to build up merit first?"
"He went straight for Aelric?"
The shock spread beyond Evercrest.
Valerius descendants looked surprised.
Ashbourne descendants grinned with interest.
Ravenhart descendants narrowed their eyes, sensing the battle had turned interesting far sooner than they’d expected.
Even some elders traded glances.
Rose stared at Max from below, her eyes widening slightly.
She’d expected him to target Aelric eventually, since beating him would bring huge legacy merit.
She’d even hoped it would happen after Max won a few smaller battles and built up some momentum.
But Max hadn’t waited.
He’d chosen Aelric as his very first challenge.
On the Evercrest platform, the elder who’d warned Rose earlier frowned deeply.
"Audacious."
Another Evercrest elder’s expression turned cold.
"An outsider steps onto our sacred stage and challenges Aelric directly?"
Some younger Evercrest descendants looked furious, but others looked uneasy.
After all, the challenger wasn’t some unknown fool.
It was Max Morgan.
Aelric himself didn’t stand up right away.
He looked down at Max from the higher platform with that same refined smile.
"Max Morgan," he said, his voice carrying smoothly across the arena, "I didn’t expect you to pick me so quickly."
Max looked at him calmly.
"Rose needs merit."
Aelric’s eyes drifted toward Rose for a moment.
His smile turned slightly colder.
"So this is for her."
"Yes."
The simplicity of Max’s answer made the mood even heavier.
Aelric slowly stood.
The moment he rose, the Evercrest platform quieted down.
The green-gold light around him stirred, and faint spatial ripples appeared beneath his feet.
His aura didn’t burst out violently, but the space around him folded gently, as if the world itself were clearing a path for him.
Rose’s expression turned tense.
"Aelric," she whispered.
Max had already heard everything she’d told him about him.
The strongest genius of the Evercrest Clan’s current generation.
A direct heir who’d awakened the Evercrest forbidden bloodline at high purity.
A master of space, life-sealing techniques, hidden domains, and battlefield control.
A peak Law Manifestation Realm cultivator.
Aelric stepped down from the Evercrest platform.
He didn’t fly in the normal sense.
He walked through folded space, appearing closer with each step until he stood inside the central battlefield across from Max.
His robes moved softly, and his refined face carried calm pride.
Angelina looked between them.
"Aelric Evercrest," she said.
"You’ve been challenged by Max Morgan, representative of Rose Evercrest.
Do you accept?"
Aelric smiled.
"How could I refuse?"
The formation beneath the battlefield brightened instantly.
A circular boundary rose around the arena, cutting Max and Aelric off from the outside world.
The runes on the floor began rotating slowly, and the statue of the First Progenitor at the far end seemed to grow more solemn under the shifting light.
Angelina stepped back.
"Then the first battle of the Bloodline Legacy Battle shall begin."
Aelric looked at Max with calm eyes.
"Champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference," he said softly.
"You may have dominated the conference, but this isn’t the Eternal Hourglass.
This is the sacred stage of the Four Sacred Clans."
Max held out his hand.
Dragonheart appeared.
The black sword let out a low hum, and the moment it settled into his grip, Max’s aura changed.
He looked at Aelric and smiled faintly.
"Then show me what makes this stage different."

chapters.title: Chapter 1959: Max vs Aelric Evercrest!
paragraphs: The formation beneath the central battlefield kept brightening as Max and Aelric stood facing each other.

The first battle of the Bloodline Legacy Battle had already been decided before anyone else even got the chance to move. Max Morgan, the champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference and Rose Evercrest’s chosen representative, had stepped into the arena first and challenged Aelric Evercrest directly.
To outsiders, it looked like arrogance. To the Evercrest Clan, it looked like provocation. To Rose, it was both a dangerous gamble and the fastest path to the legacy merit she needed.

Aelric Evercrest stood across from Max with his hands behind his back, his green and silver robe stirring gently as faint spatial ripples flowed around him. He didn’t draw a weapon. He didn’t release his aura right away. Instead, he looked at Max with a faint sneer.

"Show me what I have got? Don’t make laugh," Aelric said, his voice smooth but cold enough to carry across the battlefield, "don’t think too highly of yourself just because you won the Cosmic Ascension Conference."

The moment he spoke, the whole arena quieted a little. Plenty of people from the Four Sacred Clans narrowed their eyes with interest. Aelric’s words weren’t just aimed at Max. They also voiced what a lot of sacred clan geniuses secretly felt.

The Cosmic Ascension Conference had been grand, and Max’s win had shaken the Divine Realm, but the Four Sacred Clans hadn’t actually sent their strongest hidden heirs into that stage. To them, the conference mattered, but it hadn’t fully represented the deepest strength the sacred clans held.
Aelric continued, "The Divine Realm might call you the strongest genius of this generation, but that title only stuck because the stage you stood on was incomplete."
Rose’s expression turned colder. On the Evercrest platform, several young descendants smiled faintly, clearly pleased with Aelric’s words.

Aelric kept his eyes fixed on Max. "If the geniuses of the Four Sacred Clans had taken part in the Cosmic Ascension Conference, things would’ve gone differently. Do you really think you’d have walked away with twenty-four wins and no losses if Cassian Valerius, Draven Ashbourne, Seraphine Ravenhart, or I had stood across from you inside the Eternal Hourglass?"

A wave of murmurs moved through the arena. The Valerius platform stayed dignified, but several descendants there looked toward Cassian with pride. The Ashbourne platform burst into a few low laughs, as if they were already picturing Draven tearing through the so-called conference champion.

The Ravenhart side stayed quiet, but plenty of silver-purple eyes watched Max carefully, waiting to see how he’d respond. The Evercrest side was the loudest, since Aelric’s words had directly defended their pride.
"Being called the strongest genius of the Divine Realm without ever facing the sacred clans’ strongest heirs," Aelric said, his sneer deepening, "is almost funny."

Max listened calmly. He didn’t get angry. He didn’t release any killing intent. He didn’t bother pointing out that he’d defeated Revona, Damian Voss, Ervin, Orion Starfall, Kaiden Voidmere, and countless other top geniuses.
He also didn’t remind Aelric that the Primordial Race itself had acknowledged his victory, granted him the champion’s highest reward, and chosen him above everyone else.
He only smiled. That smile was light, almost casual. And somehow that casualness made Aelric’s expression turn colder.
Max looked at him and said, "Are you done?"
The arena went quiet again. Aelric’s eyes narrowed.
Max continued, "You’ve already said the Four Sacred Clans are stronger. You’ve said the Cosmic Ascension Conference was incomplete. You’ve said things would’ve gone differently if you’d taken part."
His smile stayed exactly the same. "Now show me."
The words were simple, but they hit harder than any angry outburst would have.
Aelric’s sneer froze slightly.
Max raised Dragonheart and let the black blade rest casually at his side.
"Show your strength instead of just talking."
For a breath, the battlefield went completely silent. Then the Ashbourne platform burst into laughter.
"Hahaha! Good!"
"That outsider’s got some nerve!"
"Talking’s useless. Fight if you’re strong!"

Even a few Ravenhart descendants smiled faintly, while the Valerius side watched with more interest than before. On the Evercrest platform, plenty of expressions turned ugly. Aelric was their strongest heir of the current generation, and Max had just brushed off his words in front of all Four Sacred Clans.
Rose stood below the Evercrest end and quietly let out a breath she hadn’t realized she’d been holding. This was Max. He didn’t need speeches to defend his title. He only needed his sword.
Aelric looked at Max for a long moment. The faint sneer slowly faded from his face, replaced by a cold, elegant smile.
"Very well," Aelric said. "Since you’re so eager to see the difference between the Cosmic Ascension Conference and the sacred clans’ stage, I’ll show you."
His aura finally began to rise. The green-gold light around him deepened. At first it looked gentle, almost beautiful, like the vitality of an ancient forest waking up under sunlight.

But the next moment, that beauty turned strange. Space around Aelric folded in layers. The air split into faint transparent surfaces, each one reflecting a different angle of the battlefield. Thin threads of life force spread out from beneath his feet and sank into the arena floor, merging with the runes as if trying to claim the battlefield for himself.

The pressure of peak Law Manifestation Realm came down over the arena. It was powerful, far stronger than what ordinary young geniuses could put out. Aelric hadn’t exaggerated about being one of the strongest heirs of the Four Sacred Clans.

His cultivation sat at the peak of Law Manifestation Realm, and his forbidden bloodline had clearly pushed his foundation past normal limits. The moment his aura spread, plenty of ordinary descendants in the arena felt their chests tighten.
Rose’s expression turned tense. "Aelric’s Evercrest bloodline," she whispered.

Max’s eyes stayed calm. His Dimensional Sovereign Body immediately picked up on the shifts in space around him. Aelric wasn’t just releasing aura. He was quietly folding the battlefield into layers, getting ready to turn the arena into a domain that favored him.

The life force threads sinking into the ground weren’t harmless either. They were anchors. Once enough of them spread, Aelric would likely be able to seal off movement, redirect attacks, and restrict space itself.
Max smiled slightly. "As expected, you’re better when you stop talking."
Aelric’s gaze turned colder. "Let’s see how long your arrogance lasts."
Angelina Valerius, who’d stepped back to the edge of the battlefield, raised her hand. The formation between Max and Aelric lit up fully. Her voice rang across the arena.
"First battle of the Bloodline Legacy Battle."
"Max Morgan, representative of Rose Evercrest, against Aelric Evercrest of the Evercrest Clan."
She lowered her hand. "Begin."

chapters.title: Chapter 1960: The Profound Primordial Bloodline!
paragraphs: The moment the word fell, Aelric vanished. Not through speed. Through folded space. One moment he stood across the battlefield.

The next, his figure appeared above Max’s left side, his palm already coming down with a green-gold seal forming at its center. The seal was made from life force and spatial law, and the moment it appeared, the air around Max tightened, as if an invisible cage had closed around him.
"Evercrest Life-Sealing Palm."
Aelric’s voice came from above, calm and cold. The palm descended.
But Max didn’t step back. His eyes sharpened. The Dimensional Sovereign Body activated silently. The cage around him twisted.
Then Max raised Dragonheart and slashed upward. A black sword light cut through the sealed air, meeting Aelric’s palm seal head on.
Boom!
The first collision exploded across the battlefield. Green-gold light and black sword aura spread out in every direction, striking the arena boundary hard enough to make the runes flash violently.
Aelric’s figure got pushed back half a step in the folded space, while Max stayed right where he’d been standing, his sword raised and his white hair moving under the shockwave.
The whole arena went quiet.
Aelric’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Max lowered Dragonheart and looked at him. "Is that all?"
The question came out calm. But to everyone listening, it sounded far more arrogant than anything Aelric had said.
The first collision had only been a greeting.

Aelric understood that the moment Max cut through his Evercrest Life-Sealing Palm. The refined smile on his face finally disappeared completely, and the green-gold light around his body grew much denser than before.

The space around him folded layer after layer, while threads of life force spread out from beneath his feet and sank deep into the battlefield. He no longer looked like a noble heir casually teaching an outsider a lesson. He looked like the strongest Evercrest genius of his generation, getting ready to protect his pride in front of all Four Sacred Clans.
"Good," Aelric said coldly. "At least you’re not completely unworthy of your reputation."
Max lowered Dragonheart slightly. "You’re still talking."
Aelric’s eyes went cold. The next instant, his aura erupted fully.

Peak Law Manifestation Realm pressure swept across the battlefield like a storm. The central arena trembled as the green-gold light around him expanded, forming a massive domain of folded space and ancient vitality.

Layers of transparent space appeared around Max from every direction, each one reflecting Aelric’s figure. In one reflection, Aelric stood above him. In another, he stood behind him. In another, he stood a thousand meters away. In another, he was already striking toward Max’s heart.
The whole battlefield turned uncertain.
"Evercrest Hidden Domain," Rose muttered from the lower platform, her expression turning solemn. "He’s getting serious now."
The Evercrest platform erupted with excitement.
"Aelric’s using the Hidden Domain!"
"That outsider is finished."
"Once Evercrest’s space layers close around him, even a peak Law Manifestation Realm opponent can’t find the real way out."
"Max Morgan might be strong, but this isn’t the Cosmic Ascension Conference. This is Evercrest’s sacred field."
Aelric raised both hands. The countless reflections moved with him.
"Let me show you the difference between an outsider and a sacred clan heir."
The transparent layers of space around Max suddenly collapsed inward. At the same time, green-gold vines made of life force burst out of the floor. They didn’t grow like ordinary plants.

They appeared out of different folded spaces, bypassing normal distance entirely, and wrapped toward Max’s limbs, sword arm, neck, and chest. Each vine carried sealing power, and every spatial layer around him tried to lock down his movement from a different angle.
Aelric wasn’t holding back anymore. He wanted to crush Max completely.

Max stood still and watched the storm coming at him. His Dimensional Sovereign Body could track the path of each folded layer. He could sense where the real Aelric hid and where the false reflections stood. But this time, Max didn’t counter with space right away. He wanted to test something else.
His Primordial Bloodline stirred. A faint ancient pulse spread out from inside him. It was quiet. But the moment it moved, the laws around Max changed.
His eyes sharpened slightly. The world felt closer.

That was the first sensation. It wasn’t that Max’s understanding had suddenly grown in some ordinary way. It felt like the laws of the world, which normally sat around him like distant rivers, had suddenly pulled in close to his skin.
Space, lightning, flame, emotion, sword, vitality, resistance, body, soul, and every trace of law on the battlefield became clearer.
The Primordial Bloodline didn’t force these laws under its control like a tyrant. It made Max feel like he naturally belonged closer to the source they all flowed from.
Then power surged through him. Not as an ability. Not as a technique. As direct enhancement.
His body, soul, law affinity, and foundation all rose at once. Ten times over. Max felt it clearly.
Just activating the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline pushed his strength to ten times his normal state.

This worked completely differently from his Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline and his Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline. Those bloodlines gave him powerful abilities, transformations, bloodline techniques, light authority, chaotic dragon force, and other tools he could use to boost his combat power under the right circumstances.
But they didn’t directly multiply his base strength the moment they stirred.
The Primordial Bloodline did. It was simple. Terrifyingly simple.

His strength increased. His control increased. His closeness to the laws increased. His foundation grew heavier. His Pseudo Cosmic Paths, already refined far beyond their original state, suddenly turned ten times stronger under this primordial condition.
The Emotion Severing Path became sharper, as if every invisible connection in the world had drawn closer to the edge of his sword.
Divine King Punishment became more majestic, as if the thunder tribunal behind it had gained deeper authority.
The Devouring Flames Domain turned darker and more controlled, as if the black flames could now bite closer to the source of whatever they consumed.
Max’s heart stirred faintly.
’This bloodline still isn’t fully awake.’

That much was unmistakable. The Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline had only started showing its surface. Even this tenfold boost wasn’t the full potential of the bloodline. It was only the most basic expression of the Primarch-level foundation resting inside him.
