chapters.title: Chapter 1961: Evercrest Forbidden Art!
paragraphs: Max closed his hand around Dragonheart. At the same time, the Seven Divine Veins inside his body began to open.
One. The Vein of Origin opened, stabilizing his foundation and making his whole body feel like a world-rooted vessel.
Two. The Vein of Vitality opened, flooding his flesh, blood, and organs with terrifying life force.
Three. The Vein of Speed opened, sharpening his movement and reactions until the whole battlefield seemed to slow down.
Four. The Vein of Strength opened, sending his physical power surging upward.
Then came the fifth. The Vein of Resilience opened.

This was the vein Max had opened over the past few days inside the Dimension of Time. Unlike the Vein of Strength, which boosted his destructive power, or the Vein of Speed, which sharpened his movement, the Vein of Resilience strengthened the durability of his body to a terrifying degree.

It hardened his flesh, bones, organs, meridians, and even the defensive resistance of his inner foundation. It boosted his resistance against every kind of attack, whether physical, elemental, spiritual, law-based, bloodline-based, sealing-based, or pressure-based.
The moment the Vein of Resilience opened, Max’s body turned into something like an indestructible divine mountain wrapped in living law.
The green-gold vines reached him first. They wrapped around his arms, shoulders, waist, and legs. Then they tightened. The spatial layers collapsed inward at the same time.
For a brief instant, the Evercrest platform smiled. Then their smiles froze.
Max stood there without moving. The vines tightened with enough force to crush an ordinary peak Law Manifestation Realm cultivator, and the folded space pressed down on him like overlapping worlds.
Yet Max’s body didn’t bend. His bones didn’t creak. His flesh didn’t tear.

The sealing force pushed into his body, but the Vein of Resilience held it back like an ancient wall. The life-sealing power tried to sink into his blood, but his Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline burned quietly and pushed it right back out.
Max looked at the vines around him. Then he moved his arm.
Crack.
A vine snapped. Then another. Then ten. The entire binding formation shattered, as if it had wrapped itself around something it was never meant to hold.
Aelric’s expression changed.
Max took one step forward. The folded space beneath his foot cracked. The entire Evercrest Hidden Domain trembled.
Aelric immediately shifted his hand seals, and countless spatial mirrors around the battlefield fired green-gold beams at Max.
Each beam carried life-sealing power and spatial compression. Some went for his body. Some targeted his movement route. Some tried to seal Dragonheart. Some aimed at his aura circulation.
Max only raised his sword. The Emotion Severing Path flowed into Dragonheart. But now, under the influence of the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline, this power worked completely differently from before.
The severing aura became colder, cleaner, and frighteningly close to the true essence of law. It didn’t just cut the beams. It cut the connections holding them together.
One slash. The green-gold beams collapsed.
Another slash. The spatial mirrors cracked.
A third slash. The Evercrest Hidden Domain split open in front of him.

Aelric retreated through folded space, but Max moved at almost the same instant. With the Vein of Speed active and the Primordial Bloodline boosting him tenfold, Max’s speed was terrifying. He crossed the broken spatial layers before Aelric could fully reposition himself.
Dragonheart came down. Aelric raised both palms and formed a green-gold barrier.
"Evercrest Worldwood Guard!"

A vast tree silhouette appeared behind him, its branches spreading out like a defensive sky. The barrier held both life force and folded space, making it hard to break through with a normal attack. But Max’s blade carried more than just strength. It carried severing authority.
The sword struck.
Boom!
The Worldwood Guard split from top to bottom. Aelric got thrown backward, his feet tearing across the battlefield as he coughed up a mouthful of blood.
The whole arena fell silent.
The Evercrest descendants stared in disbelief. Aelric had used his full strength. He’d opened the Evercrest Hidden Domain, used life-sealing vines, spatial mirrors, and the Worldwood Guard.
Every one of those techniques was strong enough to beat most peak Law Manifestation Realm geniuses on its own. Yet Max had broken through all of them almost casually after activating his new state.

Rose looked at Max with wide eyes. She’d known he was strong. Everyone knew he was strong. But this was different. Max sat only at the 6th level of the Law Refinement Realm, yet after activating the Primordial Bloodline and five Divine Veins, he was overpowering Aelric Evercrest, a peak Law Manifestation Realm sacred clan heir, in front of all Four Sacred Clans.

Aelric slowly stood back up. His refined appearance had finally been ruined. Blood stained the corner of his mouth, and several cuts had opened across his robe. His eyes were no longer calm. They carried anger, disbelief, and humiliation.
He clenched his fists. The space behind him began to twist violently.
"You think you can beat me that easily?"

The green-gold light around Aelric erupted again, far stronger than before. This time, the entire battlefield reacted. The runes beneath the arena flashed repeatedly, and the hidden spatial layers of the Evercrest end resonated with him.
Aelric placed both hands in front of his chest, and a mark appeared between his brows. It was leaf-shaped, but it wasn’t gentle. It looked like a blade.
Rose’s face changed. "He’s using the forbidden bloodline mark."
The Evercrest platform turned serious. Several elders leaned forward.

Aelric’s aura climbed again, and a massive tree formed behind him. This tree looked nothing like the defensive silhouette from before. It was ancient, enormous, and dark green, its branches stretching into folded space and its roots piercing into the battlefield.
Every root carried life-sealing power. Every branch held a spatial domain. Every leaf shone with runes that could tear, bind, seal, or redirect power.
Aelric’s voice rang across the arena.
"Evercrest Forbidden Art."
"Ancestor Wood Seals the Ten Thousand Spaces."
The whole arena shook. The massive tree behind him expanded so fast it looked ready to swallow the entire battlefield. Branches pierced into space and pulled out layers of hidden domains.

Roots spread across the arena floor and locked down every movement path. Countless green-gold seals appeared in the air, forming a cage so vast and complex that even the audience outside the battlefield felt suffocated.

chapters.title: Chapter 1962: Shocked Max!
paragraphs: This was Aelric’s strongest attack. A forbidden art powered by his Evercrest bloodline. It didn’t just attack the opponent. It tried to seal the entire battlefield, fold every direction, bind every escape route, and crush the enemy beneath the combined weight of space and life.
Moreover, this was also his pseudo cosmic path. His pseudo cosmic path was so strong that it couldn’t be utilized without using an external technique or having an external source of power.

The arena formation trembled under the pressure. Even Angelina Valerius narrowed her eyes slightly. The people of Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest all fell silent. No one had expected Aelric to be forced into using such a powerful attack in the very first battle.
Max looked at the enormous sealing tree descending toward him. The pressure was strong, far stronger than anything Aelric had used earlier.

The entire battlefield seemed to turn into a cage, and every part of that cage was closing in around Max. If he’d been an ordinary genius, even a peak Law Manifestation Realm genius, this attack could have decided the battle instantly.
But Max wasn’t ordinary.
His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline pulsed again. The laws around him drew even closer. The five Divine Veins inside him blazed with power.
The Vein of Origin. The Vein of Vitality. The Vein of Speed. The Vein of Strength. The Vein of Resilience. His body turned stable, full of life, fast, powerful, and nearly unbreakable.

The Vein of Resilience resisted the sealing pressure trying to push into his body. The Vein of Strength drove terrifying force into his arms. The Vein of Speed sharpened his reaction to every closing spatial layer. The Vein of Vitality kept his blood and flesh in perfect condition. The Vein of Origin anchored everything together.

Then Max raised Dragonheart. This time, he didn’t rely on the Emotion Severing Path alone. Divine King Punishment descended. Seven-colored lightning wrapped around the blade, forming the faint image of a divine tribunal above him.

At the same time, the Devouring Flames Domain condensed into black fire along the sword edge. The Emotion Severing Path flowed through the center, turning the slash into a blade that could cut through more than matter alone. It could cut connection, sealing roots, law threads, and the very structure holding Aelric’s forbidden art together.
Under the boost from the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline, all three Pseudo Cosmic Paths became terrifying. Ten times stronger. Ten times sharper. Ten times closer to the laws they represented.
Max’s white hair moved in the storm of green-gold light. He stepped forward. The arena shook.
Aelric roared, "Seal him!"
The enormous ancestor tree descended.
Max swung Dragonheart. "Break."
One word. One slash. A black, seven-colored, and invisible sword light tore across the battlefield.

The slash cut through the first layer of space. Then the second. Then the third. The roots of the ancestor tree were severed from the battlefield. The branches lost their connection to the folded domains.

The life-sealing runes were judged by Divine King Punishment and shattered under seven-colored lightning. The black flames devoured the loosened power. The Emotion Severing Path cut through the final structure holding the forbidden art together.
For a moment, the entire arena turned silent. Then the massive tree split apart.
Boom!
The explosion shook the arena violently. Green-gold light scattered like broken stars. Spatial layers collapsed one after another.
The sealing roots snapped across the battlefield, and the runes beneath the arena flashed madly to suppress the aftershock. Even the four sacred clan platforms felt the vibration under their feet.
Aelric stood frozen behind the collapsing forbidden art. His eyes went wide. He couldn’t believe it. His strongest attack had been broken. Not avoided. Not delayed. Broken straight from the front.

Max appeared before him through the storm of shattered light. Aelric tried to raise his hand, but Max was faster. Dragonheart stopped at Aelric’s throat. The black blade touched his skin lightly, and a thin line of blood appeared.
Aelric’s body stiffened. The battlefield went completely silent.
Max looked at him calmly. "You lose."

Aelric’s face turned pale. The strongest Evercrest heir of the current generation had been defeated. Not after a long battle. Not after exhausting Max. Defeated cleanly, in front of the statue of the First Progenitor, before the eyes of Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest.
For several breaths, no one spoke. Then Angelina Valerius’s voice rang across the arena.
"Aelric Evercrest is defeated."
She looked at Max, and even her eyes carried a trace of amazement.
"Winner, Max Morgan."
Angelina’s eyes remained on Max for several moments. She could feel that Max had grown way stronger than what he was at during the Cosmic Ascension Conference.
’Is it the Primordial Race bloodline?’ She wondered. Though she wasn’t certain if it was only the Primordial Race bloodline or something else was boosting Max’s power.
The entire arena erupted. The Evercrest platform filled with disbelief and humiliation. The Ashbourne side burst into excited laughter.

The Valerius side turned solemn. The Ravenhart descendants watched Max with eyes that had grown far more serious. Rose stood on the lower platform, staring at the scene with emotions she couldn’t fully hide.

Max lowered Dragonheart. His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline slowly quieted down. The five Divine Veins closed one after another. The tenfold strength faded, but the memory of that power stayed inside him like a promise.
He could feel it clearly. This was only the beginning of the Primordial Bloodline’s power. He hadn’t even unlocked its true potential yet.

But more than that, something else about the fight had left Max troubled. All through the battle with Aelric, he kept sensing that Aelric’s bloodline felt strangely familiar, and the more Aelric drew on it, the more Max felt something stirring inside himself in response.
By the very end, Max finally realized what part of him had been reacting to Aelric’s bloodline.
What he found shocked him to his core.
Even more than that, it left him with a flood of questions, questions he had no way of answering yet.

chapters.title: Chapter 1963: A Connection!
paragraphs: Aelric’s bloodline, Max’s own bloodline, and the statue were somehow connected. That much was obvious from the fight itself. But the question was how.
What truly disturbed Max wasn’t the connection itself. It was the way his own blood had responded to it.

The moment Aelric’s forbidden bloodline mark appeared, something inside Max’s foundation had stirred again. Not just the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline. Not just the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline or the Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline. Something deeper had reacted, something that didn’t clearly belong to any bloodline he could name.
It felt like his body had heard a call.
For the first time, Max realized that this reaction might not stay passive. Maybe it could be tested.

His eyes moved toward the statue of the First Progenitor standing at one end of the arena. The stone figure stayed silent, its eyes closed, its massive form towering over the Bloodline Legacy Battle like an ancient judge.
When Max looked at it now, his blood pulsed faintly again. The reaction stayed subtle because he’d kept it suppressed, but it was there.
Max’s gaze deepened.
’There’s a connection.’
He didn’t know what that connection meant. He didn’t know if it was dangerous. He didn’t know if it would benefit him, Rose, or neither of them.
But he knew one thing. If he did nothing, he might lose the chance to uncover it.

A daring thought rose in his mind. It was reckless. It was bold. It would definitely alarm the Four Sacred Clans. But the longer Max looked at the statue, the more certain he became that ordinary methods wouldn’t be enough to pull out the truth. The forbidden bloodline of the Four Sacred Clans was buried too deep.

Rose couldn’t even say its true name outside the clan. The Evercrest elders would never willingly explain the deeper secret to an outsider, no matter how famous he was. If Max wanted answers, he had to force the hidden connection to respond.
He made up his mind.
At that moment, Angelina Valerius looked toward him from the edge of the battlefield.
"Max Morgan," she said, her voice carrying across the arena once the noise started to settle. "As the victor, you may remain in the arena. Do you wish to challenge anyone else?"

The question pulled everyone’s attention back to him. Many people from the Four Sacred Clans straightened up. After beating Aelric Evercrest, Max had already earned Rose an enormous amount of legacy merit.
If he kept challenging others, the Bloodline Legacy Battle might turn into a stage where he swept through the sacred clan heirs one by one.

Cassian Valerius opened his eyes on the Valerius platform. Draven Ashbourne grinned coldly. Seraphine Ravenhart watched with calm interest. Several other heirs and representatives tensed up too, wondering if Max would point at them next.
Rose looked at Max from the lower platform. She was still stunned by his win over Aelric, but the second she saw his expression, her chest tightened.
She knew that look. Max was about to do something unexpected.
Max looked at Angelina and shook his head. "I don’t want to challenge anyone else."
The arena stirred slightly. Some people relaxed. Some frowned.
Angelina raised an eyebrow with faint interest. "Then do you wish to leave the battlefield?"
"No."
Angelina’s smile deepened. "Then what do you want to do?"
Max looked toward the statue of the First Progenitor. "I want to try something else."
The arena quieted again.
Angelina’s eyes narrowed slightly. "Try what?"

Max lowered Dragonheart, then slowly put the sword away. That alone confused a lot of people. A swordsman putting his sword away in the middle of the Bloodline Legacy Battle was strange enough on its own, but Max’s next words made things even more peculiar.
"I don’t know."
The words carried clearly across the arena. For a moment, nobody understood what he meant. Even Angelina fell silent.
Max didn’t explain. He raised his right hand slowly, then clenched it into a fist.

Deep inside his foundation, he reached toward a power he didn’t fully control and didn’t casually reveal. The Dimensional Keeper legacy had been the reason he’d beaten Revona’s Null Origin Tide, but after that battle, he’d only used it cautiously. It was too mysterious, too vast, too far beyond his current understanding.
But now Max needed something capable of touching the hidden layer behind the forbidden bloodline. Ordinary power wouldn’t be enough.
His Primordial Bloodline stirred. His Dimensional Sovereign Body woke up. His blood pulsed toward the statue.
Then the Dimensional Keeper legacy answered.

A dark starry light began gathering around Max’s fist. At first, it looked like faint specks of silver shining beneath his skin. Then those specks multiplied, spreading across his hand like a night sky being born inside flesh.

Each point of light looked small, but if you looked closely, each star seemed to hold a sealed dimension. They shimmered, rotated, and folded inward, making Max’s fist look like it was no longer made of flesh but of countless small worlds hidden inside a dark cosmic sky.
The whole arena went silent.
A star fist. That was the only way to describe it. Max’s fist looked like a piece of the universe had condensed around his hand.
The moment this power appeared, the Four Sacred Clans reacted instantly. Bloodline pressure erupted across the arena, not from Max attacking anyone, but from their own bloodlines reacting.
Every member of Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest felt it at once. Their forbidden bloodlines trembled inside their bodies, then sank, as if an invisible weight had come down from above.

Some weaker descendants clutched their chests. Some heirs stood up in disbelief. Several elders’ expressions changed sharply. Even the strongest young geniuses of the four clans couldn’t stay fully calm.

Cassian Valerius opened his eyes fully, sacred solar light flickering around him in an unstable rhythm. Draven Ashbourne’s grin vanished as the blood-iron aura inside his body shook. Seraphine Ravenhart’s silver-purple eyes widened slightly for the first time, and the shadows around her seat pulled back as if afraid.
On the Evercrest platform, Aelric’s face turned pale again even though he’d already lost. The bloodline mark between his brows flickered weakly, as if it wanted to bow and resist at the same time.
Rose staggered half a step. Her eyes widened as she stared at Max’s fist. Even though she’d been born without the forbidden bloodline, she was still a direct descendant of Evercrest.
She could feel something calling from deep within the ancestral arena. It felt faint, painful, and overwhelming, like a sealed inheritance had suddenly sensed a key.
"What is that?" someone whispered.
No one answered. Because no one knew.

Max’s gaze deepened.
’There’s a connection.’
He didn’t know what that connection meant.
He didn’t know if it was dangerous.
He didn’t know if it would benefit him, Rose, or neither of them.
But he knew one thing.
If he did nothing, he might lose the chance to uncover it.
A daring thought rose in his mind.
It was reckless.
It was bold.
It would definitely alarm the Four Sacred Clans.
But the longer Max looked at the statue, the more certain he became that ordinary methods wouldn’t be enough to pull out the truth.
The forbidden bloodline of the Four Sacred Clans was buried too deep.
Rose couldn’t even say its true name outside the clan.
The Evercrest elders would never willingly explain the deeper secret to an outsider, no matter how famous he was.
If Max wanted answers, he had to force the hidden connection to respond.
He made up his mind.
At that moment, Angelina Valerius looked toward him from the edge of the battlefield.
"Max Morgan," she said, her voice carrying across the arena once the noise started to settle.
"As the victor, you may remain in the arena.
Do you wish to challenge anyone else?"
The question pulled everyone’s attention back to him.
Many people from the Four Sacred Clans straightened up.
After beating Aelric Evercrest, Max had already earned Rose an enormous amount of legacy merit.
If he kept challenging others, the Bloodline Legacy Battle might turn into a stage where he swept through the sacred clan heirs one by one.
Cassian Valerius opened his eyes on the Valerius platform.
Draven Ashbourne grinned coldly.
Seraphine Ravenhart watched with calm interest.
Several other heirs and representatives tensed up too, wondering if Max would point at them next.
Rose looked at Max from the lower platform.
She was still stunned by his win over Aelric, but the second she saw his expression, her chest tightened.
She knew that look.
Max was about to do something unexpected.
Max looked at Angelina and shook his head.
"I don’t want to challenge anyone else."
The arena stirred slightly.
Some people relaxed.
Some frowned.
Angelina raised an eyebrow with faint interest.
"Then do you wish to leave the battlefield?"
"No."
Angelina’s smile deepened.
"Then what do you want to do?"
Max looked toward the statue of the First Progenitor.
"I want to try something else."
The arena quieted again.
Angelina’s eyes narrowed slightly.
"Try what?"
Max lowered Dragonheart, then slowly put the sword away.
That alone confused a lot of people.
A swordsman putting his sword away in the middle of the Bloodline Legacy Battle was strange enough on its own, but Max’s next words made things even more peculiar.
"I don’t know."
The words carried clearly across the arena.
For a moment, nobody understood what he meant.
Even Angelina fell silent.
Max didn’t explain.
He raised his right hand slowly, then clenched it into a fist.
Deep inside his foundation, he reached toward a power he didn’t fully control and didn’t casually reveal.
The Dimensional Keeper legacy had been the reason he’d beaten Revona’s Null Origin Tide, but after that battle, he’d only used it cautiously.
It was too mysterious, too vast, too far beyond his current understanding.
But now Max needed something capable of touching the hidden layer behind the forbidden bloodline.
Ordinary power wouldn’t be enough.
His Primordial Bloodline stirred.
His Dimensional Sovereign Body woke up.
His blood pulsed toward the statue.
Then the Dimensional Keeper legacy answered.
A dark starry light began gathering around Max’s fist.
At first, it looked like faint specks of silver shining beneath his skin.
Then those specks multiplied, spreading across his hand like a night sky being born inside flesh.
Each point of light looked small, but if you looked closely, each star seemed to hold a sealed dimension.
They shimmered, rotated, and folded inward, making Max’s fist look like it was no longer made of flesh but of countless small worlds hidden inside a dark cosmic sky.
The whole arena went silent.
A star fist.
That was the only way to describe it.
Max’s fist looked like a piece of the universe had condensed around his hand.
The moment this power appeared, the Four Sacred Clans reacted instantly.
Bloodline pressure erupted across the arena, not from Max attacking anyone, but from their own bloodlines reacting.
Every member of Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest felt it at once.
Their forbidden bloodlines trembled inside their bodies, then sank, as if an invisible weight had come down from above.
Some weaker descendants clutched their chests.
Some heirs stood up in disbelief.
Several elders’ expressions changed sharply.
Even the strongest young geniuses of the four clans couldn’t stay fully calm.
Cassian Valerius opened his eyes fully, sacred solar light flickering around him in an unstable rhythm.
Draven Ashbourne’s grin vanished as the blood-iron aura inside his body shook.
Seraphine Ravenhart’s silver-purple eyes widened slightly for the first time, and the shadows around her seat pulled back as if afraid.
On the Evercrest platform, Aelric’s face turned pale again even though he’d already lost.
The bloodline mark between his brows flickered weakly, as if it wanted to bow and resist at the same time.
Rose staggered half a step.
Her eyes widened as she stared at Max’s fist.
Even though she’d been born without the forbidden bloodline, she was still a direct descendant of Evercrest.
She could feel something calling from deep within the ancestral arena.
It felt faint, painful, and overwhelming, like a sealed inheritance had suddenly sensed a key.
"What is that?" someone whispered.
No one answered.
Because no one knew.

chapters.title: Chapter 1964: A Traitor’s Bloodline!
paragraphs: The leaders of the Four Sacred Clans, who’d been watching from the highest seats, finally reacted.

On the Valerius end, an old man in white-gold robes stood up, his eyes blazing with sacred light. On the Ashbourne end, a dark-armored patriarch leaned forward, the stone beneath his hand cracking silently. On the Ravenhart end, a veiled matriarch’s shadow spread across half the platform. On the Evercrest end, several elders rose at the same time, their faces filled with shock and alarm.
One of them shouted, "Max Morgan, what are you doing?"
Another elder’s voice followed right after. "Stop!"
Even Angelina Valerius’s expression changed.
"Max," she said, her voice sharper than before. "Wait."

But Max didn’t wait. His eyes stayed fixed on the statue of the First Progenitor. The starry light around his fist grew brighter. The arena formation trembled, not because it was being destroyed, but because it couldn’t understand the nature of the power gathering inside his hand.

It wasn’t ordinary spatial power. It wasn’t pure dimensional power either. It was legacy power, sealed-world power, and a kind of authority that seemed to stand outside the rules the Four Sacred Clans had placed inside the battlefield.
Max inhaled slowly. Then he took one step forward.
The ground beneath his foot cracked. The suppressed bloodline reactions across the four clan platforms grew even stronger.

The statue of the First Progenitor, which had stayed silent since the battle began, finally reacted. A faint vibration came from within it. It was so soft that most people probably missed it. But Max heard it. His blood heard it. The Dimensional Keeper legacy around his fist pulsed in response.

The leaders of the Four Sacred Clans were about to speak again, but Max had already raised his fist. He didn’t aim at Aelric. He didn’t aim at the clan platforms. He aimed at the ground beneath the arena.
Then he slammed his star-like fist down.
Boom.
The moment Max’s star-like fist struck the arena floor, the entire Bloodline Legacy Battle arena trembled as if something ancient beneath it had finally been woken up.
The first thing to react was the statue of the First Progenitor. The enormous stone figure that had stood silently at one end of the arena began to glow.

At first the light was faint, just a thin line spreading along the closed eyelids of the statue. Then that light moved across its face, down its neck, through the folds of its stone robe, and into the hand resting near its side.
Every line carved into the statue lit up with a deep starry radiance, not gold, not green, not crimson, not purple, but a color that seemed to hold the dark sky and countless hidden worlds inside it.
The pressure on the Four Sacred Clans increased at once. It didn’t come from Max alone. It came from the statue.

The bloodlines of Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest trembled violently, and this time the suppression was far worse than before. Countless descendants who’d awakened the forbidden bloodline clutched their chests and went pale.

Some younger heirs dropped to one knee, their faces filled with disbelief as their bloodline marks flickered uncontrollably. Even powerful elders felt the flow of their blood slow down, as if the very source of their inherited power had been pressed beneath a higher authority.
"What is happening?"
"My bloodline is being suppressed!"
"How is this possible? This is the First Progenitor’s arena!"
"The statue’s reacting to him!"
"No, impossible. He’s an outsider!"
The voices spread across the four clan ends in a wave of panic and disbelief.

Max stood at the center of the battlefield with his fist still pressed against the cracked arena floor. The Dimensional Keeper legacy kept shining around his hand like a miniature universe, and the starry light flowing from his fist had already sunk into the deepest formation beneath the battlefield.

He could feel it now. The arena wasn’t just an arena. It was a sealed structure, a lock placed over something hidden, and his fist had struck exactly the layer that the Four Sacred Clans themselves seemed to have forgotten or deliberately buried.
The statue’s closed eyes glowed brighter. Then the fifth end of the arena lit up. Not the Valerius end. Not Ashbourne. Not Ravenhart. Not Evercrest. Not even the end where the statue stood.
The abandoned end.
The broken, dark, empty platform that no one had occupied since the Bloodline Legacy Battle began suddenly erupted with light. Ancient cracks across its surface filled with starry radiance.

Broken stone seats repaired themselves in flashes of silver and black. Old banners that hadn’t been visible before slowly appeared out of the air, torn and faded, yet still carrying a symbol that made the blood of the Four Sacred Clans tremble even harder.
The entire arena froze. Even Max was surprised. His eyes moved toward the abandoned end, and for the first time since he’d entered this arena, his expression changed openly.
The abandoned platform wasn’t empty anymore. It had never been truly empty. It had been sealed. Forgotten. Erased from open memory. But not destroyed.

The starry symbol above that end began to take shape. It didn’t look like the sacred sun of Valerius, the blood-iron mark of Ashbourne, the shadow-feather of Ravenhart, or the worldwood emblem of Evercrest.
It looked like a dark star surrounded by broken dimensional rings, and every time the symbol pulsed, the Dimensional Keeper legacy around Max’s fist responded.
The leaders of the Four Sacred Clans all stood up at once. Their expressions had completely changed. Shock. Fear. Rage. Recognition.
The old man from Valerius stared at Max, his white-gold eyes no longer calm. "That symbol..."
The dark-armored leader of Ashbourne clenched his hand so hard the space around his fingers cracked. "Impossible. That bloodline should have disappeared."
The veiled matriarch of Ravenhart whispered, but her voice still carried strangely across the arena. "The abandoned end has awakened."
The Evercrest patriarch looked at Max as if he’d finally seen a ghost from an ancient nightmare. "No wonder the statue reacted."
Rose stood below the Evercrest platform, completely stunned. She looked from Max to the glowing abandoned end, then back to Max. All the color had drained from her face.

She didn’t understand everything, but she understood enough to realize that something far bigger than the Bloodline Legacy Battle had just happened. Max wasn’t merely a powerful outsider who’d come to represent her.
The arena had recognized him. Or rather, something hidden inside the arena had recognized his power.

Angelina Valerius stood at the edge of the battlefield with narrowed eyes, her expression more serious than Max had ever seen it. She looked at the abandoned end, then at the statue, then at Max’s star-like fist.
For a moment, no one moved.
Then the Valerius leader spoke in a cold voice.
"He carries it."
The Ashbourne leader’s eyes filled with killing intent. "The traitor’s bloodline."
The words hit the arena like thunder. The descendants of the Four Sacred Clans turned toward Max in disbelief.
"The traitor’s bloodline?"
"What does that mean?"
"Is he connected to the abandoned end?"
"But he’s Max Morgan. Wasn’t he from the Black Dragon Clan?"
"Did the traitor’s line survive?"
"How can a descendant of that bloodline show up here now?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1965: Blood of traitor!
paragraphs: Max slowly stood up straight. The starry light around his fist hadn’t disappeared. It kept flowing faintly, and every pulse from it made the abandoned end brighter. His gaze swept across the leaders of the Four Sacred Clans, and his mind raced.
’Traitor’s bloodline?’
He’d expected a reaction. He’d expected the statue to reveal something. He hadn’t expected the Four Sacred Clans to recognize him as the descendant of something they called a traitor.

The Evercrest patriarch’s voice turned colder. "No outsider could awaken the abandoned end. No outsider could make the First Progenitor statue glow like this. No outsider could suppress the bloodlines of the Four Sacred Clans through that cursed star power."
The Ravenhart matriarch said softly, "He’s using the stolen legacy to suppress us. So it was true after all. The Voidwalker really did steal the true legacy and betray us."

The Ashbourne leader took one step forward, and the entire Ashbourne end shook beneath him. "I told you this many times, and it was true. There’s no need to keep going with the Bloodline Legacy Battle."
Rose’s expression changed. "Wait!"
No one listened to her.
The Valerius leader raised his hand. "Seal the arena."
The moment his command fell, the ancient formations around the entire battlefield activated at full power. Golden chains rose from the Valerius end. Crimson-black chains erupted from Ashbourne.

Purple shadow chains extended from Ravenhart. Green-silver spatial chains surged from Evercrest. All four sacred clan ends released their authority at once, and the chains shot toward the central battlefield like divine serpents.
Their target was Max.
Angelina’s face changed slightly. "Elders, this is still the Bloodline Legacy Battle."
The Valerius leader said coldly, "This is no longer a matter of the battle."
The Evercrest patriarch’s voice followed. "A descendant of the traitor’s bloodline has appeared in the First Progenitor Arena. He must be imprisoned immediately."
Max’s eyes turned cold. "So that’s your decision?"
The Ashbourne leader sneered. "You dare to awaken that abandoned end and still ask about our decision? Do you even know whose bloodline you’re carrying?"
Max’s eyes narrowed at that question, but he didn’t need to think it over.

The chains descended. Max sensed right away how powerful they were. These weren’t ordinary sealing chains. They were formed from the combined bloodline authority of the Four Sacred Clans and empowered by the arena itself.
If they caught him, even his current strength might get heavily suppressed, especially with the First Progenitor Arena acting as the foundation.
The first golden chain reached him. Max raised his hand and struck it with his star-like fist.
Boom!
The chain trembled violently and cracked halfway, but it didn’t break completely. The crimson-black chain from Ashbourne wrapped around from the side, carrying brutal bloodline force.
The purple chain from Ravenhart vanished into shadow and appeared behind his back. The Evercrest chain folded through space and tried to bind his legs.
Max’s Dimensional Sovereign Body activated. His Primordial Bloodline stirred. The five Divine Veins inside him opened in rapid succession.
The Vein of Origin. The Vein of Vitality. The Vein of Speed. The Vein of Strength. The Vein of Resilience.

His body erupted with terrifying power, and the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline multiplied his strength tenfold again. For a moment, the air around him twisted under the combined force of Primordial authority, Divine Veins, and the Dimensional Keeper legacy.
Yet the four chains were still dangerous. They weren’t coming from young geniuses. They were coming from the leaders and formations of the Four Sacred Clans.

Max moved. The Vein of Speed pushed him out of the first sealing layer, while his Dimensional Sovereign Body tore open a gap in the folded space. The Evercrest chain chased him through the gap. Max turned, Dragonheart appearing in his hand again, and slashed down with the Emotion Severing Path.

The green-silver chain got cut apart from its spatial anchor. But before it could fully collapse, the Ravenhart shadow chain struck his back. The Vein of Resilience flared. The chain failed to pierce him, but its shadow force still wrapped around his aura and tried to pull his soul into stillness.
Max’s eyes sharpened. His Dimension of Soul opened faintly inside him, swallowing the soul-stilling force before it could settle.

The arena erupted into chaos. The crowd scattered backward as the sealing pressure spread. Many younger descendants couldn’t even stand. Some elders hurriedly shielded their clan members, while others stared at Max in shock.
"He resisted the four-clan seal!"
"How is that possible?"
"He’s only at the Law Refinement Realm!"
"That fist, that starry power, and his body, what kind of monster is he?"
Rose tried to rush forward, but several Evercrest elders appeared in front of her and blocked her path.
"Move!" Rose shouted.
One elder looked at her coldly. "Rose Evercrest, you brought him here."
Her face went pale.
The elder’s voice grew heavier. "If he truly carries the traitor’s bloodline, then you’ve committed a serious offense."
Rose clenched her fists. "I didn’t know."
"Then pray that ignorance is enough to save you."
On the battlefield, Max glanced toward Rose for a brief instant and saw what was happening around her. His gaze turned colder.
The Valerius leader’s voice rang out again.
"Max Morgan, you carry the bloodline of the traitors. You are a Voidwalker. Do not resist. The Four Sacred Clans will investigate your origin. If you’re innocent, you’ll be given an explanation."
Max laughed. It wasn’t loud, but it carried clearly across the battlefield.
"Innocent?"
His grip on Dragonheart tightened.
"You call me the descendant of a traitor’s bloodline, try to imprison me in front of everyone, and then talk about innocence?"
The Ashbourne leader’s eyes burned with dark killing intent. "You are not qualified to argue."

Max’s smile disappeared. The Dimensional Keeper legacy around his fist grew brighter. The abandoned end of the arena pulsed again in response, and the pressure suppressing the Four Sacred Clans grew even heavier.
Several elders’ faces changed as they realized that the more they tried to seal Max, the more the abandoned end woke up.

The statue of the First Progenitor glowed brighter. Its closed eyes trembled. A deep, ancient voice seemed to echo faintly from beneath the arena, too unclear to make out, but powerful enough to make every forbidden bloodline in the arena shake.
Max looked at the leaders of the Four Sacred Clans. His expression settled back into calm. But this calm ran far colder than before.
"I came here to repay a promise," he said. "I didn’t come here to be chained."
The golden, crimson-black, purple, and green-silver chains attacked again, this time with even greater force.
Max raised Dragonheart in one hand and kept the star-like fist clenched in the other. His white hair moved in the storm of bloodline pressure.
"If you want to imprison me," Max said, his voice cutting through the entire arena, "then you’d better be ready to pay the price."

He finally understood why Freya had told him to never reveal his Voidwalker name. It turned out Voidwalker was tied to the Four Sacred Clans. And from the looks of things, Voidwalker had done something pretty ugly to the other four.

"He’s only at the Law Refinement Realm!"
"That fist, that starry power, and his body, what kind of monster is he?"
Rose tried to rush forward, but several Evercrest elders appeared in front of her and blocked her path.
"Move!" Rose shouted.
One elder looked at her coldly.
"Rose Evercrest, you brought him here."
Her face went pale.
The elder’s voice grew heavier.
"If he truly carries the traitor’s bloodline, then you’ve committed a serious offense."
Rose clenched her fists.
"I didn’t know."
"Then pray that ignorance is enough to save you."
On the battlefield, Max glanced toward Rose for a brief instant and saw what was happening around her.
His gaze turned colder.
The Valerius leader’s voice rang out again.
"Max Morgan, you carry the bloodline of the traitors.
You are a Voidwalker.
Do not resist.
The Four Sacred Clans will investigate your origin.
If you’re innocent, you’ll be given an explanation."
Max laughed.
It wasn’t loud, but it carried clearly across the battlefield.
"Innocent?"
His grip on Dragonheart tightened.
"You call me the descendant of a traitor’s bloodline, try to imprison me in front of everyone, and then talk about innocence?"
The Ashbourne leader’s eyes burned with dark killing intent.
"You are not qualified to argue."
Max’s smile disappeared.
The Dimensional Keeper legacy around his fist grew brighter.
The abandoned end of the arena pulsed again in response, and the pressure suppressing the Four Sacred Clans grew even heavier.
Several elders’ faces changed as they realized that the more they tried to seal Max, the more the abandoned end woke up.
The statue of the First Progenitor glowed brighter.
Its closed eyes trembled.
A deep, ancient voice seemed to echo faintly from beneath the arena, too unclear to make out, but powerful enough to make every forbidden bloodline in the arena shake.
Max looked at the leaders of the Four Sacred Clans.
His expression settled back into calm.
But this calm ran far colder than before.
"I came here to repay a promise," he said.
"I didn’t come here to be chained."
The golden, crimson-black, purple, and green-silver chains attacked again, this time with even greater force.
Max raised Dragonheart in one hand and kept the star-like fist clenched in the other.
His white hair moved in the storm of bloodline pressure.
"If you want to imprison me," Max said, his voice cutting through the entire arena, "then you’d better be ready to pay the price."
He finally understood why Freya had told him to never reveal his Voidwalker name.
It turned out Voidwalker was tied to the Four Sacred Clans.
And from the looks of things, Voidwalker had done something pretty ugly to the other four.

chapters.title: Chapter 1966: A Grave Sin!
paragraphs: The four bloodline chains coming down from the sacred clan platforms slowed for the smallest instant, not because the leaders of the Four Sacred Clans were scared, but because the pressure coming off Max had changed.

Up until now, he’d only resisted. He’d cut, dodged, countered, and broken through their seals with the Dimensional Keeper legacy, the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline, the five Divine Veins, and Dragonheart.
But the aura spreading from him now no longer belonged to someone simply defending himself.
It belonged to someone who’d decided to stop holding back.
Max’s eyes swept across the four clan leaders standing high above the arena. Valerius. Ashbourne. Ravenhart. Evercrest.

All four looked at him with cold recognition and hostility. They weren’t treating him as the champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference anymore, or as a Primordial inheritor, or as Rose’s representative. In their eyes, something older had woken up the moment the abandoned end of the arena lit up.
The Valerius leader raised his hand again, and golden sacred fire wrapped around the chain stretching from his platform. "Max Morgan, there’s no use resisting. You carry the blood of traitors."
The Ashbourne leader’s voice followed like iron grinding against bone. "The blood of the Voidwalker Clan."
The moment that name was spoken, the whole arena seemed to freeze.
Voidwalker.

Many younger descendants didn’t understand the weight behind that name, but the elders did. The instant they heard it, their expressions shifted. Some showed fear. Some showed hatred. Some showed disbelief, as if an ancient taboo had been dragged back from the dead and dropped right into the center of the First Progenitor Arena.
Max’s gaze sharpened.
"Traitors?" he repeated slowly. "Voidwalker betrayed you?"
The Ravenhart matriarch’s veiled face turned toward him. "Not just betrayed us. They abandoned their sacred duty and turned their blades against the Four Sacred Clans."
The Evercrest patriarch’s voice was cold enough to freeze space itself. "They tried to sever the foundation of the First Progenitor’s order."
Max’s expression darkened slightly.
"That’s your claim," he said. "But what did the Voidwalker Clan actually do?"
Silence. A heavy, suffocating silence. None of the four leaders answered.
Instead, the Valerius leader’s sacred fire burned brighter. "You are not qualified to question ancient judgment."
Max’s eyes narrowed further. "So you’re telling me nothing."
The Ashbourne leader’s tone turned sharper. "You carry their blood. That’s enough."
Max let out a slow breath. "So I’m an enemy just because of blood?"
The Ravenhart matriarch spoke again, colder this time. "The Voidwalker Clan are a sin to the Four Sacred Clan and that makes you a sin as well."
The Evercrest patriarch raised his hand slightly. "By sacred law, any inheritor of the Voidwalker lineage must be sealed."
Rose’s face went pale.
"Max!" she shouted from below. "This is insane! He hasn’t done anything!"

But several Evercrest elders immediately smothered her voice with pressure and forced her back. Her eyes trembled as she struggled, realizing she was being treated as a liability just for bringing him here.
Max’s gaze flicked toward her for a moment. That alone was enough. His expression cooled completely. Then he looked back at the four leaders.
"You still haven’t told me anything," he said quietly. "What did the Voidwalker do? What are their sins?"
The Valerius leader’s eyes burned. "You do not need to know."
The Ashbourne leader added, "You will be imprisoned for the sins your Voidwalker Clan committed."
Max’s voice dropped. "So that’s it."
A faint, humorless smile crossed his face. "You want to seal me without even explaining why."
The Ravenhart matriarch’s voice turned final. "Seal him."
The Evercrest patriarch followed immediately. "By order of the Four Sacred Clans, Max Morgan is to be imprisoned as a Voidwalker inheritor."
The moment those words landed, the chains changed. They no longer aimed to restrain him. Now they carried execution-level sealing intent.
Max stood still for a heartbeat. Then he exhaled.
"Then I guess I don’t have a choice."

The Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline erupted, and it didn’t build up gradually. It happened violently. Black-gold scales surged across his skin as his body began rejecting its human form entirely. His pupils narrowed into vertical slits, and a draconic pressure exploded outward, crashing into the Four Sacred Clans’ sealing force.

The Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline stabilized the foundation underneath it. The five Divine Veins ignited all at once. And the Dimensional Keeper legacy resonated with the abandoned fifth end of the arena, as if something there was answering him.
Max’s voice dropped low.
"Dragon Transformation."

Black light detonated outward. His body expanded, his bones reshaping and his flesh rewriting itself under ancient draconic law. Wings tore out from his back, massive and overwhelming. Horns curved like dark crowns. His form stretched and grew until a gigantic black dragon stood at the center of the arena.
This wasn’t an illusion. It was a true transformation.
The arena erupted in shock.
"A dragon?!"
"He’s a Voidwalker and a dragon bloodline user?!"
"No wonder the clans want him sealed!"
Rose stared upward, her hands trembling.
"Max," she whispered, fear and helplessness mixing in her voice. "Don’t push yourself too far."
But she already knew he had no other choice.
Angelina Valerius stood silently at the edge of the platform, her eyes narrowing slightly.
Above, the four leaders moved at once.
"Suppress him!" the Valerius leader ordered.
The chains came down again, stronger, deeper, more absolute this time. But Max’s dragon eyes opened, and he roared. The sound shattered space itself.
ROAR!

The golden chain got bitten apart instantly. The Ashbourne chain struck his wing but failed to break it. The Ravenhart soul threads pushed into his mind but sank straight into the vast Dimension of Soul. The Evercrest spatial seal tried to lock his body but got redirected into a false dimension and crushed.
The arena trembled violently.
Max lifted his enormous dragon head.
"You want to imprison me," his voice rumbled like collapsing stars, "without even telling me what I’m guilty of?"
The abandoned fifth end of the arena pulsed brighter. The broken dimensional rings above it flickered as if responding.
The Valerius leader’s expression turned cold. "No more words. Seal him completely."
The Ashbourne leader’s killing intent sharpened. "Voidwalker Clan has a committed a grave sin and so they must be punished for their actions."
The Ravenhart matriarch whispered, almost reluctantly, "Even if the truth stays buried with him."
The Evercrest patriarch finished, "He will not leave this arena."
Four massive sealing formations rose.
Rose’s eyes widened in panic. "No!"

But Max had already moved. Black flames gathered in his mouth. The Primordial Bloodline surged. The five Divine Veins burned brighter than ever. And the Dimensional Keeper legacy wrapped around his claw like a star-forged weapon.
Max lowered his dragon body slightly, not retreating but preparing. Then he roared again.
"Then come!"
And the black dragon launched forward to meet the Four Sacred Clans head on.

chapters.title: Chapter 1967: Max vs Four Sacred Clan Heads!
paragraphs: The black dragon launched forward.

His massive wings tore through the air with enough force to stir up a storm across the entire arena. Black chaotic flames burned between his scales, and the starry light of the Dimensional Keeper legacy wrapped around one of his claws like a weapon forged from sealed worlds.

The five Divine Veins burned inside his dragon body, each one magnified by the enormous true-dragon form, and the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline sat above everything like an ancient source pulling him closer to the laws of the world.

The first sealing formation came down from Valerius. A white-gold sun appeared above the arena, and from that sun came countless sacred chains, each one wrapped in burning light. They didn’t simply fall toward Max.
They tried to define him as guilty, brand his bloodline as sinful, and force his dragon body under the judgment of the Four Sacred Clans.
Max roared. Black dragon flames burst from his mouth and collided with the golden chains.
Boom!
The whole sky above the arena exploded in black and white-gold light. The golden chains burned through the dragon flames and kept descending, but their speed dropped sharply.

Max’s enormous claw swept upward, and the starry Dimensional Keeper light around it smashed into the first cluster of chains. Dozens of chains shattered instantly, their fragments falling like broken sunlight across the battlefield.
But the Valerius leader didn’t move. His eyes only turned colder.
"His attacks are fierce," he said, "but his realm is still too low."

The truth in those words showed itself in the next breath. Even though Max shattered dozens of chains, the white-gold sun above him didn’t collapse. The Valerius leader stood far above Max in cultivation, and that gap wasn’t something bloodline and talent alone could erase. Max’s dragon form made him terrifyingly durable.

His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline gave him ten times his normal strength. His five Divine Veins, especially the Vein of Resilience, made his defense almost monstrous. Yet when his attack hit the full formation controlled by a sacred clan head, it could only break part of it, not destroy its source.

Then Ashbourne’s formation arrived. A crimson-black mountain of blood iron dropped from the sky, covered in battle runes and ancient killing marks. It crashed straight onto Max’s back, trying to pin his dragon body to the arena floor.
Boom!
The arena sank. Cracks spread out in every direction. Many descendants from the Four Sacred Clans cried out as the shockwave slammed into the protective barriers around the platforms.
Max’s dragon body bent slightly under the enormous weight, but it didn’t break. His scales shone with black-gold light, and the Vein of Resilience erupted with terrifying defensive power.

The blood-iron mountain pressed down with the might of a sacred clan head, but Max’s body held. His bones didn’t shatter. His wings didn’t snap. His organs didn’t burst. The force poured into his body, only to be resisted by the combined durability of his dragon form, his fifth Divine Vein, and the stabilizing power of the Primordial Bloodline.
The Ashbourne leader’s pupils contracted. "He endured it?"
Max twisted his massive body and slammed his tail against the crimson-black mountain. The impact sent cracks across its lower half, but the mountain didn’t fully break.

It trembled, shifted, and kept pressing down. Max’s attack was powerful enough to stun every younger genius present, but against the deeper formation of Ashbourne’s clan head, it still wasn’t enough to fully throw off the suppression.
The gap in cultivation was too wide. Max understood this instantly.
’Their attacks can’t easily hurt me, but my attacks can’t easily destroy their foundations either.’
That was the problem. Their attacks bounced off him because his defensive foundation had grown too terrifying. His dragon form was simply too durable to be damaged by anything they threw at him.
On top of that, Max could feel his own abilities reinforcing his dragon body. The Vein of Resilience made it resistant to physical, spiritual, elemental, law-based, sealing, and bloodline attacks.

His Dimension of Soul swallowed any soul interference. His Dimensional Sovereign Body twisted spatial restraints out of shape. His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline pulled him closer to the laws and made his Pseudo Cosmic Paths stronger than ever.

But the four people attacking him weren’t young geniuses. They were the heads of the Four Sacred Clans. Their cultivation stood far above his, and their command over sacred clan formations gave every attack the weight of ancient inheritance.
Max could resist them, break parts of their seals, and force them to take him seriously, but beating all four outright was a different matter entirely.

The Ravenhart matriarch raised her hand. The world darkened. A shadow feather appeared above Max’s head and dissolved into thousands of silent threads. These threads didn’t go for his scales or flesh.
They slipped into the gaps between perception, thought, and reaction, trying to make his mind hesitate for one breath.
One breath was all the four leaders needed. But Max’s dragon eyes glowed coldly. The Dimension of Soul opened up like an endless inner night, and the shadow threads entered him and vanished.
The Ravenhart matriarch’s voice turned solemn. "His soul defense isn’t normal. Don’t waste subtle attacks on him."

The Evercrest patriarch’s face had already darkened. He raised both hands, and the spatial layers around the battlefield folded inward. Green-silver roots appeared from every direction, but unlike Aelric’s roots, these carried the authority of an entire sacred clan head.
They pierced through folded space and wrapped around Max’s wings, claws, horns, and tail, trying to lock the enormous dragon form in place.
Max tore through the first wave. Then the second. Then the third. But more roots kept coming. And more.

The four leaders had already figured out the problem. Max was too hard to injure. His dragon form was too durable, his bloodline too strange, and his fifth Divine Vein made most direct attacks nearly useless unless they threw overwhelming force at him. Since they couldn’t easily destroy his body, they’d try to seal it instead.

The Valerius sun lowered. The Ashbourne blood-iron mountain expanded. The Ravenhart shadow feather spread across the arena like a dark sky. The Evercrest spatial roots tightened. Four greater seals formed together.

The pressure that came down this time worked completely differently from before. It didn’t try to cut Max, burn him, crush him, or pierce his soul. It tried to deny his movement, suppress his bloodline, lock down his dragon form, and bury him under the combined authority of the Four Sacred Clans.
Max’s wings strained. His claws dug into the arena floor. The abandoned Voidwalker end pulsed violently, but even its reaction couldn’t fully break the seals coming down from all four clan heads.
The Valerius leader spoke coldly. "He’s durable, but durability is useless against eternal imprisonment."
The Ashbourne leader clenched his fist. "Seal the dragon body first. Once he’s back in human form, pulling out the truth will be easier."
Rose struggled below, her eyes red with anger and fear. "You call yourselves sacred clans, yet four clan heads are ganging up on one young cultivator?"
An Evercrest elder looked at her coldly. "Silence. You’ve already caused enough trouble."
Rose’s face went pale from the pressure, but she kept glaring at them.
On the battlefield, Max heard her voice. His dragon eyes turned colder.
The four greater seals tightened. His massive dragon body began sinking inch by inch toward the arena floor.
The younger descendants watched in shock and awe.

None of them had expected Max to hold out this long against the leaders of the Four Sacred Clans. Most people at his realm would have been sealed in the first exchange. Yet Max, in true dragon form, had taken attacks from all four sides, shattered parts of their formations, and forced the clan heads to combine their greater seals.
But now, even he seemed to be getting pushed down.

His massive dragon body began sinking inch by inch toward the arena floor.
The younger descendants watched in shock and awe.
None of them had expected Max to hold out this long against the leaders of the Four Sacred Clans.
Most people at his realm would have been sealed in the first exchange.
Yet Max, in true dragon form, had taken attacks from all four sides, shattered parts of their formations, and forced the clan heads to combine their greater seals.
But now, even he seemed to be getting pushed down.

chapters.title: Chapter 1968: Arrival of the Anceastors!
paragraphs: Angelina Valerius watched from the side with a complicated look on her face.
’If this keeps going, they’ll seal him.’
At that moment, Max stopped resisting randomly. His enormous dragon body lowered slightly, not because he was giving up, but because he was gathering power.
The Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline pulsed once. Then twice. The five Divine Veins burned brighter.

The Vein of Origin anchored his entire dragon body. The Vein of Vitality poured life force into every scale and muscle. The Vein of Speed sharpened the movement of his blood, energy, and law. The Vein of Strength gathered all his destructive force into his chest. The Vein of Resilience let him endure the four seals long enough to prepare.

Then the Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline erupted to its absolute limit. The black-gold patterns across Max’s dragon scales lit up like chaotic stars. His wings spread as wide as they could under the pressure of the seals. His massive chest expanded, and all the black flames surrounding his body rushed toward his mouth.
But this wasn’t an ordinary breath attack. The Dimensional Keeper legacy gathered inside the flames.

The Devouring Flames Domain condensed at the core. Divine King Punishment wrapped around it as seven-colored lightning. The Emotion Severing Path became the edge that would cut through sealing foundations. The Primordial Bloodline pulled all of it ten times closer to the source of law.
The entire arena felt the attack coming.
The Valerius leader’s expression shifted. "Stop him."

The Evercrest patriarch immediately tightened the spatial roots. The Ravenhart matriarch sent shadow seals toward Max’s throat. The Ashbourne leader pushed the blood-iron mountain down with both hands.
But Max had already finished gathering his power. His dragon eyes locked onto the Evercrest patriarch.

Among the four clan heads, the Evercrest patriarch’s spatial seal posed the greatest danger to Rose and the biggest restriction on Max’s movement. If Max wanted to break the encirclement, he needed to injure one of them, and the Evercrest patriarch was the right target.
Then Max opened his mouth.
"Black Dragon Cataclysm Breath."

A beam of black-gold dragon fire burst from his mouth. It was enormous. It tore through the battlefield like a collapsing night, carrying chaotic dragon force, primordial closeness to the laws, seven-colored punishment lightning, devouring black flames, and the starry fragments of the Dimensional Keeper legacy.
The moment it moved, the arena formation screamed under the pressure. The attack didn’t spread out randomly. It compressed into a single terrifying line and shot straight toward the Evercrest end.
The Evercrest patriarch’s face changed drastically. He crossed his hands, and countless spatial walls formed in front of him.
"Evercrest Sacred Spatial Wall!"

The first wall shattered. The second wall shattered. The third, fourth, fifth, and sixth walls shattered one after another. The Evercrest patriarch roared and summoned a massive tree of green-silver light in front of him, but the Cataclysm Breath pierced straight through its trunk. Devouring flames ate away its vitality.

The Emotion Severing Path cut its spatial anchors. Divine King Punishment shattered the defensive laws. The Dimensional Keeper legacy warped the distance between the attack and the target, making it arrive faster than the patriarch expected.
Boom!

The breath struck the Evercrest patriarch. The entire Evercrest platform exploded with light. Several elders screamed in shock as the protective formations cracked. The Evercrest patriarch got thrown backward, blood spraying from his mouth.
His robe tore apart across the chest, his aura collapsed violently, and a massive wound burned with black-gold flames that refused to go out right away.
The arena went dead silent. A clan head had been injured. Not by another elder. Not by a Divine Lord ancestor. By Max. By a young cultivator in dragon form.

Even though the Evercrest patriarch hadn’t been killed, and even though he’d blocked most of the attack with layers of sacred defenses, the fact remained that Max had heavily wounded one of the heads of the Four Sacred Clans in front of everyone.

The Valerius leader’s eyes went wide. The Ashbourne leader froze for half a breath. The Ravenhart matriarch’s veil fluttered violently. Angelina stared at Max, her expression finally showing open shock. Rose covered her mouth, unable to speak.

The Evercrest patriarch slowly pushed himself up from the shattered platform, blood still dripping from his lips. The wound on his chest kept burning, and his eyes filled with humiliation and killing intent.
His voice shook with rage.
"You dare injure me?"
Max’s dragon voice rumbled across the arena.
"You tried to imprison me."
That answer only made the silence heavier.

Then the air above the arena changed. Ancient pressure descended, not from the four clan heads, but from deeper within the Four Sacred Clans. One after another, old auras woke up from the sacred clan platforms.

These auras felt far more terrifying than the clan heads. They were ancient, heavy, and carried the weight of countless years. The younger descendants could barely breathe as the sky above Valerius turned white-gold, Ashbourne turned crimson-black, Ravenhart turned shadow-purple, and Evercrest turned green-silver.
The ancestors of the Four Sacred Clans were coming out.
An old voice from Valerius echoed first. "The Voidwalker bloodline has returned."
A brutal voice from Ashbourne followed. "And it’s already injured a clan head."
A soft, eerie voice from Ravenhart whispered across the arena. "The Voidwalker Bloodline."
Then, from the depths of Evercrest, an ancient and furious voice came down. "Let’s seal him before history repeats itself."
Four ancestral figures began forming above the arena. The pressure was so overwhelming that even Max’s massive dragon body felt the weight of it. His eyes narrowed.

This was bad. The clan heads had already given him trouble because of the gap in cultivation and the arena formations working against him. If the ancestors of the Four Sacred Clans stepped in personally, even Max’s current cards might not be enough to get out easily, especially while trying to protect Rose.

But just as the four ancestral pressures were about to fully descend, the abandoned fifth end of the arena erupted. The dark star and broken dimensional rings above it blazed with ancient light. The pressure from the Four Sacred Clan ancestors froze.

A crack opened above the abandoned platform. Not in space. In history. It felt like a sealed presence had been waiting there for countless years, and Max’s bloodline, his Dimensional Keeper legacy, and his defiance as a dragon had finally given it enough reason to appear.
A calm voice echoed from the abandoned end.
"Enough."
One word. The entire arena stopped. The four ancestral figures stiffened. The statue of the First Progenitor glowed brighter.

Max slowly turned his dragon head toward the abandoned end. From the starry crack above that forgotten platform, an old man walked out. He wore a black robe marked with faint silver dimensional rings.

His hair was long and gray, and his eyes looked like two quiet stars surrounded by darkness. He didn’t give off any wild pressure, yet the moment he appeared, the Dimensional Keeper legacy around Max’s body resonated so strongly that the starry light across his dragon scales grew brighter.
The old man stood above the abandoned end and looked at Max. For a moment, his expression softened.
"So one of our blood finally returned."
The Four Sacred Clan ancestors looked at him in shock and fury.
The Valerius ancestor’s voice trembled with disbelief. "You..."
The Ashbourne ancestor growled, "What are you doing here?"
The Ravenhart ancestor whispered, "You should have stayed sealed."
The Evercrest ancestor’s killing intent surged. "So you were still hiding beneath the abandoned end."
The old man didn’t look at them right away. He kept his eyes on Max. Then he raised one hand.
The four greater seals pressing on Max cracked at the same time. The pressure around Max let up instantly.
Only then did the old man turn toward the Four Sacred Clans. His voice stayed calm, but the entire arena trembled beneath it.
"You dare attack my descendant in front of me?"
The arena fell into a silence so heavy that even the younger generation forgot how to breathe.
The ancestor of the Voidwalker Clan had revealed himself. And he had come to protect Max.

chapters.title: Chapter 1969: Ancestor of Voidwalker!
paragraphs: The old man’s voice echoed across the First Progenitor Arena, calm yet heavy enough to silence the chaos that had swallowed the battlefield.
"You dare attack my descendant in front of me?"

The four ancestral figures that had started descending from the sacred clan platforms froze in midair. Their bodies weren’t fully physical yet, but the pressure coming off them was enough to make the whole arena feel like it had sunk beneath four ancient heavens. One stood wrapped in white-gold light, his eyes burning like sacred suns.

One was covered in crimson-black battle aura, his armor lined with old scars and blood iron marks. One stayed half-hidden beneath a veil of shadow and purple feathers, silent and eerie. The last was surrounded by green-silver spatial roots, his old eyes filled with cold fury as he stared at both Max and the Voidwalker Ancestor.
The Voidwalker Ancestor stood above the abandoned fifth end. Compared to the other four, he looked simple. He wore only a black robe marked with faint silver dimensional rings.

His long gray hair drifted slightly in the wind, and his eyes looked like two quiet stars resting inside an endless night. He didn’t release overwhelming rage. He didn’t roar. He didn’t even raise his voice after that first sentence.

Yet the abandoned fifth end glowed beneath his feet. The dark star and broken dimensional rings above it pulsed brighter and brighter, and every pulse made the bloodlines of the Four Sacred Clans tremble, as if being forced to remember a history they’d tried hard to bury.

Max, still in his enormous black dragon form, looked at the old man in silence. The Dimensional Keeper legacy across his scales resonated with the Voidwalker Ancestor’s presence. It wasn’t the simple resonance of similar techniques.

It felt like blood recognizing blood, legacy recognizing its source, and a forgotten seat recognizing the return of its heir. For the first time since the Four Sacred Clans had tried to imprison him, Max felt like the battlefield was no longer completely against him.
The pressure binding his dragon body had loosened. The greater seals from the four clan heads had cracked. Even the ancestors of the Four Sacred Clans had paused.
The Valerius ancestor’s eyes narrowed. "Voidwalker, you still dare call him your descendant?"
The Voidwalker Ancestor turned toward him slowly. "He carries our blood. Of course he’s my descendant."

The Ashbourne ancestor let out a cold laugh laced with killing intent. "Your blood? You talk like that’s something to be proud of. That bloodline should have stayed buried with the rest of your clan."

The Ravenhart ancestor’s voice drifted across the arena like a whisper from a grave. "The abandoned end was sealed. Your name was erased from the sacred records. Your descendants were forbidden from ever coming back. Yet now one’s appeared, holding the stolen legacy in his hands."
Max’s dragon eyes sharpened.
Stolen legacy. That phrase again.

The Evercrest ancestor’s expression was colder than anyone else’s. His descendant, the Evercrest patriarch, had just been badly injured by Max’s Black Dragon Cataclysm Breath, and the wound still burned with black-gold flames across his chest despite several elders’ efforts to suppress it.
That humiliation had already pushed the Evercrest side into fury.

The Evercrest ancestor raised his hand, and the green-silver roots beneath his feet coiled like living serpents. "This boy carries the blood of traitors, and he’s woken up the abandoned Voidwalker end. He has to be sealed, just like the others."
Those words spread across the whole arena.
Just like the others.
Max’s gaze turned colder.
’So there are others.’
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s expression barely shifted, but the air around him grew slightly heavier.
"The others," he repeated softly.

The Valerius ancestor looked at him with stern eyes. "Don’t pretend you’ve forgotten. After the Voidwalker Clan betrayed the sacred pact and stole the legacy that should have belonged to all five clans together, the judgment was already made. Your line was sealed. Your descendants were sealed. Your ancestral end was abandoned. That was the decision of the Four Sacred Clans."
"The four clans," the Voidwalker Ancestor said, his voice still calm. "Not the five?"
The Ashbourne ancestor’s battle aura flared. "Because the fifth lost the right to stand with us."
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked toward the glowing statue of the First Progenitor. For a brief moment, something old and painful crossed his eyes.
"Did we lose that right," he said, "or did you take it from us after deciding the truth was inconvenient?"
The arena went deathly silent. The younger generation of the Four Sacred Clans didn’t dare breathe too loudly.

Most of them had grown up hearing fragments of old warnings, forbidden names, and vague mentions of a traitorous bloodline. They’d been told the Voidwalker Clan was cursed, dangerous, and sealed for the sins it committed. But no one had ever laid out the full story for them.
Now, standing in the First Progenitor Arena, they could sense the truth might not be as simple as their elders claimed.
The Ravenhart ancestor’s shadow stirred. "Don’t twist the past. The Voidwalker Clan took what should never have been taken."
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at her. "We protected what should never have been handed over."
The Valerius ancestor’s eyes burned brighter. "Lies."
"Convenient word," the Voidwalker Ancestor replied. "You used it last time too."

The Evercrest ancestor stepped forward in the air, and the spatial roots around him spread toward the abandoned fifth end. "Enough. Whatever words you use, the result won’t change. The boy has woken up the Voidwalker legacy. He carries the stolen inheritance. If he leaves this place, everything we sealed away might come back."
Max’s massive dragon body shifted slightly. His claws pressed against the broken arena floor, and the black-gold scales along his body gave off a faint chaotic glow.

The Vein of Resilience still strengthened his body, the Primordial Bloodline still multiplied his foundation, and the Dimensional Keeper legacy still shimmered across him, but he didn’t attack. Not yet. He wanted to hear more.
