chapters.title: Chapter 1970: Voidwalker Bloodline!
paragraphs: The Voidwalker Ancestor, though, took one step forward. The abandoned fifth end brightened beneath him.
"You talk about sealing him like he’s some criminal," he said. "What crime has he actually committed?"
The Ashbourne ancestor growled, "He carries the traitor’s blood."
"So do your descendants," the Voidwalker Ancestor said. "They carry the blood of your clans. Does that mean they personally answer for every sin you committed?"
The words landed like a blade. Several elders’ expressions changed.
The Valerius ancestor’s voice turned colder. "Don’t compare our clans to yours."

"I’ll compare them however I please," the Voidwalker Ancestor said. "You’re judging a young man who hasn’t even heard the truth of our history. You call him a traitor because his blood woke up a seat you failed to destroy. You call his legacy stolen because you couldn’t take it back yourselves. You’re trying to seal him because you’re afraid of what he might learn."
The Evercrest ancestor’s killing intent surged. "Careful, Voidwalker."
The Voidwalker Ancestor finally smiled faintly. It wasn’t a warm smile. It was tired and cold.
"Don’t speak to me like you still hold the chains around my neck."
The entire arena trembled. The four ancestors froze. For the first time, their expressions showed genuine shock.
The Valerius ancestor’s voice dropped. "You agreed to the seal."
"Yes," the Voidwalker Ancestor said. "I agreed."
His gaze moved across the four ancestors one by one.

"I agreed last time for the sake of the five clans." The words carried across the arena like thunder hidden beneath calm speech. "Not because I believed your judgment was right. Not because I admitted guilt. Not because the Voidwalker Clan deserved to be erased. I agreed because if the five clans had fought to the end back then, the First Progenitor’s inheritance would have shattered, and every sacred bloodline descended from him would have suffered damage that could never be undone."
The younger descendants stared in shock. This wasn’t the version of history they’d been told.
The Ashbourne ancestor’s face darkened. "You dare bring up old matters in front of juniors?"
"They deserve to know why you’re trying to chain a young man in front of them," the Voidwalker Ancestor said.
The Ravenhart ancestor’s voice turned dangerous. "Some truths are sealed for a reason."
"And some lies are sealed because the people who told them are afraid of being questioned."
The statue of the First Progenitor glowed brighter after those words. The light from its closed eyes deepened, and a pulse passed through the arena.
Max noticed. So did the four ancestors.
The Evercrest ancestor’s expression turned uglier.

The Voidwalker Ancestor continued, "I let myself be sealed because the five clans were already on the edge of collapse. I let the Voidwalker end be abandoned because I thought time might cool your fear and anger. I let your version of history stand because I thought protecting the sacred inheritance mattered more than proving who was right."
His eyes turned colder. "But I won’t make that mistake again."
The arena went silent. The words came out calm. Yet they felt like a declaration of war.
The Valerius ancestor’s sacred light rose higher. "You’d break the old pact?"
"The old pact was between five clans," the Voidwalker Ancestor said. "You four turned it into a prison."

The Ashbourne ancestor clenched his fist, and crimson-black blood iron light spread out behind him like a battlefield of ancient corpses. "If you protect him, you’re standing against the Four Sacred Clans."
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at him without fear. "I’ve stood against worse."
The Ravenhart ancestor whispered, "You’re only a remnant."
The Voidwalker Ancestor nodded. "Yes. I’m only a remnant."
Then his gaze moved to Max. "But he isn’t."
The whole arena turned toward the black dragon. Max’s enormous eyes met the old man’s gaze. There wasn’t full understanding between them yet.

Max still didn’t know the truth about the Voidwalker Clan, the so-called stolen legacy, the old betrayal, or why his blood had awakened the abandoned end. But when the Voidwalker Ancestor looked at him, there was no hatred in it, no suspicion, and no urge to use him as a tool.
There was only protection. Fierce, absolute protection. The kind Max had rarely ever gotten from ancient powers.
The Voidwalker Ancestor turned back to the four ancestors.

"You sealed me. You sealed the others. You buried our end, erased our name, and taught your descendants to spit on a bloodline whose truth they never even knew. I stayed silent once because I thought it would keep the five clans together."
His voice deepened. "This time, I won’t."

The abandoned end erupted with starry light. The dark star symbol above it expanded, and broken dimensional rings rotated around the whole arena. Space folded, not the way Evercrest’s life-space seals did, but in a deeper, more absolute way.
For a moment, everyone present felt like the arena had been pulled out of normal space and placed inside a vast hidden dimension under the Voidwalker Ancestor’s control.

The four ancestors released their auras at once. White-gold fire. Crimson-black blood iron. Shadow-purple fate feathers. Green-silver worldwood space. Four ancient powers pressed toward the abandoned end.

The Voidwalker Ancestor raised one hand. A starry barrier appeared between Max and the four ancestors. Their pressure struck the barrier and spread across it like waves crashing into an endless night sky. The barrier trembled. But it held.
The Valerius ancestor shouted, "Voidwalker, step aside. The boy has to be sealed before the stolen legacy fully wakes up."
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s expression turned cold. "No." The word was simple. Final.
The Evercrest ancestor’s eyes narrowed. "You’d risk everything for one descendant you just met?"
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked back at Max. "He’s not just one descendant," he said. "He’s proof the Voidwalker bloodline survived despite everything you did to stop it."
Max’s heart stirred faintly.

Rose stood below, still surrounded by Evercrest elders, her face full of shock and confusion. But watching the Voidwalker Ancestor stand in front of Max, she understood one thing clearly.
This wasn’t just her battle anymore. This was history coming back.

chapters.title: Chapter 1971: Arrival of the Others!
paragraphs: The Ashbourne ancestor roared, "Then you leave us no choice."
The four ancestors moved.

At the same time, the Voidwalker Ancestor stepped forward. The starry barrier around Max expanded, and the broken dimensional rings above the abandoned end spun faster. The statue of the First Progenitor glowed even brighter, as if watching a scene that had happened once before, long ago, now repeating in front of its closed eyes.
Max’s dragon claws dug into the ground. His voice rumbled behind the barrier.
"Ancestor."
The old man didn’t turn back. But he answered.
"Stay behind me for now."
Max’s dragon eyes narrowed.

The Voidwalker Ancestor’s voice softened just slightly. "You’ve done enough. You woke up the fifth end. You forced the buried truth to the surface. Now let this old man do what he failed to do properly last time."

The four ancestral powers descended. The Voidwalker Ancestor raised both hands. A sea of stars opened up behind him. And the abandoned fifth end, forgotten for countless years, finally returned to the Bloodline Legacy Battle.
The sea of stars behind the Voidwalker Ancestor had just started to open when the sky above the Bloodline Legacy Battle arena changed again.
This time, the change didn’t come from the abandoned fifth end. It came from outside.
A tremendous spatial pressure came down from above the arena, and the protective boundary around the Bloodline Legacy Battle shook, as if countless hands had grabbed it from every direction at once.

The four ancestors, who’d been ready to clash with the Voidwalker Ancestor, lifted their heads almost at the same moment. The clan heads and elders looked upward too, their expressions shifting sharply as they sensed thousands of auras appearing beyond the sacred arena’s outer sky.
Max also lifted his massive dragon head. He didn’t need to look carefully to know who stood at the front. His blood recognized her before his eyes did.
High above the arena, a crack opened across the sky like a blade slicing through silk. Figures emerged from that crack one after another. Not dozens. Not hundreds. Thousands.
They appeared in perfect formation, surrounding the entire Bloodline Legacy Battle arena from the sky, each one carrying a cold, disciplined aura.
Their robes were dark, marked with silver dimensional lines, and many of them held weapons glowing faintly with the same star-like light that had woken from the abandoned fifth end.
At the front stood a woman with long silver-white hair flowing behind her like a river of moonlight.
Freya.
Max’s dragon eyes went wide. For a moment, even the storm of battle inside him went still.

He’d known she was alive, known she existed somewhere outside the ordinary reach of his current life. But knowing and seeing were two different things. Now she stood above the Bloodline Legacy Battle arena, alive, powerful, carrying an aura that felt deeply familiar.
His big sister.
Max’s heart shook in a way no battle had ever managed to shake it.
"Freya," he murmured, though it came out as a deep dragon rumble.
A strange kind of happiness rose in him, sharp enough to cut through all the danger surrounding him.

The Four Sacred Clans were trying to seal him. Their ancestors had shown up. The Voidwalker Ancestor stood in front of him. The truth about his bloodline was turning the whole arena upside down. Yet for that one breath, Max only looked at Freya.
She was here. His big sister was here.

Freya’s gaze found him immediately. She saw the enormous black dragon standing in the ruined central battlefield, saw the broken seals around him, saw the bloodline pressure surrounding him, and saw the glow of the abandoned Voidwalker end beneath the ancestor. Her expression barely changed, but her eyes softened for the smallest instant.
Then her gaze turned cold. Very cold.
She looked toward the four ancestors of Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest.
"Stop."
Her voice wasn’t loud, but it carried across the whole arena with terrifying clarity.
The four ancestors looked at her, eyes narrowed.
The Valerius ancestor’s sacred light burned brighter. "Who are you to give orders to the Four Sacred Clans?"
Freya didn’t answer right away. She raised one hand.

At that instant, the thousands of figures who’d arrived with her moved. They spread across the sky and completely surrounded the Bloodline Legacy Battle arena. Space rippled around them as formation flags, star-like seals, and dimensional weapons activated one after another.

A ring of Voidwalker power formed above the arena, and for the first time since the conflict began, the descendants of the Four Sacred Clans felt danger coming not from inside the battlefield, but from above their own heads.
Freya’s voice stayed calm.
"If you keep this fight going, we’ll attack the descendants of the Four Sacred Clans."
The entire arena froze. For a breath, nobody believed what they’d just heard.
Then the sacred clan platforms erupted.
"What did she just say?"
"She dares threaten us?"
"She wants to attack sacred clan descendants?"
"Who are these people?"
"Are they out of their minds?"

The younger descendants of Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest looked up in shock and anger. The elders’ faces darkened instantly. The clan heads, already shaken by Max injuring the Evercrest patriarch, grew furious.

The Four Sacred Clans had stood at the top of humanity for countless ages. Even supreme forces treated them with caution. Yet now a woman had shown up with thousands of people and openly threatened their descendants right inside the First Progenitor Arena.
The Ashbourne ancestor’s battle aura exploded. "How bold."
The crimson-black sky behind him shook, as if an ancient battlefield had come back to life. "You dare threaten the bloodlines of the Four Sacred Clans?"
Freya looked at him without fear. "Yes."
The answer came so direct that the air around them turned even colder.
The Evercrest ancestor’s spatial roots twisted violently. "You think surrounding the arena gives you leverage?"
Freya’s eyes stayed calm. "It does actually."
The Ravenhart ancestor’s shadow spread across the air. "If you attack them, none of you will leave here alive."
Freya replied, "If Max gets sealed, none of them will live long enough to care whether we leave or not."

chapters.title: Chapter 1972: Secret of the Four Sacred Clans!
paragraphs: A deadly silence fell over everything. The descendants of the Four Sacred Clans suddenly felt the full weight of the situation. This wasn’t an empty threat. Freya’s people had already positioned themselves above every major platform.
Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest each had crowds of younger descendants gathered to watch the Bloodline Legacy Battle.

The Four Sacred Clan ancestors were powerful, terrifyingly powerful, but their descendants weren’t invincible. If thousands of Voidwalker fighters struck at once from prepared positions, even a moment’s hesitation could turn into a massacre.
The four ancestors’ faces turned unbelievably dark. No one had dared threaten them like this in countless years.
Then the Valerius ancestor’s expression changed. His eyes fixed on Freya. The sacred light around him flickered slightly, as if he’d sensed something.
The Ashbourne ancestor narrowed his eyes too. His battle aura, which had been raging wildly, suddenly sharpened into focus.
The Ravenhart ancestor’s veil moved without any wind.
The Evercrest ancestor stared at Freya with disbelief and anger.
"She carries it too."
The Valerius ancestor’s voice turned colder. "Voidwalker bloodline."
Those words spread across the arena again. The sacred clan descendants looked up at Freya in shock.
Freya stood calmly in the sky, surrounded by thousands of her people, and the star-like dimensional light around her made the abandoned fifth end pulse even stronger.

Unlike Max, whose Voidwalker connection had stayed hidden beneath layers of other bloodlines and legacies, Freya’s presence carried that bloodline out in the open. It felt cold, deep, and wrapped in the quiet authority of distance, space, and hidden worlds.
The Ashbourne ancestor’s killing intent grew heavier. "How many of you got away?"
The Ravenhart ancestor whispered, "How many of these traitors weren’t sealed last time?"
The Evercrest ancestor’s eyes turned vicious. "So the Voidwalker remnants have been hiding this whole time."
Freya looked at them with cold eyes. "Some of us managed to survive."
The word was simple. But it hit the four ancestors like a slap.

The Voidwalker Ancestor, still standing in front of Max, looked up at Freya. For the first time since he’d appeared, his expression shifted more visibly. He stared at her for a long moment, and something like sorrow and relief passed through his old eyes.
"You two must be his son and daughter," he said softly.
Freya lowered her gaze toward him. "Ancestor."
That one word confirmed everything.

The whole arena stirred again. The black dragon at the center of the battlefield was a descendant of the Voidwalker Clan. The woman in the sky was also a descendant of the Voidwalker Clan. The thousands surrounding the arena were likely Voidwalker remnants as well.

The fifth sacred end, which everyone had believed abandoned forever, was waking up right in front of them. The Four Sacred Clans had tried to bury this bloodline, but it had come back, and everyone was watching it happen.

Max looked up at Freya, his happiness now tangled with a flood of questions. He wanted to ask where she’d been all this time, how she’d survived, how many Voidwalkers were left, why she’d never told him the truth, and what had actually happened between the Voidwalker Clan and the Four Sacred Clans.
But this wasn’t the time.
Freya seemed to know that too. Her gaze stayed on the Voidwalker Ancestor.
"Ancestor," she said, her voice carrying across the arena, "it’s time."
The Voidwalker Ancestor didn’t answer right away.

Freya continued, "For many years, the Four Sacred Clans have called us traitors. They sealed our people, abandoned our sacred end, erased our name, and taught their descendants that Voidwalker blood is a sin. Today, Max was nearly imprisoned without even being told what crime he was supposed to have committed."
Her eyes swept across the four ancestors. "They keep talking about stolen legacy. They keep talking about betrayal. They keep talking about ancient judgment. But they never explain the actual truth."
The Valerius ancestor’s face turned stern. "Some truths should stay sealed."
Freya looked at him. "No." Her voice turned colder. "Not anymore."

The thousands of Voidwalker descendants above the arena released their auras all at once. Their power didn’t attack yet, but it pressed downward, reminding everyone that Freya’s threat still stood. If the Four Sacred Clan ancestors chose to fight, the younger descendants below them would be the first to pay for it.
Freya turned back to the Voidwalker Ancestor. "Tell the truth."
The whole arena went silent.

Rose stood below, surrounded by Evercrest elders, staring up at Freya with wide eyes. Angelina Valerius stayed motionless at the edge of the battlefield, her expression heavy with thought. Cassian Valerius, Draven Ashbourne, Seraphine Ravenhart, and the other sacred clan geniuses looked between Freya, Max, the Voidwalker Ancestor, and their own ancestors, realizing that the Bloodline Legacy Battle had turned into something far bigger than any of them had expected.
Max’s massive dragon body stayed still, his eyes fixed on the Voidwalker Ancestor.
Freya’s voice rang out again, calm but impossible to ignore.
"Tell everyone what the Voidwalker Clan actually did. Tell them why we were called traitors. Tell them what legacy was supposedly stolen. Tell them what really happened to the fifth sacred clan."
The Voidwalker Ancestor slowly closed his eyes. For a long moment, he said nothing.

The glowing statue of the First Progenitor stood behind the arena, its closed eyes shining like stars trapped in stone. The abandoned fifth end burned with dark light. The Four Sacred Clan ancestors stayed silent, furious and unwilling, but unable to act recklessly with their descendants surrounded.
At last, the Voidwalker Ancestor opened his eyes. He looked at the four ancestors. Then at Freya. Then at Max.
The old man’s voice came out quiet.
"Very well."
The whole arena held its breath.
"Then let the buried truth return."
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s expression became solemn.
"It is time everyone knows the history of the sacred clans."
He looked across the arena.
"Or should I say, the history of the Five Sacred Clans."
The whole arena went still.
Above, Freya lowered her gaze in silence.
Below, Max’s enormous dragon body remained unmoving, his heart pounding with questions that were finally about to receive answers.

If the Four Sacred Clan ancestors chose to fight, the younger descendants below them would be the first to pay for it.
Freya turned back to the Voidwalker Ancestor.
"Tell the truth."
The whole arena went silent.
Rose stood below, surrounded by Evercrest elders, staring up at Freya with wide eyes.
Angelina Valerius stayed motionless at the edge of the battlefield, her expression heavy with thought.

Cassian Valerius, Draven Ashbourne, Seraphine Ravenhart, and the other sacred clan geniuses looked between Freya, Max, the Voidwalker Ancestor, and their own ancestors, realizing that the Bloodline Legacy Battle had turned into something far bigger than any of them had expected.
Max’s massive dragon body stayed still, his eyes fixed on the Voidwalker Ancestor.
Freya’s voice rang out again, calm but impossible to ignore.
"Tell everyone what the Voidwalker Clan actually did.
Tell them why we were called traitors.
Tell them what legacy was supposedly stolen.
Tell them what really happened to the fifth sacred clan."
The Voidwalker Ancestor slowly closed his eyes.
For a long moment, he said nothing.
The glowing statue of the First Progenitor stood behind the arena, its closed eyes shining like stars trapped in stone.
The abandoned fifth end burned with dark light.
The Four Sacred Clan ancestors stayed silent, furious and unwilling, but unable to act recklessly with their descendants surrounded.
At last, the Voidwalker Ancestor opened his eyes.
He looked at the four ancestors.
Then at Freya.
Then at Max.
The old man’s voice came out quiet.
"Very well."
The whole arena held its breath.
"Then let the buried truth return."
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s expression became solemn.
"It is time everyone knows the history of the sacred clans."
He looked across the arena.
"Or should I say, the history of the Five Sacred Clans."
The whole arena went still.
Above, Freya lowered her gaze in silence.
Below, Max’s enormous dragon body remained unmoving, his heart pounding with questions that were finally about to receive answers.

chapters.title: Chapter 1973: History of the Four Sacred Clans - 1
paragraphs: The Voidwalker Ancestor stood above the awakened fifth end for a long moment before speaking again.

The entire Bloodline Legacy Battle arena stayed silent. The thousands of Voidwalker descendants in the sky held their formation, surrounding the arena like a dark starry net. Freya stood at the front of them with her silver-white hair moving in the wind, her gaze cold and steady.

The four sacred ancestors had already pulled back their pressure, while the four current clan leaders stood below them with ugly expressions, unable to accept that the truth they’d worked so hard to bury was about to come out in front of the whole younger generation.
Max stayed in his true dragon form at the center of the ruined battlefield. His enormous black-gold body had gone quiet, but the chaotic flames between his scales hadn’t fully died down.
He watched the old man closely, his mind racing with thoughts.

The Four Sacred Clans had called him a descendant of traitors. They’d accused him of carrying the stolen legacy. They’d tried to imprison him without ever explaining why. Now, finally, he was about to understand why Freya had once warned him never to reveal the name Voidwalker.
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked toward the statue of the First Progenitor.
"Before the Four Sacred Clans existed," he said slowly, "there were the Five Sacred Clans."

His voice wasn’t loud, but it reached every corner of the arena. The younger descendants of Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest listened with tense faces. Some of them had already guessed as much from what had just happened, but hearing the Voidwalker Ancestor say it outright still shook them.

The official history they’d grown up learning only spoke of four sacred bloodlines descending from the First Progenitor. The fifth had been erased so completely that even mentioning it felt like trespassing on forbidden ground.

The Voidwalker Ancestor raised his hand slightly. The starry screen behind him brightened, and ancient images began to appear across it. There stood a younger First Progenitor Arena, whole, undivided, and unscarred by abandonment.

Five platforms surrounded the statue. Valerius shone with sacred white-gold light. Ashbourne burned with crimson-black battle force. Ravenhart stood beneath silent purple shadows. Evercrest bloomed with green-silver life-space radiance. And the fifth platform, the one now awake beneath the Voidwalker Ancestor, glowed with dark stars and silver dimensional rings.

"Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, Evercrest, and Voidwalker," the old man continued. "Those were the Five Sacred Clans born from the legacy of the First Progenitor. Each clan inherited a different branch of his forbidden bloodline, and each carried a different duty."
His gaze moved across the four clan platforms.

"Valerius guarded the sacred flame and the judgment of light. Ashbourne guarded the martial body and the blood-iron battlefield. Ravenhart guarded shadows, prophecy fragments, and the silence of the soul. Evercrest guarded life, space, and sealed domains."
Then his gaze returned to the fifth end.
"And Voidwalker guarded distance, hidden worlds, dimensional passage, and the deepest seal placed around the sacred legacy itself."
Those words changed a lot of expressions in the crowd.

The Voidwalker Ancestor went on. "The sacred legacy of the First Progenitor wasn’t a simple inheritance technique. It wasn’t a martial art anyone could learn through effort. It was the deepest thing he left behind, the core inheritance holding the reason the five sacred bloodlines existed and the secret of what our ancestor truly carried."
The four sacred ancestors lowered their eyes slightly. The clan leaders’ faces turned even uglier. The young geniuses of the Four Sacred Clans stared at the starry screen, unable to look away.

The Voidwalker Ancestor’s voice grew heavier. "Since ancient times, the duty of the Five Sacred Clans was to protect that sacred legacy. None of us owned it. None of us had the right to use it however we wanted. None of us could force it open. The five clans were only guardians, waiting for the day the sacred legacy would choose an inheritor on its own."

On the starry screen, the five ancient clans could be seen kneeling before the First Progenitor’s statue, their bloodline marks glowing as they formed a vast seal around a dark, mysterious light hidden beneath the arena.

"For countless years, the sacred legacy stayed silent," the Voidwalker Ancestor said. "Generation after generation guarded it. Ancestors rose and fell. Heirs were born and died. Wars came and went. The clans changed leaders again and again, yet the sacred legacy never once chose anyone."
His old eyes narrowed slightly.
"Then, one day, everything changed."

The image on the starry screen trembled. The peaceful arena from ancient times turned darker. Beneath the statue of the First Progenitor, the sealed sacred legacy suddenly pulsed. Its light wasn’t ordinary. It looked like a folded universe, a starry abyss, and a hidden world all rolled into one.
The moment it moved, the five platforms shook, and the Voidwalker platform reacted more violently than the rest.
The descendants in the current arena held their breath.

The Voidwalker Ancestor said, "According to the history written by the other four clans, the Voidwalker Clan betrayed the sacred pact. We stole the sacred legacy of the First Progenitor, the very thing we’d sworn to protect with our lives, and fled from the Five Sacred Clans."

The Valerius platform fell silent. The Ashbourne descendants clenched their fists. The Ravenhart geniuses traded shocked looks. The Evercrest descendants looked unsettled. This was the version most of them had heard before, though never spelled out so directly.
The Voidwalker Ancestor didn’t deny the story right away. He only looked at the starry screen.
"That’s what they saw."

The image changed. Several members of the ancient Voidwalker Clan stood before the sealed sacred legacy, their eyes glowing with a strange starry light. Their faces looked dazed, pained, and reverent all at once. They didn’t look like thieves who’d come for greed. They looked like people being pulled along by a voice no one else could hear.
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s voice went quiet.
"But it wasn’t that simple."
The whole arena leaned into the silence.
"It wasn’t the Voidwalker Clan that first chose to steal the sacred legacy," he said. "It was the sacred legacy that chose to move."

chapters.title: Chapter 1974: History of the Four Sacred Clans - 2
paragraphs: A wave of shock rolled through the arena.
"What?"
"The sacred legacy moved on its own?"
"How is that even possible?"
"Wasn’t it just an inheritance?"

The young geniuses of the Four Sacred Clans looked the most shaken. Cassian Valerius opened his eyes fully, his sacred solar aura unstable for the first time. Draven Ashbourne frowned deeply, his usual battle hunger replaced by solemn confusion. Seraphine Ravenhart’s silver-purple eyes shone with a strange light, as if the truth itself had disturbed the shadows around her. Aelric Evercrest, still injured and humiliated from his loss to Max, stared at the screen with a pale face.

The Voidwalker Ancestor continued, "For countless years, we protected the sacred legacy, yet it never once chose an inheritor. But in that era, for reasons even I never understood, the sacred legacy suddenly responded to the Voidwalker bloodline."
The starry screen showed several Voidwalker elders clutching their heads as the legacy’s light poured into their bodies.
"It didn’t just resonate with them. It influenced them. It called to them. It possessed them."
The four sacred clan platforms erupted in disbelief.
The Valerius leader’s face twisted. "Nonsense."
The Voidwalker Ancestor ignored him.

"Some members of the Voidwalker Clan were affected lightly. They heard whispers. They had dreams. They saw hidden doors in their bloodline. But others were pulled in much deeper. They started believing the sacred legacy didn’t belong under the Five Sacred Clans anymore. They believed it had chosen Voidwalker, and that if they didn’t take it, the chance would vanish forever."

On the screen, the ancient Voidwalker members moved under the legacy’s influence. They broke through several layers of the seal their own clan had helped maintain. Other Voidwalker members tried to stop them, but the sacred legacy’s light warped space and turned the entire platform into a maze of folded worlds.
The old man’s voice grew heavier.
"In the end, a group of Voidwalker clan members took the sacred legacy and fled."

The arena buzzed with murmurs. The image showed the five ancient platforms erupting into chaos. Valerius sacred fire rose into the sky. Ashbourne battle aura split the ground. Ravenhart shadows tried to trace the escape path.

Evercrest space roots sealed off countless directions. The Voidwalker platform tore itself apart as some Voidwalkers chased the thieves, some protected their clan members, and some just stood frozen in disbelief.

"The five clans were shocked," the Voidwalker Ancestor said. "The other four clans watched the sacred legacy vanish in the hands of Voidwalker members. They watched the very guardians closest to the seal break it. They watched the fifth clan become the path through which the legacy disappeared."
His eyes lowered faintly.
"At that time, even I believed the fault belonged to my own clan members."
Those words stunned everyone all over again.
Max’s dragon eyes narrowed slightly. The Voidwalker Ancestor wasn’t hiding his own past mistake.

"I believed those who took the legacy had betrayed the sacred pact. I believed they’d been overcome by greed, ambition, and bloodline pride. I believed the Voidwalker Clan had failed in its duty, and that our failure had nearly torn apart the Five Sacred Clans."

The starry screen showed battles breaking out across ancient domains. Voidwalkers got seized, sealed, hunted, interrogated, and imprisoned. Some resisted. Some surrendered. Some tried to explain that the legacy had called to them. Few people believed them.
"That belief," the old man said, "is what led to the imprisonment and sealing of the Voidwalker Clan."
Freya’s expression turned colder up in the sky. The thousands of Voidwalker descendants behind her let out a faint wave of restrained fury.

The old man continued, "I agreed to be sealed because I thought my clan had committed an unforgivable failure. I thought that if I resisted, the five clans would collapse completely. I thought accepting the seal would preserve the inheritance, protect the remaining bloodlines, and stop an all-out war."
His voice dropped even quieter.
"But time turned out to be a cruel teacher."
The starry screen faded a bit, leaving only the glow of the sacred legacy.

"Slowly, over the long years of being sealed, I started to think. I started to recall the faces of those who’d taken the sacred legacy. I remembered their eyes. Their fear. Their madness. Their devotion. Their pain. I remembered the way the sacred legacy moved before they ever did."
His eyes sharpened.
"And eventually, I began to wonder whether the real fault belonged not to my clan members, but to the sacred legacy itself."
A heavy silence spread. This time, even the four sacred ancestors didn’t rush to respond.

The younger geniuses of the Four Sacred Clans looked completely stunned. This wasn’t the history they’d been taught. They’d been told the Voidwalker Clan betrayed the First Progenitor and stole the sacred legacy. They’d been told the fifth clan was sealed because of greed.

They’d been told the four clans protected the world from traitors. Nobody had told them the sacred legacy might have influenced the Voidwalker Clan first. Nobody had told them the Voidwalker Ancestor himself once believed in the punishment. Nobody had told them the whole tragedy might have started because the sacred legacy wanted something.
Rose stared at the old man in disbelief.
Angelina Valerius stood silently, her eyes deep in thought.
Freya didn’t look surprised. Maybe she’d already known part of it. Maybe she’d carried this weight for a long time.

Max, though, was thinking about something else. The Dimensional Keeper legacy. The starry fist. The sealed worlds inside his body. The way the abandoned Voidwalker end had reacted to him. The way the First Progenitor’s statue had glowed. The way everyone kept repeating the words stolen sacred legacy.
A thought took shape in his mind.
’Could the Dimensional Keeper legacy be the sacred legacy of the First Progenitor?’
His dragon head lowered slightly as he looked at the Voidwalker Ancestor.
"What happened to the sacred legacy?"
His voice came out deep and heavy in his dragon form, rumbling across the arena. Everyone turned toward him. The question sounded simple, but it carried a thought many others hadn’t dared to voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 1975: The Lost Legacy!
paragraphs: The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at Max for a moment. Then he shrugged lightly. For such a solemn moment, the gesture felt strangely casual.
"It was lost."
The arena froze.
Max’s eyes narrowed. "Lost?"

The Voidwalker Ancestor nodded. "Since the day those Voidwalker members took it, the sacred legacy of the First Progenitor never returned to the Five Sacred Clans. Those who fled disappeared. The legacy disappeared with them. Every trace of it became uncertain."
The Valerius leader immediately shouted, unable to hold back. "Lies! The sacred legacy isn’t lost. It’s standing right in front of us!"
His furious gaze locked onto Max.

The Ashbourne leader jumped in right after. "Max Voidwalker carries it. That star-like dimensional power, the awakening of the fifth end, the way the First Progenitor’s statue reacted, all of it proves he’s inherited the stolen sacred legacy."
The Ravenhart leader’s eyes flashed. "The Voidwalker bloodline has been hiding it all these years."

The Evercrest leader, still pale from his injuries, pointed at Max with a trembling, furious hand. "That’s why the abandoned end reacted. That’s why our bloodlines got suppressed. That’s why the statue lit up. Max Voidwalker has the sacred legacy."
Several elders from the Four Sacred Clans started shouting too.
"He has to be sealed!"
"The legacy has to be recovered!"
"The Voidwalker Clan has been hiding it this whole time!"
"They came back because the sacred legacy found a new vessel!"
The mood surged back toward chaos. Freya’s eyes turned cold, and the thousands of Voidwalker descendants above the arena immediately tightened their formation.
Max’s dragon eyes narrowed dangerously.
But before things could explode, the Voidwalker Ancestor raised his hand.
"Wrong."
His voice stayed calm. But it cut through every accusation at once.
The Four Sacred Clan leaders glared at him.
The Valerius leader said coldly, "You still want to deny it?"
The Voidwalker Ancestor shook his head. "If Max carried the true sacred legacy of the First Progenitor, the statue would have lit up the second he entered the domain of the Four Sacred Clans."
The arena quieted down a bit.

The Voidwalker Ancestor continued, "He entered Evercrest territory earlier. He passed through the outer spatial layers. He stood in front of the statue. He walked into the Bloodline Legacy Battle arena. The statue reacted faintly, yes, but it didn’t fully wake up. The fifth end didn’t light up. The bloodlines of the Four Sacred Clans weren’t fully suppressed."

Max remembered that moment clearly. When he’d first seen the First Progenitor’s statue, his blood had reacted violently, but the statue itself had stayed silent. He’d hidden that reaction from Rose, and nothing more happened until he used the star-like fist formed by the Dimensional Keeper legacy.
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at the glowing statue.

"The true sacred legacy was bound too deeply to the First Progenitor’s statue and the five-clan arena. If it had come back in its real form, this place would have known instantly. The statue would have woken up before Max even stepped onto the battlefield. All five ends would have reacted together. The old seal would have opened on its own without him needing to strike the ground."
The four sacred ancestors stayed silent. None of them denied it. That silence made a lot of elders and descendants uneasy.
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s gaze returned to Max.

"What Max carries is indeed oddly similar to the sacred legacy of the First Progenitor. The dimensional resonance, the sealed-world feel, the way it suppresses the five bloodline branches, and the way it can wake the forgotten end are all too close to ignore."
Max listened carefully. The old man’s expression grew more serious.
"But it isn’t the true sacred legacy."
The whole arena held its breath.
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at the starry traces flickering around Max’s massive dragon body.

"What he carries is different. Older in feeling, but not necessarily older in time. Higher in structure, but not something I can fully pin down. It resembles the sacred legacy, yet it isn’t bound by the First Progenitor’s seal. It answers to the Voidwalker bloodline, but it doesn’t belong only to the Voidwalker Clan. It can touch the statue, but it isn’t controlled by it."
His eyes narrowed faintly.
"And when it woke up through his fist, I felt something even the sacred legacy never once gave me."
Max’s heart stirred.
The Voidwalker Ancestor said slowly, "Whatever Max carries isn’t the stolen sacred legacy of the First Progenitor."
The old man paused. Then his voice dropped lower and heavier.
"It’s something beyond it."
A wave of shock ran through the arena. Even the four sacred ancestors’ expressions shifted.
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at Max with eyes full of confusion, caution, and a trace of awe.
"Something even I can’t understand."
Max frowned.
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s final words echoed through the arena like a stone dropped into a bottomless well.
Something beyond the sacred legacy. Something even he couldn’t understand. Those words should have cleared things up, but instead they only made everything more confusing.

Max’s enormous dragon body stayed still at the center of the shattered battlefield, but his mind kept racing. From the moment he’d entered the hidden domain of the Four Sacred Clans, he’d felt something off.

When he first saw the statue of the First Progenitor, his blood had reacted violently. When Aelric awakened the Evercrest forbidden bloodline, Max’s foundation had stirred again. When he gathered the power of the Dimensional Keeper legacy into his fist and struck the ground, the statue had glowed, the abandoned fifth end had woken up, and the bloodlines of the Four Sacred Clans had been suppressed.

All of it pointed in one direction. His Dimensional Keeper legacy was connected to this place. It was connected to the Four Sacred Clans. It was connected to the Voidwalker Clan. It was connected to the First Progenitor’s statue.
Yet now the Voidwalker Ancestor, the very ancestor of the clan that had guarded the sacred legacy most closely, was saying that what Max carried wasn’t the true sacred legacy of the First Progenitor.
Max’s dragon eyes narrowed. ’Maybe it wasn’t the Dimensional Keeper legacy reacting; maybe it was my Voidwalker Bloodline reacting to them...’

sentences.text: The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at Max for a moment.
Then he shrugged lightly.
For such a solemn moment, the gesture felt strangely casual.
"It was lost."
The arena froze.
Max’s eyes narrowed.
"Lost?"
The Voidwalker Ancestor nodded.
"Since the day those Voidwalker members took it, the sacred legacy of the First Progenitor never returned to the Five Sacred Clans.
Those who fled disappeared.
The legacy disappeared with them.
Every trace of it became uncertain."
The Valerius leader immediately shouted, unable to hold back.
"Lies!
The sacred legacy isn’t lost.
It’s standing right in front of us!"
His furious gaze locked onto Max.
The Ashbourne leader jumped in right after.
"Max Voidwalker carries it.
That star-like dimensional power, the awakening of the fifth end, the way the First Progenitor’s statue reacted, all of it proves he’s inherited the stolen sacred legacy."
The Ravenhart leader’s eyes flashed.
"The Voidwalker bloodline has been hiding it all these years."
The Evercrest leader, still pale from his injuries, pointed at Max with a trembling, furious hand.
"That’s why the abandoned end reacted.
That’s why our bloodlines got suppressed.
That’s why the statue lit up.
Max Voidwalker has the sacred legacy."
Several elders from the Four Sacred Clans started shouting too.
"He has to be sealed!"
"The legacy has to be recovered!"
"The Voidwalker Clan has been hiding it this whole time!"
"They came back because the sacred legacy found a new vessel!"
The mood surged back toward chaos.
Freya’s eyes turned cold, and the thousands of Voidwalker descendants above the arena immediately tightened their formation.
Max’s dragon eyes narrowed dangerously.
But before things could explode, the Voidwalker Ancestor raised his hand.
"Wrong."
His voice stayed calm.
But it cut through every accusation at once.
The Four Sacred Clan leaders glared at him.
The Valerius leader said coldly, "You still want to deny it?"
The Voidwalker Ancestor shook his head.
"If Max carried the true sacred legacy of the First Progenitor, the statue would have lit up the second he entered the domain of the Four Sacred Clans."
The arena quieted down a bit.
The Voidwalker Ancestor continued, "He entered Evercrest territory earlier.
He passed through the outer spatial layers.
He stood in front of the statue.
He walked into the Bloodline Legacy Battle arena.
The statue reacted faintly, yes, but it didn’t fully wake up.
The fifth end didn’t light up.
The bloodlines of the Four Sacred Clans weren’t fully suppressed."
Max remembered that moment clearly.
When he’d first seen the First Progenitor’s statue, his blood had reacted violently, but the statue itself had stayed silent.
He’d hidden that reaction from Rose, and nothing more happened until he used the star-like fist formed by the Dimensional Keeper legacy.
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at the glowing statue.
"The true sacred legacy was bound too deeply to the First Progenitor’s statue and the five-clan arena.
If it had come back in its real form, this place would have known instantly.
The statue would have woken up before Max even stepped onto the battlefield.
All five ends would have reacted together.
The old seal would have opened on its own without him needing to strike the ground."
The four sacred ancestors stayed silent.
None of them denied it.
That silence made a lot of elders and descendants uneasy.
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s gaze returned to Max.
"What Max carries is indeed oddly similar to the sacred legacy of the First Progenitor.
The dimensional resonance, the sealed-world feel, the way it suppresses the five bloodline branches, and the way it can wake the forgotten end are all too close to ignore."
Max listened carefully.
The old man’s expression grew more serious.
"But it isn’t the true sacred legacy."
The whole arena held its breath.
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at the starry traces flickering around Max’s massive dragon body.
"What he carries is different.
Older in feeling, but not necessarily older in time.
Higher in structure, but not something I can fully pin down.
It resembles the sacred legacy, yet it isn’t bound by the First Progenitor’s seal.
It answers to the Voidwalker bloodline, but it doesn’t belong only to the Voidwalker Clan.
It can touch the statue, but it isn’t controlled by it."
His eyes narrowed faintly.
"And when it woke up through his fist, I felt something even the sacred legacy never once gave me."
Max’s heart stirred.
The Voidwalker Ancestor said slowly, "Whatever Max carries isn’t the stolen sacred legacy of the First Progenitor."
The old man paused.
Then his voice dropped lower and heavier.
"It’s something beyond it."
A wave of shock ran through the arena.
Even the four sacred ancestors’ expressions shifted.
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at Max with eyes full of confusion, caution, and a trace of awe.
"Something even I can’t understand."
Max frowned.
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s final words echoed through the arena like a stone dropped into a bottomless well.
Something beyond the sacred legacy.
Something even he couldn’t understand.
Those words should have cleared things up, but instead they only made everything more confusing.
Max’s enormous dragon body stayed still at the center of the shattered battlefield, but his mind kept racing.
From the moment he’d entered the hidden domain of the Four Sacred Clans, he’d felt something off.
When he first saw the statue of the First Progenitor, his blood had reacted violently.
When Aelric awakened the Evercrest forbidden bloodline, Max’s foundation had stirred again.

chapters.title: Chapter 1976: Who was the First Progenitor?!
paragraphs: The Dimensional Keeper legacy had always felt strange. It wasn’t like his Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline. It wasn’t like his Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline. It wasn’t even like his Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline.

Those powers had sources, traits, and growth paths he could at least make sense of. The Dimensional Keeper legacy was different. It felt vast, ancient, and hidden in a way that went beyond ordinary inheritance.
Back then, he’d just assumed the legacy was powerful beyond his current level. Now he wasn’t so sure.

He looked toward the statue of the First Progenitor. It still glowed. Its eyes stayed closed, but the star-like light running through its stone body made it look less like a lifeless sculpture and more like a sleeping presence that had noticed him. That reaction made Max uneasy. Not because it felt hostile, but because it felt too familiar, like the statue was waiting for something from him.

’The true sacred legacy was lost after those Voidwalker members ran off with it,’ Max thought. ’But why did the legacy choose the Voidwalker Clan in the first place? Why did it possess them? Why did it leave the five clans? And if what I carry isn’t that legacy, why does it feel so similar?’
His thoughts dug deeper. What was the sacred legacy even about?

The Voidwalker Ancestor had said it wasn’t a simple martial art or inheritance technique. It was the deepest thing the First Progenitor had left behind, the core inheritance holding the reason the five sacred bloodlines existed and the secret of what the First Progenitor truly carried.
That sentence bothered Max the most. The reason the five sacred bloodlines existed. The secret of what the First Progenitor truly carried.
Max slowly lifted his dragon head and looked at the glowing stone figure towering over the arena.
Who was the First Progenitor?

Rose had told him the Four Sacred Clans didn’t descend from Primordials like ordinary humans. They descended from the First Progenitor. Their forbidden bloodlines came from him. The Four Sacred Clans, or really the Five Sacred Clans, could rival Primordials despite lacking Primordial Race bloodline because they carried that forbidden source instead.

But what kind of man could stand outside the Primordial origin of humanity? If humans came from Primordials who’d given up their bloodline to become mortal and have children, where did the First Progenitor fit into that history?
Was he a Primordial? Was he something beyond the Primordials? Was he the first true human? Or was he something else entirely?

Max felt the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline inside him stir faintly as he turned the question over. The bloodline he’d gotten from the Primarchs made him closer to the laws of the world and multiplied his strength tenfold, but standing in front of the First Progenitor’s statue, even that Primarch-level bloodline had reacted. It hadn’t rejected the statue, but it hadn’t fully submitted either. It had trembled, pulsed, and seemed to acknowledge that the figure before it wasn’t simple.
The more Max thought about it, the heavier his heart grew.
’Even the Primordials might not know the full truth about this man.’

The arena stayed silent around him. The young geniuses of the Four Sacred Clans were still frozen in shock after hearing the Voidwalker Ancestor’s explanation. Cassian Valerius sat with his brows tightly furrowed, no longer carrying the calm pride of the Sun-Crowned Heir.

Draven Ashbourne’s fists stayed clenched, but for once there was no battle hunger on his face, only rare seriousness. Seraphine Ravenhart’s silver-purple eyes looked distant, as if she were digging through fragments of fate and memory for something her clan had never let her see.
Aelric Evercrest’s face stayed pale, his loss to Max now almost forgotten next to the collapse of the history he’d believed his whole life.

Rose stayed quiet too. She looked at the Evercrest elders around her, then at the Voidwalker Ancestor, then at Max’s huge dragon body. She’d grown up cast aside by the Evercrest Clan for being born without the forbidden bloodline, but now she realized the sacred clans’ cruelty wasn’t simply personal.
Their entire history had been built on selective memory, fear, and punishment that could stretch across countless generations.
Freya stayed in the sky, watching Max. Her expression was calm, but Max could feel the emotion underneath it. She’d known more than him.

Maybe she’d carried this weight for years. Maybe she’d wanted to tell him and couldn’t. Maybe she’d warned him not to reveal the Voidwalker name because she knew exactly what would happen if the Four Sacred Clans recognized him.
Max wanted to ask her everything. But first, he needed to understand the core of this mystery.

His gaze went back to the Voidwalker Ancestor. The old man stood above the awakened fifth end, still looking at Max with a complicated expression. There was relief in his eyes, but also uncertainty. He clearly knew a lot about the Voidwalker Clan and the sacred legacy, yet even he didn’t fully understand the power Max carried.
Max spoke slowly. His dragon voice rumbled across the arena, deep and heavy.
"If what I carry isn’t the sacred legacy, then what happened to the real sacred legacy after it disappeared?"
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s gaze shifted slightly.

Max continued, "You said those Voidwalker members were influenced by it. You said they stole it and fled. You said it was lost after that. But something like that shouldn’t just vanish forever. If it was powerful enough to possess members of your clan and make them break the seal of the Five Sacred Clans, it must have had a purpose."
The old man didn’t answer right away.
Max’s eyes moved back to the statue.

"And what exactly is the sacred legacy? What did the First Progenitor leave behind that made the Five Sacred Clans guard it for countless years? What did it choose those Voidwalkers for? What did it actually want?"
His voice dropped lower.
"And who was the First Progenitor?"

That final question hit the arena harder than all the rest. The younger descendants immediately looked toward the statue. To them, the First Progenitor had always been a sacred figure, the origin of their clans, the source of their forbidden bloodlines, and the ancestor whose name stood above everything else.
But because he was so sacred, nobody ever questioned him. They worshiped him. They inherited from him. They carried his bloodline branches. But how many of them actually knew who he really was?

The four sacred ancestors grew visibly tense. The Valerius ancestor’s sacred light flickered. The Ashbourne ancestor lowered his gaze. The Ravenhart ancestor’s shadow went still. The Evercrest ancestor looked at the statue with an expression carrying both reverence and fear.
Their reactions told Max one thing clearly. They knew something. Maybe not everything, but enough to make them afraid of the question.

chapters.title: Chapter 1977: A Way To Find The Truth!
paragraphs: The Voidwalker Ancestor sighed softly.
"Those are the same questions I asked myself after being sealed."
His voice came out quieter than before.

"At first, I thought the sacred legacy was simply an inheritance the First Progenitor left behind for one chosen descendant. I thought it held a supreme path, a forbidden technique, or maybe the complete source of the five bloodline branches. That’s what all five clans believed. We protected it because our ancestors told us to. We feared it because our bloodlines feared it. We worshiped it because it came from him."
The old man looked up at the glowing statue.
"But after the legacy moved on its own, after it influenced members of my clan and disappeared, I started to question whether we’d ever really understood it at all."
A cold silence spread through the arena.

The Voidwalker Ancestor continued, "The sacred legacy may not have been waiting for an inheritor the way we believed. It may have been waiting for a condition. A moment. A bloodline resonance. Or maybe a door that only the Voidwalker branch could open."
Max’s heart stirred. A door.
The old man noticed the reaction, and his eyes deepened.

"That’s why I said what you carry is similar. The sacred legacy also gave me the feeling of hidden worlds, sealed dimensions, and doors beyond ordinary law. But yours is different. The sacred legacy was tied to the First Progenitor. It was anchored here. It belonged to the origin of the Five Sacred Clans."
He paused.
"What you carry feels like something that can touch that origin, but isn’t limited by it."
Max frowned even more. That answer didn’t solve the mystery. It only made it bigger.
The Valerius leader suddenly spoke up, unable to hold back. "This is absurd. You’re trying to protect him by making his legacy sound different."
The Ashbourne leader followed coldly, "Whether it’s the original sacred legacy or something beyond it, it’s connected to the stolen inheritance. That alone makes him dangerous."
The Evercrest leader’s eyes burned with anger. "Max Voidwalker woke up the abandoned end and suppressed our bloodlines. You expect us to believe this has nothing to do with the sacred legacy?"
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at them with mild annoyance.
"I didn’t say it has nothing to do with the sacred legacy."
The leaders fell silent.
The old man continued, "I said it isn’t the sacred legacy."
Freya’s voice came down from the sky. "There’s a difference."
The Ravenhart leader’s expression darkened, but she didn’t argue the point.

Max’s mind sharpened even further. Not the sacred legacy, but connected to it. Similar, but beyond it. Able to awaken the fifth end, but not recognized immediately by the statue. Able to suppress the Four Sacred Clan bloodlines, yet not controlled by the First Progenitor’s arena.

’Then maybe the Dimensional Keeper legacy isn’t something the First Progenitor left behind. That goddess told me an inheritor of the Dimensional Keeper legacy gets born every era, which in a way means it has nothing to do with the Five Sacred Clans,’ Max thought.
Max stared at the statue. For the first time, that calm stone face seemed to carry more mystery than majesty.
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s voice rang out again.

"I can’t tell you what happened to the true sacred legacy after it was taken. I only know it never came back to us. I can’t tell you its final purpose because I no longer believe any of the Five Sacred Clans ever truly understood it. As for the First Progenitor..."
The old man stopped. The entire arena held its breath. Even the four sacred ancestors looked at him with solemn expressions.
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s gaze turned distant.
"He wasn’t just the ancestor of the Five Sacred Clans."
The statue glowed brighter.
"He was the first being who carried the forbidden source that let us stand beside Primordials without being Primordials themselves."
Max’s eyes narrowed.
The old man looked at him.
"And if your legacy is truly beyond the sacred legacy he left behind, then Max Voidwalker, you may one day uncover something even the First Progenitor never managed to reveal."

The arena sank into a suffocating silence. Max looked at the glowing statue, the awakened fifth end, the four sacred ancestors, Freya in the sky, and the Voidwalker Ancestor standing beneath the dark star.

For the first time since this mystery began, he realized the truth about the Voidwalker Clan might only be the outer layer. The deeper secret wasn’t just what happened to the sacred legacy. It was what the sacred legacy had been connected to in the first place.
"Hmph, we’ll know once this kid touches the statue of the First Progenitor," the head of the Valerius Clan said.
His voice came out cold and full of distrust, but the moment he said it, several people in the arena fell into thought.

The Valerius ancestor, still standing in the dim glow of sacred white-gold light, narrowed his eyes and looked at the statue. After a brief silence, he nodded slowly. "That’s true. If Max Voidwalker really carries the Sacred Legacy of the Five Sacred Clans, the statue of the First Progenitor won’t stay silent once he touches it."

The Ashbourne ancestor crossed his arms, his crimson-black aura still rolling around him like a sleeping battlefield. "The sacred legacy came from the First Progenitor’s deepest source. It can’t hide from his statue. If the boy carries it, the statue will react in a way none of us can deny."

The Ravenhart ancestor’s shadow feathers drifted around her veil as her soft voice spread across the arena. "The statue already reacted to his star-like power, but that reaction was indirect. It woke up when he struck the arena and stirred the hidden formation beneath the fifth end. Touching the statue directly will be different. It’ll show whether his legacy actually belongs to the First Progenitor’s sacred inheritance or just resembles it."

The Evercrest ancestor looked at Max with cold eyes, his expression still ugly since the Evercrest patriarch had been badly hurt earlier. "If the statue confirms he carries the sacred legacy, then no excuse from the Voidwalker Clan will save him."

Freya’s eyes turned cold up above the arena. The thousands of Voidwalker descendants surrounding the Bloodline Legacy Battle arena let out a faint pressure at the same time, but Freya didn’t speak right away.

She just stared at the Evercrest ancestor as if memorizing his words. The threat she’d placed over the four clans’ descendants hadn’t gone anywhere. If they tried to use this test as an excuse to attack Max again, she wouldn’t hesitate.
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at the statue for a long while.

The enormous stone figure kept glowing faintly. Its closed eyes shone with a star-like light, and the lines across its body pulsed in rhythm with the awakened fifth end. It looked calm, majestic, and mysterious, as if it had been waiting through countless years for exactly this moment.
No one could say for sure whether the statue’s current reaction came from Max, the Voidwalker end, the Dimensional Keeper legacy, the starry fist, or the old history that had finally come to light.

The Valerius ancestor, still standing in the dim glow of sacred white-gold light, narrowed his eyes and looked at the statue.
After a brief silence, he nodded slowly.
"That’s true.
If Max Voidwalker really carries the Sacred Legacy of the Five Sacred Clans, the statue of the First Progenitor won’t stay silent once he touches it."
The Ashbourne ancestor crossed his arms, his crimson-black aura still rolling around him like a sleeping battlefield.
"The sacred legacy came from the First Progenitor’s deepest source.
It can’t hide from his statue.
If the boy carries it, the statue will react in a way none of us can deny."
The Ravenhart ancestor’s shadow feathers drifted around her veil as her soft voice spread across the arena.
"The statue already reacted to his star-like power, but that reaction was indirect.
It woke up when he struck the arena and stirred the hidden formation beneath the fifth end.
Touching the statue directly will be different.
It’ll show whether his legacy actually belongs to the First Progenitor’s sacred inheritance or just resembles it."
The Evercrest ancestor looked at Max with cold eyes, his expression still ugly since the Evercrest patriarch had been badly hurt earlier.
"If the statue confirms he carries the sacred legacy, then no excuse from the Voidwalker Clan will save him."
Freya’s eyes turned cold up above the arena.
The thousands of Voidwalker descendants surrounding the Bloodline Legacy Battle arena let out a faint pressure at the same time, but Freya didn’t speak right away.
She just stared at the Evercrest ancestor as if memorizing his words.
The threat she’d placed over the four clans’ descendants hadn’t gone anywhere.
If they tried to use this test as an excuse to attack Max again, she wouldn’t hesitate.
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at the statue for a long while.
The enormous stone figure kept glowing faintly.
Its closed eyes shone with a star-like light, and the lines across its body pulsed in rhythm with the awakened fifth end.
It looked calm, majestic, and mysterious, as if it had been waiting through countless years for exactly this moment.
No one could say for sure whether the statue’s current reaction came from Max, the Voidwalker end, the Dimensional Keeper legacy, the starry fist, or the old history that had finally come to light.

chapters.title: Chapter 1978: Touching The Statue!
paragraphs: The Voidwalker Ancestor nodded slowly.
"That method can confirm some things, yes."
His voice carried across the arena.

"If Max carries the true Sacred Legacy of the Five Sacred Clans, the statue of the First Progenitor will recognize it the moment he touches it directly. The sacred legacy and this statue were connected at their deepest roots. Even if the legacy changed hands, even if it hid for countless years, that connection wouldn’t just disappear."

Max listened quietly. His enormous black dragon body stayed at the center of the shattered arena. The chaotic flames between his scales had slowly dimmed, but his golden-black eyes were still sharp. He looked at the statue, then at the Voidwalker Ancestor, then up at Freya.

He was curious about the test. More than curious. This whole time, he’d been trying to make sense of the Dimensional Keeper legacy. It had saved him against Revona’s Null Origin Tide. It had resonated with the abandoned Voidwalker end.
It had woken up the First Progenitor Arena. It had suppressed the bloodlines of the Four Sacred Clans. Even the Voidwalker Ancestor said it resembled the sacred legacy without actually being it.
If touching the statue could hand him even one more clue, Max wanted to try it.
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at him.
"Go back to your human form first."
Max’s dragon eyes shifted slightly.

The old man explained, "The statue doesn’t just respond to power. It responds to bloodline, origin, and legacy. Your true dragon form is powerful, but it’s also wrapped heavily in the Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline. If you approach the First Progenitor’s statue like that, the reaction might get muddled. Let the statue sense your human foundation clearly."
Max understood. His massive dragon head lowered slightly.
"Fine."

The moment he said it, black-gold light began shrinking around his huge body. The transformation didn’t happen all at once. His wings folded first, turning into streams of chaotic black light that flowed back into his back.

His enormous claws pulled in, the sharp talons reshaping into fingers. The black-gold scales across his body dissolved one after another, sinking beneath his skin like fragments of night returning to blood. His long dragon body condensed, compressed, and reshaped itself under his control.
The pressure of the true dragon form faded. The enormous shadow covering the battlefield disappeared.

A few breaths later, Max stood in human form again at the center of the ruined arena. His white hair fell around his shoulders. His black robe was slightly torn from the earlier fighting, but his aura stayed calm and terrifyingly steady.

Faint traces of black-gold scales still flickered at the edges of his skin before vanishing completely. The five Divine Veins closed one by one, and the Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline settled back into silence.
The Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline also pulled back beneath his foundation, leaving only a faint ancient pulse that even the sacred ancestors couldn’t fully read.
Dragonheart appeared in his hand for a moment, then disappeared again.
He wasn’t here to fight now. He was here to test the truth.
Freya watched him from the sky, and for the first time since her arrival, a trace of worry crossed her eyes.
"Max," she said.
He looked up at her.
Her voice softened. "Be careful."
Max smiled faintly. It was a small smile, but it was real.
"I will."
For a moment, the tense mood of the arena seemed to shift. The younger geniuses of the Four Sacred Clans watched this exchange in silence.

Many of them had only known Max as the champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference, the terrifying outsider who’d beaten Aelric, injured an Evercrest clan head, turned into a huge black dragon, and dragged ancient history back into the light.
But now, watching Freya talk to him like that, they suddenly remembered that underneath all those impossible powers, Max was also someone’s little brother.
That thought made the whole situation feel stranger. More human. More dangerous.
The head of the Valerius Clan looked impatient. "Enough delays. Let him touch the statue."
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s gaze turned cold. "He’ll touch it because he chooses to. Not because you order him to."
The Valerius head’s expression darkened.
The Valerius ancestor raised a hand slightly, stopping him from saying more.
"Let the test proceed."
The four sacred ancestors stayed alert. Their auras didn’t press down on Max, but none of them relaxed either.

The four clan heads watched with heavy suspicion, while the elders of Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest formed protective barriers around their descendants. Above the arena, Freya’s Voidwalker forces stayed in formation, ready to act if the Four Sacred Clans tried anything.
Rose stood near the Evercrest platform, still surrounded by elders, though no one dared pressure her as harshly now. Too much had happened.

The Evercrest elders no longer knew how to treat her. She’d brought Max here as her representative, and that one decision had cracked open an ancient secret buried beneath the Four Sacred Clans themselves.
Angelina Valerius stood silently at the edge of the battlefield, looking at Max with a complicated expression. The Bloodline Legacy Battle had completely lost its original meaning.

This was no longer a contest between young geniuses fighting for legacy merit. It had turned into a trial of history, bloodline, and inheritance, with the statue of the First Progenitor about to sit in judgment.

Max started walking toward the statue. Each step echoed clearly across the arena. The shattered battlefield repaired itself faintly beneath his feet, not because the formation had fully healed, but because the First Progenitor Arena seemed to be clearing a path for him.

The light from the abandoned fifth end followed him quietly. The other four clan platforms trembled slightly as he passed, and the forbidden bloodlines inside many descendants stirred again, though not as violently as before.
Max’s own blood pulsed in response.

The closer he got to the statue, the more clearly he felt that strange connection. It wasn’t the same feeling as when he tapped into his Primordial Bloodline. It wasn’t the same as using the Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline. It wasn’t the same as the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline either. It felt deeper, stranger, and far harder to put into words.
The Dimensional Keeper legacy inside him stayed silent for now, but that silence felt deliberate, like a hidden beast watching another ancient existence from behind a closed door.

Max stopped in front of the statue. The First Progenitor towered above him. The stone face stayed calm, the eyes closed, the hand resting near its side. Up close, Max could feel the ancient pressure much more clearly. It didn’t crush him. It didn’t push him away. It just watched, even with its eyes still shut.
The entire arena held its breath.
The Valerius head said coldly, "Touch it."
Max ignored him. He looked up at the statue and narrowed his eyes slightly.
’If you really know something, then show me.’

Then he raised his hand. Slowly, under the eyes of the Five Sacred Clan descendants, the four sacred ancestors, the Voidwalker Ancestor, Freya, Rose, Angelina, and the countless elders gathered across the arena, Max placed his palm against the statue of the First Progenitor.
For one breath, nothing happened.
Then...

chapters.title: Chapter 1979: Meeting the First Progenitor!
paragraphs: For one breath, the whole arena seemed to stop with Max’s hand resting against the statue of the First Progenitor.

Then another breath passed. Nothing happened. The statue stayed still. The glowing lines that had appeared earlier across its stone body didn’t grow brighter. The closed eyes stayed shut. The enormous hand resting near its side didn’t move.

The ancient pressure around the statue didn’t shift in any obvious way. Even the awakened Voidwalker end, which had been pulsing with dark starry light, went strangely quiet, as if it too were waiting for a response that refused to show up.
Three seconds passed. Five seconds passed. Ten seconds passed.

The expressions of the Four Sacred Clan leaders began to shift. The head of the Valerius Clan narrowed his eyes, and a cold smile slowly crept onto his face. The Ashbourne head crossed his arms with a heavy snort.

The Ravenhart head looked thoughtful, while the Evercrest head’s pale, injured face showed a flash of unwillingness mixed with relief. If Max really carried the Sacred Legacy of the Five Sacred Clans, there should have been an undeniable reaction the moment he touched the statue directly.
The statue had once anchored the sacred legacy. No disguise, no bloodline concealment, and no Voidwalker trick should have been able to hide the legacy from it at this close range.
Yet nothing had happened.
The younger descendants of the Four Sacred Clans started whispering again.
"So he really doesn’t carry the sacred legacy?"
"But his power woke up the fifth end."
"Maybe the Voidwalker Ancestor was right. It’s similar, but not the true sacred legacy."
"Then what exactly is that power?"
Rose watched nervously from the Evercrest side, her hands clenched tight. Freya stood in the sky without a word, but her gaze never left Max for even a moment.

The Voidwalker Ancestor stood above the fifth end, his eyes deep and solemn as he watched the statue. Even he seemed uncertain now, since the statue’s silence confirmed part of what he’d said, yet it also deepened the mystery around Max.
But while everyone outside saw nothing, Max was no longer standing in front of the statue.

The moment his palm touched the stone, his senses had shifted. At first, there was only silence. Then the arena, the clan platforms, Freya’s figure in the sky, Rose, Angelina, the four ancestors, the Voidwalker Ancestor, and the countless watching descendants all vanished without warning.
Max found himself standing in a different world.

There was no arena here. No clan platforms. Only a vast land beneath a starless sky. The ground under his feet looked like dark glass, smooth and endless, reflecting faint points of light that didn’t exist above him.

In the distance, countless doors floated in the air, each one half open, each one showing a different scene behind it. Some doors showed burning worlds. Some showed silent oceans. Some showed battlefields littered with broken stars. Some showed empty palaces. Some showed nothing but darkness.
Max’s eyes narrowed.
’A dimensional world.’
He felt it right away. This place wasn’t an ordinary illusion, and it wasn’t a simple memory either. It carried the feel of sealed dimensions, hidden passages, and forgotten worlds.

It felt far too close to the deeper sensation of the Dimensional Keeper legacy, but at the same time it felt weaker, older, and incomplete, like a shadow left behind by someone who’d once touched the same source.
Then a man appeared in front of him. He stood with his back to Max, dressed in a plain long robe.

His hair was long and dark, falling down his back with no crown or ornament. His figure looked calm, not tall enough to seem monstrous, not majestic enough to resemble an emperor, yet the moment Max saw him, an invisible weight settled over his heart.
The man didn’t need to release any aura. His presence alone carried a stillness heavy enough to stop the countless floating doors from moving.
Max recognized him instantly. It was the man from the statue. The First Progenitor.

The man slowly turned around. His face matched the statue’s exactly, but alive. His eyes were deep and quiet, holding neither arrogance nor hostility. He looked at Max for a long time, as if measuring not his strength, but something hidden deeper in his foundation.
Then he spoke.
"So you’re the one carrying the current legacy."
Max frowned. The current legacy. Those words hit harder than he expected.
He didn’t answer right away. His body stayed tense, and his senses spread out through the strange world around him.

He couldn’t feel the arena outside anymore. He couldn’t feel Freya, Rose, or the Voidwalker Ancestor. He could still feel his own powers, but they sat quiet here, as if this world had no intention of suppressing him, yet could still see every part of him clearly.
Max looked at the man in front of him and asked, "Who are you?"
The man’s expression didn’t change.
"My descendants called me many things," he said. "Ancestor. Origin. First Progenitor. Founder of the Five Sacred Clans."
He paused. Then his voice dropped quieter.
"But before all of that, I was the first inheritor of the Dimensional Keeper Legacy."
Max’s pupils contracted. For a moment, even his breathing stopped.
The first inheritor of the Dimensional Keeper Legacy.

His mind raced. The forbidden bloodline of the Five Sacred Clans, the sacred legacy of the First Progenitor, the Voidwalker Clan’s connection to hidden worlds, the statue’s reaction to him, the strange pulse in his own blood, and the way his Dimensional Keeper legacy had responded to the arena all started fitting together in a way that finally made sense.
The forbidden bloodline everyone had been talking about this whole time hadn’t simply come from a man blessed by some unknown power. It came from the first inheritor of the Dimensional Keeper Legacy.
The First Progenitor wasn’t the source of the legacy. He’d been one of its inheritors. His descendants became the Five Sacred Clans because his bloodline had been transformed by that inheritance.

That was why they weren’t like ordinary humans descended from Primordials. That was why their forbidden bloodlines could rival Primordial Race bloodlines. That was why their sacred legacy felt similar to the Dimensional Keeper legacy without actually being the same thing.
It wasn’t the original source. It was a trace, an inheritance fragment, or maybe a bloodline echo left behind by the first inheritor.
Max’s frown deepened.
’So that’s why my blood reacted.’
