chapters.title: Chapter 1980: Anover!
paragraphs: The Dimensional Keeper legacy hadn’t reacted because the First Progenitor was its master. It had reacted because the statue belonged to a previous inheritor. The bloodlines of the Five Sacred Clans hadn’t trembled because Max carried their stolen legacy.
They’d trembled because his current Dimensional Keeper legacy stood closer to the true source than their inherited fragments ever could.
The First Progenitor looked at him quietly, then smiled. There was no pride in that smile. Only pity.
"I didn’t expect it," he said softly. "Even after countless generations, one of my descendants would once again become the carrier of the legacy."
Max’s eyes sharpened. "One of your descendants?"
The man nodded. "Voidwalker blood flows in you. Faint after so many generations, mixed with plenty of other powers, buried beneath bloodlines even I can’t fully read, but it’s still there."

Max fell silent. He’d known his surname carried danger. He’d known Freya had hidden their identity for a reason. But hearing the First Progenitor himself call him a descendant carried a completely different weight.
The man’s pity deepened.

"To ordinary people, inheriting something like this looks like fortune," the First Progenitor said. "To ambitious cultivators, it looks like destiny. To clans, forces, and races, it looks like supremacy. But I know better."
His gaze drifted toward the countless doors floating behind him.
"The Dimensional Keeper Legacy isn’t a blessing."
Max’s expression turned serious.
The First Progenitor looked back at him.
"It’s cursed by fate."

The strange world grew colder. The floating doors trembled faintly, and for a moment Max thought he heard sounds coming from behind them. Screams. Prayers. Battles. Collapsing worlds. Chains dragging across empty space. Then all of it vanished.

The First Progenitor continued, "Those who carry this legacy get pulled into conflicts that started long before they were even born. Doors will open in front of them whether they want to walk through or not. Powers hidden from ordinary law will take notice of them. Enemies they never wronged will hunt them down. Allies will fear them. Bloodlines will react to them. Ancient seals will wake up because of them. Fate itself will try to use them as a key."

Max’s heart sank slightly. That explanation sounded far too close to everything that had already happened to him. He hadn’t chosen to get tangled up in the Five Sacred Clans’ ancient history. He’d simply come to help Rose.
Yet because of the Dimensional Keeper legacy, the whole buried conflict had woken up, the Voidwalker Clan had come back out into the open, and the sacred ancestors had nearly gone to war.
The First Progenitor’s voice turned more urgent.

"You have to be careful out there. The legacy will make you stronger, but every step forward will drag out things that should’ve stayed asleep. Don’t trust every door it opens. Don’t assume every inheritance that recognizes you is on your side. And most importantly."
His expression suddenly shifted. For the first time, the calm in his eyes cracked. He looked past Max, as if seeing something through him, something distant and terrifying.
"Watch out for Anover-"

Before he could finish the sentence, the world shattered. Max’s vision blurred. The endless dark glass land disappeared. The floating doors vanished. The First Progenitor’s figure broke apart into countless fragments of light.
The next instant, Max found himself standing back in the Bloodline Legacy Battle arena.

His hand was still touching the statue. His body hadn’t moved. The arena looked exactly as it had before. The Four Sacred Clan leaders were watching him with suspicion. The four sacred ancestors stayed silent.

The Voidwalker Ancestor stood above the fifth end with a deep gaze. Freya still hovered in the sky with thousands of Voidwalker descendants. Rose watched anxiously from the Evercrest side. Angelina stood at the edge of the battlefield, her expression unreadable.

To everyone else, nothing had happened. Not one flash. Not one tremor. Not one shift in pressure. The statue of the First Progenitor didn’t glow brighter. Its closed eyes stayed shut. The five ends of the arena didn’t resonate. The bloodlines of the Four Sacred Clans weren’t suppressed any further.
In the eyes of everyone watching, the test had failed to prove that Max carried the Sacred Legacy of the Five Sacred Clans.
The Valerius Clan head sneered.
"As expected." His voice carried across the arena. "The statue didn’t react."
The Ashbourne head narrowed his eyes. "So he doesn’t carry the sacred legacy."
The Ravenhart head looked thoughtful. "At least not the one sealed by the Five Sacred Clans."
The Evercrest head gritted his teeth in frustration, but even he couldn’t deny what everyone had just witnessed. "Then whatever he carries is something else."
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at Max carefully.

Freya noticed something strange too. Max’s expression had changed. It was subtle, but she knew him too well. Everyone else saw the statue stay silent and assumed nothing had happened. Freya saw the look in Max’s eyes, the brief heaviness in his gaze, and the tension hidden beneath his calm face.
Something had happened. Only Max had seen it.
Max slowly pulled his hand back from the statue. His face stayed composed, but his mind was still echoing with that unfinished warning.
’Anover.’

He had no idea who or what Anover was. But the First Progenitor, the first inheritor of the Dimensional Keeper Legacy, had warned him with actual fear in his eyes. That alone was enough to make Max hold onto the name.
He turned away from the statue and looked at the crowd. The test had cleared him of carrying the sacred legacy in front of everyone.

But it had handed Max a far more dangerous truth. The sacred legacy of the Five Sacred Clans wasn’t the Dimensional Keeper Legacy. It was only something left behind by the first person who’d once carried it. And now, countless generations later, Max had inherited the current legacy.
A legacy cursed by fate.
’Even the goddess had warned me the Dimensional Keeper Legacy was cursed by fate, that every inheritor of it had died a brutal death.’ Max’s expression turned solemn.
That, combined with the fear he’d just seen in the First Progenitor’s eyes, told him he hadn’t experienced much of what this so-called curse of fate really meant yet.

Max slowly turned away from the statue of the First Progenitor. His hand had already left the stone, but the cold feeling from that strange world still lingered on his palm. The unfinished warning kept echoing in his mind.
Anover.
He didn’t know whether that was a person, a race, an organization, a world, or something even stranger, but he’d already carved the name into his memory.
Anything capable of making the First Progenitor, the first inheritor of the Dimensional Keeper Legacy, show fear right before his remnant vanished wasn’t something Max could afford to ignore.
Even so, now wasn’t the time to reveal what he’d seen. To everyone else, the test had ended without any reaction. The statue hadn’t brightened. Its eyes hadn’t opened.
The five clan platforms hadn’t resonated. The bloodlines of the Four Sacred Clans hadn’t been suppressed any further. In the eyes of the whole arena, the conclusion seemed obvious.
Max didn’t carry the Sacred Legacy of the Five Sacred Clans. The four clan heads and the four sacred ancestors could no longer use that excuse to imprison him.

chapters.title: Chapter 1981: A Shocking News!
paragraphs: Max’s gaze swept across them. The head of the Valerius Clan still looked cold, but the arrogance in his eyes had faded a little. The Ashbourne head frowned deeply, clearly unwilling to accept the result but unable to deny what had just happened in front of everyone.

The Ravenhart head stayed silent, her gaze thoughtful, as if she suspected there was more to this than met the eye. The Evercrest head, his chest still carrying faint traces of the wound Max had given him, looked at Max with anger, humiliation, and restrained killing intent.
Above them, the four sacred ancestors stayed equally silent, their expressions complicated. They’d wanted to test whether Max carried the stolen sacred legacy.

The test had failed to prove that. Worse for them, it had happened in front of the entire younger generation, in front of the Voidwalker remnants, in front of Freya, and in front of the awakened fifth end.

They could still distrust Max. They could still fear the Dimensional Keeper Legacy. But they couldn’t openly claim he was the vessel of the stolen sacred legacy anymore without making themselves look unreasonable.
Max’s voice broke the silence.
"Now that it’s proven I don’t carry your sacred legacy."
His tone stayed calm, but every word carried clearly across the arena. The four clan heads all looked at him at once.
Max continued, "Will you unseal the Voidwalker Clan?"

That question hit the arena like a thunderclap. Many descendants of the Four Sacred Clans widened their eyes. The elders frowned sharply. Several clan guards tightened their grips on their weapons without meaning to.

Even Rose looked at Max in surprise, and Angelina Valerius’s expression shifted slightly. Freya, though, stayed still in the sky, her gaze locked on the four sacred ancestors. The thousands of Voidwalker descendants behind her didn’t say anything, but their auras turned colder.
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at Max. For the first time since revealing the buried history, the old man’s expression softened again.
The question was simple. But it carried a weight that had lasted countless years. The Voidwalker Clan had been sealed because of the sacred legacy.
The Four Sacred Clans had called them traitors, imprisoned their people, abandoned their platform, erased their name, and hunted down or suppressed their remaining bloodline branches.

Now the very reason they’d used to imprison Max had been weakened in front of everyone. If Max didn’t carry the stolen sacred legacy, the old accusation couldn’t be thrown around so carelessly anymore.
The Valerius head’s face darkened.
"Unseal the Voidwalker Clan?" he repeated coldly.
The Ashbourne head snorted. "You think one test is enough to overturn countless years of judgment?"
Freya’s eyes turned icy.

Max looked at him calmly. "Then what would be enough? You accused me of carrying the stolen legacy. I touched the statue. Nothing happened. Your own ancestors said the statue would react if I carried it."
The Ravenhart head narrowed her eyes. "The test only proves you don’t carry the true sacred legacy. It doesn’t erase the old crimes of the Voidwalker Clan."
Max’s eyes turned colder. "Old crimes committed by some members influenced by the sacred legacy itself."
The Evercrest head gritted his teeth. "You’re in no position to lecture us about our own history."
Max smiled faintly. "Your history seems like it could use some correcting."

The mood tightened at once. Several Evercrest elders glared furiously at him, while Ashbourne warriors let out low growls of battle intent. The Valerius descendants looked offended, and even a few Ravenhart elders frowned.

But among the younger geniuses, the reactions weren’t so simple. Cassian Valerius stayed silent. Draven Ashbourne looked at Max with a strange expression, no longer dismissing him as just arrogant. Seraphine Ravenhart watched everything with deep, thoughtful eyes. Aelric Evercrest stood pale and wounded, but even he seemed shaken by how far this had all gone.
The Valerius ancestor slowly raised his hand, and the sacred clan heads immediately fell silent.
His old eyes settled on Max.

"The sealing of the Voidwalker Clan can’t be undone with one sentence," he said. "Even if you don’t carry the sacred legacy, even if the history is more complicated than our descendants ever knew, the Voidwalker Clan still broke the seal and caused the sacred legacy to disappear. A matter like this can’t be settled in the middle of an arena."
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s gaze turned cold. "How convenient."
The Ashbourne ancestor said heavily, "Voidwalker, don’t test our patience. We agreed to stop the fighting because the truth needed to come out. That doesn’t mean the old judgment has been erased."
Freya’s voice came down from the sky. "Then when will it be erased?"
No one answered right away. The silence itself was the answer.
Max’s expression turned colder.

Before the four clan heads could say anything more, a disturbance suddenly broke out from outside the arena. A spatial gate tore open violently near the outer entrance of the Bloodline Legacy Battle grounds.

The gate looked unstable, trembling as if whoever opened it had used emergency authority without waiting for proper clearance. Several guards immediately stepped forward, but before they could stop the newcomer, a figure rushed through the gate and stumbled into the arena.

It was a messenger of the Four Sacred Clans. His robe was torn. His face was pale. Blood stained the corner of his mouth, and his aura felt chaotic, as if he’d crossed several emergency transfer formations back to back without stabilizing himself. The moment he appeared, everyone’s attention snapped toward him.
The Valerius head frowned. "What’s the meaning of this?"

The messenger didn’t even manage a proper bow at first. He nearly collapsed to the ground, caught himself with one hand, and then lifted his head with a look of panic that instantly tightened the chests of several elders.
"Masters!" His voice cracked. "Devils!"
The entire arena went still. That single word carried a chill sharp enough to cut through every argument going on.
The messenger’s eyes were wide with panic.
"Devils have appeared in the Divine Realm!"
For a moment, no one reacted. Then the whole arena exploded with disbelief.
"Impossible!"
"How could devils show up in our Divine Realm?"
"How could they have even reached our universe?"
"Devils? Here?"
"Are you certain?"
The messenger trembled under the weight of every gaze fixed on him.
The Valerius head’s expression changed drastically. "What did you just say?"
The Ashbourne head stepped forward, his voice booming across the arena. "How could devils get into our universe? Weren’t all the devils supposed to have been wiped out long ago?"
"That’s impossible!" an elder shouted. "The ancient records clearly say the last devil army was completely exterminated!"
"The remaining devils were sealed outside the universe!"
"There shouldn’t be a single devil left anywhere in the Divine Realm!"
"Did the border seals break?"
"Who opened the passage?"

The descendants of the Four Sacred Clans were completely shaken, their faces filled with disbelief, fear, and confusion. Many of them had grown up hearing that the devils were eradicated from the Divine Realm countless years ago.
To them, devils weren’t a living race that could just suddenly come back. They were remnants of an ancient catastrophe, enemies already destroyed and buried in history.

chapters.title: Chapter 1982: Devils!
paragraphs: ’Devils?!’ Max’s expression also turned dark. He hadn’t forgotten what had happened to his world just because of a drop of blood from a being called True Origin Devil.
Even the four sacred ancestors had lost their calm.

The Valerius Ancestor’s sacred light erupted around him. "Impossible. Every devil in the Divine Realm was killed during the final war. The surviving remnants were driven out of the universe and sealed away. How could they possibly show up here?"
The Ravenhart Ancestor’s eyes narrowed sharply. "Unless the ancient records were wrong."
"No," the Ashbourne Ancestor said coldly, though a trace of shock slipped into his voice. "The records weren’t wrong. I personally saw the remnants of the devil army get destroyed."
The Evercrest Ancestor’s spatial roots twisted violently around him. "Then how did they get into our universe?"
The messenger forced himself to keep talking.

"They attacked several planets in a small star realm out near the outer regions. Local forces intercepted them, but the damage has already spread across multiple worlds. We got urgent reports through the sacred warning network. The aura’s been confirmed."
He swallowed hard.
"They’re not corrupted beasts. They’re not abyssal cultivators. They’re not some disguised race."
His voice trembled even more.
"They’re devils."
The arena fell into an even deeper uproar.
"Impossible!"
"Devils can’t exist in the Divine Realm!"
"They were all killed!"
"How could they have survived this long?"
"Were they hiding somewhere in the universe?"
"Could they have come from another universe?"
"Is there a passage connecting our universe to the outside?"

The shock was so massive that even the dispute between Max and the Voidwalker Clan got pushed aside for the moment. This wasn’t an internal conflict, an old historical dispute, or a bloodline accusation you could argue through ancestors and legacy tests. This was something that should have been impossible.
Devils had appeared in their Divine Realm. In their universe.

The younger descendants, already shaken by the Voidwalker truth, now turned pale for an entirely different reason. Many of them had only ever heard about devils in old war scriptures and ancestral warnings.
They’d been taught the devil race was exterminated from the Divine Realm long ago, that the final devil army had been destroyed, and that no devil could ever come back.
Yet now a messenger stood in front of them claiming devils had attacked their planets.
The clan heads’ expressions shifted sharply.
The Valerius head stared at the messenger. "You’re certain of this?"
"Yes!" the messenger replied urgently. "The aura was verified through the ancient devil-suppression formations. There’s no mistake. They’re genuine devils."
The Ashbourne head’s face turned grim. "How many?"

"The exact number’s unknown. The first report says only a vanguard showed up, but their power was strange. Some were weak, but a few were strong enough to destroy planetary defense formations. Local star realm forces are holding them off for now, but they’ve asked for immediate reinforcement."
The Ravenhart head’s gaze darkened. "Were there any warning signs before the attack?"
The messenger shook his head. "None that we detected. They just appeared suddenly, like a crack opened out of nowhere."
Max’s heart stirred.
A crack opened out of nowhere.
The First Progenitor’s unfinished warning echoed in his mind again.
’Watch out for Anover.’
His eyes narrowed slightly. He didn’t know if this devil attack was connected, but the timing felt far too strange to ignore.
The Evercrest head looked toward the four ancestors. "Ancestors, how is this even possible? If all the devils were killed in the Divine Realm long ago, where did these come from?"

The four sacred ancestors didn’t answer right away. Their expressions had turned extremely grave. Even the Voidwalker Ancestor frowned deeply. The old man had lived through the ancient era and understood better than anyone just how terrifying the devil race had once been. If devils had truly come back to the Divine Realm, the consequences would be unimaginable.

Freya’s face changed slightly too, and the thousands of Voidwalker descendants in the sky shifted their formation, their earlier hostility toward the Four Sacred Clans momentarily pushed aside by the sudden news.
The Valerius Ancestor looked at the messenger. "Which star realm?"
The messenger answered quickly. "The Veyrith Star Realm. It’s a small star realm under the protection route of the eastern Divine Realm forces."
The Ashbourne Ancestor’s eyes turned fierce. "How long ago did this start?"
"The first attack began less than an hour ago," the messenger said. "The report reached us through emergency channels only moments ago."
The Ravenhart Ancestor’s shadow feathers trembled faintly. "Less than an hour, and they’ve already hit several planets."
The Evercrest Ancestor’s spatial roots coiled tight. "This isn’t some random breach."
The Valerius Ancestor’s expression turned terrifyingly cold.
"If the devils were truly wiped out of the Divine Realm, then their appearance means someone opened a passage into our universe."
His gaze swept across the arena.
"Or something from outside the universe found a way in."
A heavy pressure spread across the arena. The Bloodline Legacy Battle had already collapsed into chaos, but now even that chaos felt beside the point.
The dispute between the Four Sacred Clans and the Voidwalker Clan was still unresolved.

Max still stood at the center of a mystery tangled up with the Dimensional Keeper Legacy, the sacred legacy, and the First Progenitor. The Voidwalker Clan was still sealed, and the four sacred ancestors hadn’t agreed to release them.
But the universe had moved before any of that could get settled.

Devils had appeared. Not in some distant, forgotten realm. Not on an ancient battlefield. They’d appeared right in the Divine Realm, inside their own universe. The entire Divine Realm might be about to get shaken to its core.
Max slowly looked up at Freya. Freya looked back down at him. Neither of them said anything. But both understood this was no ordinary interruption.
The Four Sacred Clans had just been forced to face their buried past. And at that exact moment, an ancient enemy that should have gone extinct had returned to their universe.
The head of the Valerius Clan looked at Max, then at the Voidwalker Ancestor, then at the messenger. His expression was ugly, but even he understood the situation had changed.
The argument over the Voidwalker Clan wouldn’t end here. But for now, the whole arena had been hit with news carrying the weight of war.

The messenger lowered his head and said in a shaking voice, "Masters, the forces of the Veyrith Star Realm are asking for immediate aid. If reinforcements don’t arrive soon, the devils might break through their defense line and spread into nearby star realms."
The arena sank into a grim silence. No one dared treat the devils as some distant legend anymore. They’d entered their universe. They’d attacked their planets. And no one knew how they’d come back.
The four sacred ancestors traded grave glances. The Voidwalker Ancestor looked toward the glowing statue of the First Progenitor.
Max’s hand slowly curled into a fist. And in his mind, one name echoed again.
Anover.

sentences.text: ’Devils?!’ Max’s expression also turned dark.
He hadn’t forgotten what had happened to his world just because of a drop of blood from a being called True Origin Devil.
Even the four sacred ancestors had lost their calm.
The Valerius Ancestor’s sacred light erupted around him.
"Impossible.
Every devil in the Divine Realm was killed during the final war.
The surviving remnants were driven out of the universe and sealed away.
How could they possibly show up here?"
The Ravenhart Ancestor’s eyes narrowed sharply.
"Unless the ancient records were wrong."
"No," the Ashbourne Ancestor said coldly, though a trace of shock slipped into his voice.
"The records weren’t wrong.
I personally saw the remnants of the devil army get destroyed."
The Evercrest Ancestor’s spatial roots twisted violently around him.
"Then how did they get into our universe?"
The messenger forced himself to keep talking.
"They attacked several planets in a small star realm out near the outer regions.
Local forces intercepted them, but the damage has already spread across multiple worlds.
We got urgent reports through the sacred warning network.
The aura’s been confirmed."
He swallowed hard.
"They’re not corrupted beasts.
They’re not abyssal cultivators.
They’re not some disguised race."
His voice trembled even more.
"They’re devils."
The arena fell into an even deeper uproar.
"Impossible!"
"Devils can’t exist in the Divine Realm!"
"They were all killed!"
"How could they have survived this long?"
"Were they hiding somewhere in the universe?"
"Could they have come from another universe?"
"Is there a passage connecting our universe to the outside?"
The shock was so massive that even the dispute between Max and the Voidwalker Clan got pushed aside for the moment.
This wasn’t an internal conflict, an old historical dispute, or a bloodline accusation you could argue through ancestors and legacy tests.
This was something that should have been impossible.
Devils had appeared in their Divine Realm.
In their universe.
The younger descendants, already shaken by the Voidwalker truth, now turned pale for an entirely different reason.
Many of them had only ever heard about devils in old war scriptures and ancestral warnings.
They’d been taught the devil race was exterminated from the Divine Realm long ago, that the final devil army had been destroyed, and that no devil could ever come back.
Yet now a messenger stood in front of them claiming devils had attacked their planets.
The clan heads’ expressions shifted sharply.
The Valerius head stared at the messenger.
"You’re certain of this?"
"Yes!" the messenger replied urgently.
"The aura was verified through the ancient devil-suppression formations.
There’s no mistake.
They’re genuine devils."
The Ashbourne head’s face turned grim.
"How many?"
"The exact number’s unknown.
The first report says only a vanguard showed up, but their power was strange.
Some were weak, but a few were strong enough to destroy planetary defense formations.
Local star realm forces are holding them off for now, but they’ve asked for immediate reinforcement."
The Ravenhart head’s gaze darkened.
"Were there any warning signs before the attack?"
The messenger shook his head.
"None that we detected.
They just appeared suddenly, like a crack opened out of nowhere."
Max’s heart stirred.
A crack opened out of nowhere.
The First Progenitor’s unfinished warning echoed in his mind again.
’Watch out for Anover.’
His eyes narrowed slightly.
He didn’t know if this devil attack was connected, but the timing felt far too strange to ignore.
The Evercrest head looked toward the four ancestors.
"Ancestors, how is this even possible?
If all the devils were killed in the Divine Realm long ago, where did these come from?"
The four sacred ancestors didn’t answer right away.
Their expressions had turned extremely grave.
Even the Voidwalker Ancestor frowned deeply.
The old man had lived through the ancient era and understood better than anyone just how terrifying the devil race had once been.
If devils had truly come back to the Divine Realm, the consequences would be unimaginable.

Freya’s face changed slightly too, and the thousands of Voidwalker descendants in the sky shifted their formation, their earlier hostility toward the Four Sacred Clans momentarily pushed aside by the sudden news.
The Valerius Ancestor looked at the messenger.
"Which star realm?"
The messenger answered quickly.
"The Veyrith Star Realm.
It’s a small star realm under the protection route of the eastern Divine Realm forces."
The Ashbourne Ancestor’s eyes turned fierce.
"How long ago did this start?"
"The first attack began less than an hour ago," the messenger said.
"The report reached us through emergency channels only moments ago."
The Ravenhart Ancestor’s shadow feathers trembled faintly.
"Less than an hour, and they’ve already hit several planets."
The Evercrest Ancestor’s spatial roots coiled tight.
"This isn’t some random breach."
The Valerius Ancestor’s expression turned terrifyingly cold.
"If the devils were truly wiped out of the Divine Realm, then their appearance means someone opened a passage into our universe."
His gaze swept across the arena.
"Or something from outside the universe found a way in."
A heavy pressure spread across the arena.
The Bloodline Legacy Battle had already collapsed into chaos, but now even that chaos felt beside the point.
The dispute between the Four Sacred Clans and the Voidwalker Clan was still unresolved.
Max still stood at the center of a mystery tangled up with the Dimensional Keeper Legacy, the sacred legacy, and the First Progenitor.
The Voidwalker Clan was still sealed, and the four sacred ancestors hadn’t agreed to release them.
But the universe had moved before any of that could get settled.
Devils had appeared.
Not in some distant, forgotten realm.
Not on an ancient battlefield.
They’d appeared right in the Divine Realm, inside their own universe.
The entire Divine Realm might be about to get shaken to its core.
Max slowly looked up at Freya.
Freya looked back down at him.
Neither of them said anything.
But both understood this was no ordinary interruption.
The Four Sacred Clans had just been forced to face their buried past.
And at that exact moment, an ancient enemy that should have gone extinct had returned to their universe.

chapters.title: Chapter 1983: Sending Help!
paragraphs: The arena stayed silent after the messenger’s report.
For a few moments, even the ancient conflict between the Four Sacred Clans and the Voidwalker Clan seemed to fade beneath the weight of that one word.
Devils.
The Bloodline Legacy Battle had already turned into something far bigger than a battle between young geniuses, but the sudden news of devils in the Divine Realm changed the whole mood.

This was no longer just about buried history, a stolen sacred legacy, or whether the Voidwalker Clan should stay sealed. If devils had really entered their universe again, every supreme force in the Divine Realm would have to respond.
The Valerius head’s expression turned sharp and decisive.

"Summon the third and seventh sacred response teams," he ordered right away. "Send them to the Veyrith Star Realm immediately. Have them assist the local forces, stabilize the planetary defense lines, rescue important survivors where possible, and eliminate every devil they find."
Several Valerius elders bowed at once.
"Yes, Clan Head!"

The Ashbourne head stepped forward, his earlier anger at Max still there but pushed down beneath battle intent. "Send Ashbourne’s Blood-Iron Vanguard with them. If devils have really shown up, ordinary reinforcements might not cut it. Let our warriors find out whether these devils are remnants, scouts, or part of something bigger."

The Ravenhart head’s eyes stayed cold and thoughtful. "Ravenhart will send a shadow-prophecy unit too. We need information more than we need blind slaughter. Find out where the crack opened, whether it’s stable, whether it can be traced, and whether there are signs of a second breach."

The Evercrest head, still wounded from Max’s attack, clenched his teeth and gave his own order. "Evercrest will send a spatial sealing team. If the devils came through a crack, space itself needs to be locked down before more of them cross over."
The messenger lowered his head quickly, relief flashing across his pale face.

The Valerius head looked at the gathered elders and younger participants. "Don’t assume this is only our problem. The Primordial Race and the other top first-rate forces should have gotten the warning by now too. If they have any sense, they’ll have already sent a team or two."
His voice grew heavier.
"But we are the Four Sacred Clans. We don’t wait for others to move before we act."

The Ashbourne head said coldly, "Whoever’s chosen to go needs to treat this like a real battlefield, not an investigation. If the report’s true, kill every devil you see. Only capture one if it doesn’t risk the defense line."

The Ravenhart head added, "And don’t trust how they look. Devils aren’t always mindless monsters. Some can think, deceive, possess, and hide their aura. Confirm with devil-suppression formations before you bring anything back."
The Evercrest head looked at his people. "Prepare cross-realm spatial gates. I want the first reinforcement team gone within a hundred breaths."

The whole arena moved at once. Elders passed on orders. Sacred clan guards rushed out. Formation masters started activating emergency platforms behind the clan seats. Several young geniuses who’d been watching the Bloodline Legacy Battle with pride and excitement now stood with grim faces, realizing the stage they’d come to compete on might soon turn into a battlefield soaked in devil blood.
Cassian Valerius rose from his seat. "I’ll go too."
The Valerius head looked at him. "You’re one of the main participants in the Bloodline Legacy Battle here."
Cassian’s expression didn’t change. "The battle’s already been interrupted. If devils have returned, sitting here to protect our reputation doesn’t mean anything."
Draven Ashbourne laughed coldly and stood as well. "Good. I was getting tired of listening to old secrets anyway. Devils sound more interesting."
The Ashbourne head glared at him. "This isn’t a hunt for your entertainment."
Draven’s grin faded slightly, but the battle intent in his eyes only grew stronger. "I know."
Seraphine Ravenhart also stood, her silver-purple eyes distant. "I’ll go with the Ravenhart unit and give them whatever help I can."
Aelric Evercrest tried to stand, but the wound from Max’s Black Dragon Cataclysm Breath flared up again, twisting his face with pain. An Evercrest elder immediately pressed a hand on his shoulder.
"You’re not going anywhere in your condition."
Aelric’s expression turned ugly, but he didn’t argue. Today’s defeat had already crushed enough of his pride.

Max watched all of this in silence. The speed at which the Four Sacred Clans switched from internal conflict to war preparation explained why they’d stayed at the top for so long. Their history might be ugly, and their treatment of the Voidwalker Clan might be built on lies and fear, but when an ancient enemy showed up, they moved without hesitation.

Freya descended slightly from the sky, though she didn’t dismiss the thousands of Voidwalker descendants surrounding the arena. Her gaze moved from the emergency formations to Max, then to the Voidwalker Ancestor.
The Voidwalker Ancestor had stayed quiet since the messenger appeared. His expression looked grave, but there was something deeper in his eyes too. Recognition. Worry. A faint trace of old fear.
Max noticed it right away. The old man knew more about the devils than he’d let on. Maybe everyone from that ancient generation did.
The Valerius ancestor looked at the Voidwalker Ancestor and said coldly, "Don’t think this matter is finished."
The Voidwalker Ancestor replied calmly, "I never thought it was."
The Ashbourne ancestor’s voice came out heavy. "The question of unsealing the Voidwalker Clan gets discussed once the devil situation is contained."
Freya’s eyes narrowed. "Discussed?"

The Ravenhart ancestor looked at her. "Don’t push too far. You threatened the descendants of the Four Sacred Clans in our own arena. If it weren’t for the devil report, this place would already be drowning in blood."
Freya’s expression didn’t change. "If it weren’t for your attempt to seal my brother, we wouldn’t even be here."
The Evercrest ancestor’s spatial roots stirred, but the Valerius ancestor raised his hand slightly and kept things from getting worse.
"Enough." His gaze turned toward the emergency gates forming behind the clan platforms. "The devil matter comes first."

Nobody liked that conclusion. Not the Four Sacred Clans. Not Freya. Not the Voidwalker descendants. Not even Max. But for now, it was the only thing keeping the arena from turning into a battlefield between five ancient bloodlines while devils attacked planets somewhere else.

chapters.title: Chapter 1984: Voidwalker Clan!
paragraphs: At that moment, the Voidwalker Ancestor looked at Max and Freya.
"Come with me."
Max turned toward him.
Freya’s eyes shifted slightly. "Where to?"
The old man glanced once at the glowing statue of the First Progenitor, then at the abandoned fifth end beneath him.
"Somewhere we can talk peacefully."
The four sacred ancestors immediately looked at him.
The Valerius ancestor’s eyes narrowed. "Voidwalker."
The Ashbourne ancestor’s aura pressed down slightly. "What are you planning?"
The Ravenhart ancestor’s shadow moved silently, as if trying to trace whatever path the old man was about to open.
The Evercrest ancestor said coldly, "You expect us to let you take him away after everything that just happened?"
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at them without fear.

"You’ve got devils in the Veyrith Star Realm, a possible breach into the universe, panic spreading through your own descendants, and emergency teams waiting on your orders. If you’d still rather spend your attention watching an old remnant talk with two descendants of my clan, then maybe the Four Sacred Clans really have gotten weaker than I thought."
The words came out calm, but they hit hard.

The four ancestors’ expressions darkened. The four clan heads looked furious too, but none of them stopped him right away. He was right. They were suspicious of him. They were suspicious of Max. They were suspicious of Freya and the thousands of Voidwalker descendants surrounding the arena. But right now, they had something much worse to deal with.

Devils had shown up in the Divine Realm. If the first reinforcements arrived too late, the Veyrith Star Realm might fall apart. If the crack widened, nearby star realms could descend into chaos. If this was just the start of a bigger invasion, every delay would cost them dearly.
The Valerius ancestor finally said, "Don’t leave the sacred domain."
The Voidwalker Ancestor smiled faintly. "This whole domain used to belong to five clans. Don’t talk to me like I’m some guest here."
The Valerius ancestor’s face turned colder, but he didn’t push further.

Freya raised her hand. The Voidwalker formations above the arena shifted, but didn’t pull back completely. The thousands of descendants stayed in position, though their pressure eased slightly. It was a quiet message. They wouldn’t strike first if the Four Sacred Clans didn’t, but they wouldn’t drop their guard either.
Max looked toward Rose. She still stood near the Evercrest platform, surrounded by elders who no longer dared treat her too harshly.

Too much had changed. Her representative had beaten Aelric, injured the Evercrest head, awakened the fifth sacred end, and dragged out the truth about the Voidwalker Clan. The Evercrest elders could hate her, blame her, or fear her, but they couldn’t dismiss her as some useless castaway anymore.

Rose met Max’s gaze. For a moment, she looked conflicted. This whole disaster had started because she’d asked him for help, yet it had also given her something she’d never expected. The Evercrest Clan could no longer hide behind a spotless sacred image. Their history had cracked wide open in front of everyone.
Max gave her a slight nod. It wasn’t a promise that everything was fixed. It was just a sign that he hadn’t forgotten why he’d come.
Rose’s eyes softened slightly.

The Voidwalker Ancestor raised his hand, and the abandoned fifth end opened beneath him. Not a door. Not a gate. A ring of dark starry light unfolded in the air, filled with layers of space twisting inward like a passage leading into a sealed dimensional chamber. It carried the same feel as the fifth end, but deeper, older, and far more private.
Freya descended from the sky and landed near Max. For the first time in years, brother and sister stood close enough to touch.

Max looked at her. Freya looked back. There was so much between them. Questions, secrets, warnings, years apart, the sudden reveal of the Voidwalker Clan, and the heavy shadow of the devils’ return. But underneath all of that, there was relief.
Freya reached out and touched his shoulder lightly.
"How have you been, Maxy?" she asked softly.
Max gave a faint smile and said solemnly, "I’m fine. Just a little shocked that the Voidwalker name has this much history behind it."
Freya sighed. "I’m sorry. Father asked me not to tell you about any of this. But who could’ve guessed you’d end up at the Four Sacred Clans anyway."
Max laughed lightly.
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at the two of them, and for a moment, the heaviness in his eyes eased. Then he turned and stepped into the starry passage.
"Come. We don’t have much time."

Max and Freya followed him. Behind them, the Bloodline Legacy Battle arena stayed tense and chaotic. The Four Sacred Clans kept preparing their reinforcements. Emergency gates lit up. Chosen teams gathered. The four sacred ancestors watched the Voidwalker passage with suspicion, but they didn’t stop it.
The starry passage closed behind Max and Freya without a sound.

One moment, the chaos of the Bloodline Legacy Battle arena had been right behind them, full of emergency orders, rushing elders, glowing spatial gates, and the heavy pressure of the Four Sacred Clans preparing for the sudden devil invasion. The next moment, all of it disappeared, replaced by a silence so complete that even Max’s own breathing sounded loud.
They’d arrived inside a chamber.

It wasn’t large in the ordinary sense, yet it felt vast because of how much space had been folded inside it. The walls were made of dark stone that shimmered faintly like a night sky, and countless silver lines ran across them in circular patterns, forming dimensional rings that overlapped one another. Some rings rotated slowly.

Some were cracked. Some sat dim, as if they hadn’t woken up in countless years. At the center of the chamber floated a black crystal sphere, and inside it drifted tiny points of light that looked like sealed worlds sitting in silence.

Max’s eyes narrowed. The aura here felt different from the arena. The Bloodline Legacy Battle arena carried the weight of the Five Sacred Clans and the statue of the First Progenitor, but this chamber carried only one thing.
Voidwalker.

The four sacred ancestors watched the Voidwalker passage with suspicion, but they didn’t stop it.
The starry passage closed behind Max and Freya without a sound.

One moment, the chaos of the Bloodline Legacy Battle arena had been right behind them, full of emergency orders, rushing elders, glowing spatial gates, and the heavy pressure of the Four Sacred Clans preparing for the sudden devil invasion.
The next moment, all of it disappeared, replaced by a silence so complete that even Max’s own breathing sounded loud.
They’d arrived inside a chamber.
It wasn’t large in the ordinary sense, yet it felt vast because of how much space had been folded inside it.
The walls were made of dark stone that shimmered faintly like a night sky, and countless silver lines ran across them in circular patterns, forming dimensional rings that overlapped one another.
Some rings rotated slowly.
Some were cracked.
Some sat dim, as if they hadn’t woken up in countless years.
At the center of the chamber floated a black crystal sphere, and inside it drifted tiny points of light that looked like sealed worlds sitting in silence.
Max’s eyes narrowed.
The aura here felt different from the arena.
The Bloodline Legacy Battle arena carried the weight of the Five Sacred Clans and the statue of the First Progenitor, but this chamber carried only one thing.
Voidwalker.

chapters.title: Chapter 1985: Oliver Voidwalker!
paragraphs: Every stone, every mark, every folded layer of space, and every star-like point of light carried that same deep bloodline resonance that had been stirring inside Max ever since the abandoned fifth end woke up. Even Freya, who’d stayed calm in front of the Four Sacred Clans and their ancestors, went quieter after stepping into this place.

The Voidwalker Ancestor walked ahead of them. His figure still looked faint, and Max could tell this wasn’t his full body. He was a remnant, a projection, or something bound to this sealed chamber. But inside this place, his presence felt far more stable. The dark starry light around him no longer flickered like a dying flame. Instead, it moved with calm strength, as if the chamber itself were lending him support.
He stopped in front of the floating black crystal sphere and turned around, his eyes moving from Freya to Max.
Then he asked, "Was your father named Oliver Voidwalker?"
The question was simple. But the moment it came out, something inside Max tightened.

Oliver Voidwalker. His father. The man who’d disappeared into the Celestial Thorn Abyss along with his mother, Divine Queen Caelira. The man Max had been searching for, tied up in the mysteries of the second elven faction, the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, Freya, and now the Voidwalker Clan itself.

Max looked at Freya. Her expression had shifted slightly too. For a brief moment, the strong, cold woman who’d surrounded the Bloodline Legacy Battle arena with thousands of Voidwalker descendants looked less like a commander and more like a daughter hearing her father’s name after far too long.
Both of them nodded.
"Yes," Max said.
Freya’s voice followed quietly. "Oliver Voidwalker is our father."

The Voidwalker Ancestor closed his eyes. For a long moment, he said nothing. The chamber stayed silent, but the silver rings on the walls trembled faintly, as if the name Oliver had stirred up some old memory buried inside the Voidwalker inheritance.
At last, the old man sighed.
"Oliver was a good kid."

His voice came out softer now. Not the voice of an ancient being facing down four sacred ancestors. Not the voice of a sealed remnant exposing buried history in front of an entire arena. It was the voice of an old man remembering someone from his own bloodline.
"One of the few who managed to escape," he continued.
Max’s eyes sharpened. "Escape from where?"

The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at him. "From the sealing net of the Four Sacred Clans. After the main Voidwalker bloodline got sealed, not every branch was captured at once. Some outer descendants had already been sent away before the final judgment. Some hid in folded worlds. Some changed their names. Some joined other races and forces. Some got hunted down over the years. Some survived."
His gaze moved to Freya.
"Your father was one of the ones who survived."
Freya’s hands tightened slightly. "He never told us everything."

The Voidwalker Ancestor nodded. "He probably couldn’t. The Four Sacred Clans placed bloodline restrictions, memory traps, and tracking seals across a lot of old records. Those who escaped carried pieces of the history, but talking too much could expose them. In the end, most of our descendants learned to stay quiet, not because they were ashamed of the Voidwalker name, but because silence kept them alive."
Max’s expression turned colder. Freya had once warned him never to say the Voidwalker name out loud. Now he finally understood why.

The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at him with a trace of regret. "Oliver should’ve been able to stand here himself one day. He had talent. He had patience. More importantly, he had the stubbornness that runs through our clan. But fate wasn’t kind to him."
Max’s eyes deepened. "My parents are still alive."
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at him.
Max continued, "They’re imprisoned in the Celestial Thorn Abyss."
A heavy silence filled the chamber. Freya looked at Max sharply. She’d known more than most, but hearing Max say it so plainly still sent a flash of pain through her eyes.
The Voidwalker Ancestor’s expression turned complicated.
"Celestial Thorn Abyss," he repeated softly. "So that’s where they ended up."
Max stepped forward. "You know it?"

"I know of that prison," the old man said. "That place isn’t simple. If Oliver’s really imprisoned there, rescuing him won’t be easy. The elves are one of the three races of the Divine Realm, and they’re not to be underestimated."
Max’s gaze didn’t waver. "I know."
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at him for a long moment. Then he nodded.
"Good. At least you understand that much."

He turned and raised his hand toward the floating black crystal sphere. The sphere trembled, and the silver rings across the walls started rotating faster. A path opened at the far end of the chamber, but it wasn’t a normal door. It was a corridor made from overlapping dimensional rings, each one leading deeper into a hidden part of the abandoned Voidwalker end.
The old man spoke again.
"Since both of you are Oliver’s children, and both of you carry the Voidwalker bloodline, you’re members of my clan."
His gaze turned solemn.
"And members of my clan shouldn’t stand before the world without our inheritance."
Max and Freya both looked at him.

The Voidwalker Ancestor continued, "The Four Sacred Clans called us traitors and sealed our main bloodline, but they never destroyed the true inheritance of the Voidwalker Clan. They could abandon our end. They could erase our name from public history. They could imprison our people. But the inheritance chamber was hidden away before the final sealing, and only a descendant with the true Voidwalker bloodline can get inside."

The corridor of dimensional rings brightened. Max could feel it calling to him from within. It wasn’t as overwhelming as the Dimensional Keeper Legacy. It didn’t make his soul tremble the way the First Progenitor’s remnant had. But it still felt powerful, ancient, and deeply tied to his blood. It felt like a road that had been waiting for him since before he even knew his surname mattered.
Freya’s eyes changed too. She’d clearly known about the Voidwalker remnants, and she’d brought thousands of them to the arena, but from her expression, even she hadn’t stepped into this place before.

The Voidwalker Ancestor noticed her look and nodded faintly. "The outer descendants held onto what they could, but this chamber was sealed with me. Neither of you could enter until the abandoned fifth end woke up again. Max’s arrival opened up what had been buried for so many years."
Freya glanced at Max. Max looked back at her. For a moment, neither of them spoke.

chapters.title: Chapter 1986: Awakening of the Voidwalker Bloodline!
paragraphs: The Voidwalker Ancestor started walking toward the dimensional corridor.
"Come."

The two siblings followed. As they stepped into the corridor, the world around them stretched out. Max felt like he was walking through several spaces at once. One step crossed a dark bridge under a starry sky. Another step passed through a silent hall filled with floating weapons.

Another step moved across a battlefield where countless Voidwalker warriors had once stood with silver rings glowing behind them. None of these were real places. They were memory fragments built into the inheritance path, letting descendants feel the weight of the clan before receiving its legacy.
The deeper they went, the stronger the bloodline resonance grew.

At last, the corridor opened. Max and Freya arrived in front of an enormous door. The door was black, but it wasn’t lifeless. Silver dimensional rings were carved across its surface, and at the center sat the same dark star symbol that had appeared above the abandoned fifth end.

Beneath that symbol were countless names carved into the stone. Some names shone bright. Some sat dim. Some had been scratched away by old battle scars. Some were covered in cracks, as if their owners had died while the clan was being sealed.
The Voidwalker Ancestor stopped in front of the door.
"This is the Inheritance Chamber of the Voidwalker Clan."
His voice grew heavier.

"Inside lies what’s left of our techniques, bloodline arts, spatial scriptures, dimensional weapons, ancestral records, and the paths left behind by our greatest descendants. Some are complete. Some are broken. Some are dangerous. Some might not even recognize the current era anymore. But they belong to our clan, and now they belong to both of you."
Max looked at the door. His heart, which had stayed steady even in front of the four sacred ancestors, stirred slightly.

This felt different from the Primordial Bloodline. Different from the Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline. Different from the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline. Different even from the Dimensional Keeper Legacy.
This wasn’t some power he’d seized through a trial or awakened through battle. This was his family’s inheritance.
Freya stood beside him, silent.
The Voidwalker Ancestor placed one hand on the door. The dark star symbol lit up. Then he looked back at them.
"Max Voidwalker. Freya Voidwalker."
His old eyes carried pride, sorrow, and expectation all at once.
"You both carry the blood of my Voidwalker Clan, but without the inheritance, that bloodline is going to waste in you two. Go on and inherit what belongs to the Voidwalker Clan."
He looked at Max next.

"And Max, make sure you use this chance to push your strength up to the Law Manifestation Realm. Devils have invaded our universe, and there’s no telling how big this invasion is going to get. You’ll need every bit of strength you can get right now. An upheaval is coming, and no one knows when the whole Divine Realm might turn into a battlefield. So push your strength up as fast as you can."
The Voidwalker Ancestor paused for a moment, his gaze deepening.

"I’m sure the Primordial Race has plans for you and the other top geniuses, but you still need to be strong enough to actually use those opportunities when they come. Opportunity without strength is just another kind of danger."
Then he stepped aside.
"Now go ahead."

Max looked at the open door. Beyond it wasn’t a room in the ordinary sense. The inside of the Inheritance Chamber looked like a silent universe sealed beneath stone. There was no floor at first glance, only a path made of dark crystal floating above a vast starry abyss.
Countless silver rings rotated slowly in the darkness, each one holding an image, a scripture, a weapon’s shadow, a memory fragment, or a sealed bloodline mark.

Some rings showed ancient Voidwalker warriors standing before broken worlds. Some held diagrams of dimensional passages and folded spaces. Some showed battle arts where a single step crossed ten thousand realms. Some contained defensive techniques that turned the body into a hidden world. Some held killing arts that cut through distance itself.
Max felt his blood stir. Not his Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline. Not his Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline. Not even his Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline. It was the buried Voidwalker blood inside him.

That bloodline had always been there, but it had stayed faint, hidden, and underdeveloped. It had reacted to the First Progenitor, to the abandoned fifth end, to the Dimensional Keeper Legacy, and to Freya, but it had never fully awakened as a complete inheritance. It was like a sword buried in stone, sharp by nature but never drawn from its sheath.
Now that sheath was opening.

Freya stepped forward first. Max followed beside her. The moment both of them crossed the threshold, the enormous black door closed behind them with a deep sound, cutting off the outside chamber. The Voidwalker Ancestor stayed beyond the door, but his voice still reached the Inheritance Chamber, as if the entire place carried his will.

"Don’t resist the bloodline memories. Let them enter you. What you can inherit depends on your foundation, your bloodline purity, your soul, your comprehension, and your own path. Don’t chase everything. Let the inheritance choose what belongs to you."
Max and Freya stopped at the center of the dark crystal path. A moment later, the starry abyss below them woke up.
Boom!
Two pillars of dark silver light burst up from beneath their feet. One wrapped around Freya. One wrapped around Max.

Freya’s eyes closed almost immediately, and a powerful Voidwalker aura surged out of her body. Her silver-white hair lifted without any wind, and countless small dimensional rings formed around her like halos.
She’d already cultivated the Voidwalker bloodline for years, but even for her, this inheritance felt different. The moment it entered her, her aura turned purer, deeper, and more complete.
Max also closed his eyes as the inheritance entered his body. It didn’t feel like ordinary energy. It felt like memories made of blood.

Ancient Voidwalker scriptures appeared in his mind. Dimensional seals, spatial folding arts, hidden world construction methods, bloodline movement techniques, and secret combat footwork poured into him like a river flowing out of a forgotten era.

He saw ancestors stepping through battlefield cracks, warriors hiding entire armies inside pocket dimensions, assassins striking from impossible distances, elders sealing off worlds between breaths, and children of the clan training in front of the dark star symbol.
Then the bloodline inheritance reached deeper. It touched his own foundation. The Voidwalker blood inside him woke up.
For a moment, Max felt like an invisible door had opened in his veins. Power that had been asleep since birth started flowing through his body.

chapters.title: Chapter 1987: Into the Law Manifestation Realm!
paragraphs: It didn’t clash with his other bloodlines.

The Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline stayed wild and ancient. The Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline stayed radiant and noble. The Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline stayed vast and close to the laws of the world. But the Voidwalker bloodline moved differently from all of them.
It didn’t roar. It opened paths.
His body suddenly felt full of doors, layers, corridors, and hidden spaces. His Dimensional Sovereign Body reacted first, resonating so violently that the entire inheritance pillar around him shook.

The Dimensional Keeper Legacy, which had stayed quiet since the First Progenitor’s test, stirred again, but this time it didn’t push back against the Voidwalker inheritance. It watched, accepted it, and let it settle in, as if the bloodline inheritance were a smaller branch returning to a much larger tree.
Max’s aura began rising. At first, the change came slowly. Then it turned terrifying.

His cultivation, sitting at the 6th level of the Law Refinement Realm, started loosening up. The energy from the inheritance didn’t behave like ordinary spiritual power. It was extremely pure, carrying bloodline source energy, dimensional law resonance, and ancestral will. It didn’t just pour into his realm. It refined the framework of his laws, widened his foundation, and pushed his cultivation upward with an almost frightening smoothness.
[Law Refinement Realm 7th Level]

Max’s aura expanded. The dark crystal path beneath his feet trembled. The inheritance rings around him rotated faster, and several ancient Voidwalker scriptures broke apart into streams of light before sinking into his body.
[Law Refinement Realm 8th Level]

The starry abyss below the path stirred. Silver rings formed around Max’s body, layer upon layer, as if multiple hidden dimensions were being born around him. His understanding of space, distance, concealment, and dimensional passage deepened rapidly. What he’d once grasped through the Dimensional Sovereign Body and the Dimensional Keeper Legacy now had the foundation of an actual bloodline system behind it.
[Law Refinement Realm 9th Level]

The Inheritance Chamber shook. Freya, still absorbing her own inheritance, opened her eyes slightly and glanced at Max. Even though she’d expected him to gain a lot, watching his cultivation climb this fast still made surprise flash across her eyes. But she soon closed her eyes again, since her own inheritance was reaching a critical point too.
[Law Refinement Realm 10th Level]
Max’s aura reached the peak of the Law Refinement Realm. The laws around him began to tremble.
Normally, breaking into the Law Manifestation Realm wasn’t a simple thing. It wasn’t just about piling up energy.

A cultivator had to refine their laws to the point where they could manifest outward, forming a true law image, a visible law phenomenon, or a manifestation that could directly influence the world. Plenty of geniuses got stuck at the peak of the Law Refinement Realm for years because their foundation wasn’t complete enough to support a stable manifestation.

But Max was different. His foundation ran too deep. The Emotion Severing Path, Divine King Punishment, the Devouring Flames Domain, the Dimensional Sovereign Body, the Dimension of Soul, the Dimension of Light, the Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline, the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline, the five Divine Veins, Dragonheart, and now the Voidwalker bloodline inheritance had all pushed his foundation to a terrifying level.
He didn’t lack laws. He had too many of them.
The moment he hit the peak of the Law Refinement Realm, the barrier to the Law Manifestation Realm appeared in front of him. Then it cracked.
Outside the Inheritance Chamber, the Voidwalker Ancestor suddenly lifted his head, his expression shifting.
"This..."
The next instant, a terrifying roar of laws erupted from inside the Inheritance Chamber.
Boom!
The entire abandoned Voidwalker end shook. Then the entire First Progenitor Arena shook. Then the entire hidden domain of the Five Sacred Clans trembled.

In the Bloodline Legacy Battle arena, the Four Sacred Clans had been preparing emergency reinforcements for the Veyrith Star Realm. Spatial gates were glowing, sacred response teams were gathering, and elders were shouting urgent orders. But the moment Max’s breakthrough aura erupted, everyone froze and turned toward the abandoned fifth end.
The dark star above the Voidwalker platform blazed brighter than it ever had. A pillar of light tore into the sky. Inside that pillar, laws began manifesting one after another.

First came space. The sky above the arena folded into countless transparent layers. Doors appeared in the air, each one leading to a different hidden distance. Silver rings rotated around them, each carrying the aura of the Voidwalker bloodline.

Then came emotion. An invisible sword light passed through the sky, and for a brief instant, countless people felt their anger, fear, hatred, pride, and killing intent go strangely still. It wasn’t suppression by force. It was severance. The Emotion Severing Path manifested as a pale, invisible sword shadow hanging in the sky like a blade aimed at the heart of every living being below.

Then came punishment. Seven-colored lightning gathered out of nothing and formed the vague image of a divine tribunal above the arena. A throne appeared inside the thunder, vast and solemn, as if some ancient law of judgment had come down to inspect everyone below.

Then came black flames. A dark domain opened up behind the lightning. Devouring flames surged inside it, swallowing stray energy from the air and turning the edges of the sky black. The flames didn’t spread recklessly, but their hunger still made even the elders uneasy.

Then came dragon law. A massive black dragon shadow appeared behind the pillar of light, coiling through the sky with chaotic golden patterns across its scales. It opened its eyes and released a silent pressure that made the beast-blooded descendants and dragon-related cultivators in the sacred domain tremble.

Then came light. A radiant white-gold glow spread across one side of the sky, not quite the same as the Valerius sacred sun, but purer, softer, and noble in a different way. The Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline manifested briefly as a domain of dawn-like light that made several Evercrest and Valerius elders stare at it in astonishment.

Then came soul. The sky seemed to sink into a boundless inner world. A vast, silent dimension appeared faintly behind Max’s breakthrough aura, so deep and empty that even the Ravenhart ancestor’s eyes changed. Soul attacks, soul perception, and fate-like observation all felt small next to that silent dimension.

Then came resilience, vitality, origin, speed, and strength. Five divine vein shadows appeared around the pillar of light like five ancient channels carved into the body of heaven itself. One stabilized the breakthrough like a world-root.

sentences.text: It didn’t clash with his other bloodlines.
The Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline stayed wild and ancient.
The Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline stayed radiant and noble.
The Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline stayed vast and close to the laws of the world.
But the Voidwalker bloodline moved differently from all of them.
It didn’t roar.
It opened paths.
His body suddenly felt full of doors, layers, corridors, and hidden spaces.
His Dimensional Sovereign Body reacted first, resonating so violently that the entire inheritance pillar around him shook.
The Dimensional Keeper Legacy, which had stayed quiet since the First Progenitor’s test, stirred again, but this time it didn’t push back against the Voidwalker inheritance.
It watched, accepted it, and let it settle in, as if the bloodline inheritance were a smaller branch returning to a much larger tree.
Max’s aura began rising.
At first, the change came slowly.
Then it turned terrifying.
His cultivation, sitting at the 6th level of the Law Refinement Realm, started loosening up.
The energy from the inheritance didn’t behave like ordinary spiritual power.
It was extremely pure, carrying bloodline source energy, dimensional law resonance, and ancestral will.
It didn’t just pour into his realm.
It refined the framework of his laws, widened his foundation, and pushed his cultivation upward with an almost frightening smoothness.
[Law Refinement Realm 7th Level]
Max’s aura expanded.
The dark crystal path beneath his feet trembled.
The inheritance rings around him rotated faster, and several ancient Voidwalker scriptures broke apart into streams of light before sinking into his body.
[Law Refinement Realm 8th Level]
The starry abyss below the path stirred.
Silver rings formed around Max’s body, layer upon layer, as if multiple hidden dimensions were being born around him.
His understanding of space, distance, concealment, and dimensional passage deepened rapidly.
What he’d once grasped through the Dimensional Sovereign Body and the Dimensional Keeper Legacy now had the foundation of an actual bloodline system behind it.
[Law Refinement Realm 9th Level]
The Inheritance Chamber shook.
Freya, still absorbing her own inheritance, opened her eyes slightly and glanced at Max.
Even though she’d expected him to gain a lot, watching his cultivation climb this fast still made surprise flash across her eyes.
But she soon closed her eyes again, since her own inheritance was reaching a critical point too.
[Law Refinement Realm 10th Level]
Max’s aura reached the peak of the Law Refinement Realm.
The laws around him began to tremble.
Normally, breaking into the Law Manifestation Realm wasn’t a simple thing.
It wasn’t just about piling up energy.
A cultivator had to refine their laws to the point where they could manifest outward, forming a true law image, a visible law phenomenon, or a manifestation that could directly influence the world.
Plenty of geniuses got stuck at the peak of the Law Refinement Realm for years because their foundation wasn’t complete enough to support a stable manifestation.
But Max was different.
His foundation ran too deep.

The Emotion Severing Path, Divine King Punishment, the Devouring Flames Domain, the Dimensional Sovereign Body, the Dimension of Soul, the Dimension of Light, the Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline, the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline, the five Divine Veins, Dragonheart, and now the Voidwalker bloodline inheritance had all pushed his foundation to a terrifying level.
He didn’t lack laws.
He had too many of them.
The moment he hit the peak of the Law Refinement Realm, the barrier to the Law Manifestation Realm appeared in front of him.
Then it cracked.
Outside the Inheritance Chamber, the Voidwalker Ancestor suddenly lifted his head, his expression shifting.
"This..."
The next instant, a terrifying roar of laws erupted from inside the Inheritance Chamber.
Boom!
The entire abandoned Voidwalker end shook.
Then the entire First Progenitor Arena shook.
Then the entire hidden domain of the Five Sacred Clans trembled.
In the Bloodline Legacy Battle arena, the Four Sacred Clans had been preparing emergency reinforcements for the Veyrith Star Realm.
Spatial gates were glowing, sacred response teams were gathering, and elders were shouting urgent orders.
But the moment Max’s breakthrough aura erupted, everyone froze and turned toward the abandoned fifth end.
The dark star above the Voidwalker platform blazed brighter than it ever had.
A pillar of light tore into the sky.
Inside that pillar, laws began manifesting one after another.
First came space.
The sky above the arena folded into countless transparent layers.
Doors appeared in the air, each one leading to a different hidden distance.
Silver rings rotated around them, each carrying the aura of the Voidwalker bloodline.
Then came emotion.

chapters.title: Chapter 1988 - 1st level of Law Manifestation Realm!
paragraphs: One poured endless life force into the manifestation. One moved like a flash across every law phenomenon. One carried raw physical might that shook the arena floor. The last stood like an indestructible wall, holding off pressure from every direction.
And above all of them, faint but terrifying, the Primordial Bloodline pulsed. The laws of the world drew closer, and every manifestation became clearer, stronger, and more complete.
The entire Five Sacred Clan domain shook under the breakthrough. Not just the arena. The Valerius platform trembled, and sacred flames bent toward the sky as if acknowledging a higher law reaction.

The Ashbourne platform cracked in several places, and blood-iron battle marks lit up defensively. The Ravenhart shadows scattered and reformed, unable to decide whether to hide or watch. The Evercrest spatial layers rippled violently, and several sealed gardens inside the hidden domain opened by themselves for a brief moment.
The abandoned Voidwalker end roared with starry light, as if after countless years of silence, it had finally watched a descendant step into a realm worth announcing.
The younger geniuses of the Four Sacred Clans stared in disbelief.

Cassian Valerius stood frozen, his eyes reflecting the seven-colored lightning, the black flames, the spatial doors, the dragon shadow, and the silent soul law above the sky. He’d seen plenty of breakthroughs into the Law Manifestation Realm. As the Sun-Crowned Heir of Valerius, he’d even caused a grand manifestation himself when he broke into that realm.
But compared to this, his own breakthrough had been simple.
Draven Ashbourne’s face filled with rare shock. "How many laws does this guy cultivate?"
No one answered him.
Seraphine Ravenhart’s silver-purple eyes trembled slightly. "Not just laws. Pseudo Cosmic Paths, bloodline laws, body laws, soul laws, and a bunch of others. They’re all manifesting together."
Aelric Evercrest, who’d once bragged that Max wouldn’t have dominated the Cosmic Ascension Conference if the Four Sacred Clan heirs had taken part, now sat pale and speechless.
He’d already lost to Max before this breakthrough. And now Max had entered the Law Manifestation Realm.

The four clan heads looked even uglier. The Evercrest head clenched his fists so tight his wound reopened, but he didn’t even notice the blood running down his chest. The Valerius head stared at the breakthrough pillar with a stiff expression. The Ashbourne head looked like he wanted to curse out loud. The Ravenhart head stayed silent, but deep caution showed in her eyes.
The four sacred ancestors looked shaken too.
"This isn’t a normal Law Manifestation breakthrough," the Valerius ancestor said in a low voice.
The Ashbourne ancestor’s expression darkened. "Normal? Even the word monster doesn’t cover this."
The Ravenhart ancestor whispered, "The laws aren’t fighting each other. They’re in harmony. That’s the terrifying part."

The Evercrest ancestor looked toward the abandoned fifth end with a grim face. "This kid is monstrous, to put it lightly. And with the Primordial Bloodline and now the Voidwalker Bloodline both truly awake, I don’t think any young genius in the Divine Realm could stand up to him."

Inside the Inheritance Chamber, Max felt the barrier shatter. His laws no longer stayed refined only inside his body. They manifested outward. Every path he carried gained a visible form and deeper authority.

His entire foundation seemed to expand from an internal world into something that could directly touch reality. The Voidwalker inheritance flowed through him, filling in a missing layer in his bloodline and giving his dimensional understanding a proper ancestral foundation.
Then his cultivation broke through.
[Breakthrough Successful.]
[Law Manifestation Realm 1st Level.]
Max opened his eyes. The moment he did, the countless law manifestations above the Five Sacred Clan domain trembled once more before slowly starting to withdraw.

But even after they faded, the shock they’d caused didn’t go away. The entire Five Sacred Clan domain stayed silent. Even the emergency teams preparing to rush toward the devil attack had stopped for a few breaths, staring up at the sky with wide eyes.
The Voidwalker Ancestor stood outside the Inheritance Chamber, his old face filled with emotion.
"He really broke through."
His voice came out soft.
"He reached the Law Manifestation Realm."

Inside the chamber, Max slowly raised his hand. Silver Voidwalker rings appeared faintly around his wrist before fading away. His aura felt much stronger than before, but more importantly, it felt more complete. The Voidwalker bloodline that had once slept inside him had finally woken up properly, and the inheritance had given it a real direction.

Freya opened her eyes not far away. Her aura had also grown deeper and purer. The Voidwalker inheritance had refined her bloodline, strengthened her foundation, and given her access to techniques she’d never had before. But even she looked at Max with a complicated expression.
"You really know how to make noise," she said.
Max looked at her and smiled faintly. "I was told to reach the Law Manifestation Realm."
Freya stared at him for a moment. Then she shook her head, though a faint warmth showed in her eyes.
Outside the chamber, the Voidwalker Ancestor’s voice came through again.
"Good. Both of you keep absorbing what you can. The inheritance won’t stay open forever."
Max closed his eyes again. But this time, his foundation was different.
He was no longer at the Law Refinement Realm. He had stepped into the Law Manifestation Realm.
Max then began focusing on understanding the inheritance of the Voidwalker Bloodline. Just like that, a month went by.
"There are so many techniques and moves in the Voidwalker Bloodline inheritance," Max muttered as he stood up. "And any single one of them could pass as a sacred art even for a first-rate force."
It was at that moment Max finally understood why the Four Sacred Clans stood above every first-rate force in the Divine Realm.
When he reached the exit door, he found Freya already waiting there.
"Done comprehending the inheritance?" Freya asked, curious.
Max nodded. "It was vast, but not impossible."
He looked at her and added, "I’m surprised you finished before me."
