chapters.title: Chapter 1989: Another Summon to the Primordial Race!
paragraphs: Freya raised her brows with a cheeky smile. "Well, I’m your big sister after all. Of course I’d learn faster than you."

Her expression turned a bit more serious as she went on. "Jokes aside, I’m way more powerful than you, and my understanding of laws runs a lot deeper than yours right now. It only makes sense I’d comprehend the inheritance faster."
Max got curious hearing that and couldn’t help but ask, "What’s your cultivation realm?"
Honestly, he couldn’t sense her strength at all.
"I’ve recovered my old strength and gone past it," Freya said with a smile. "Right now, I’m at the Holy Lord Realm."
Max’s eyes went wide.
Holy Lord Realm. If he remembered right, that sat two full realms above his own. Law Manifestation Realm, Divine Lord Realm, Divine King Realm, and then Holy Lord Realm.
In that moment, Max realized just how big the gap really was between him and his sister. She was way more powerful than he’d ever imagined.
"Don’t look so shocked, Maxy," Freya said with a smile. "I’m older than you, so of course my cultivation sits higher. Don’t overthink it."
With that, she opened the door to the Inheritance Chamber and walked out. Max nodded and followed her.
The Voidwalker Ancestor was already waiting for them outside.
"Good," he said, nodding as he sensed the awakened Voidwalker Bloodline aura in both of them.
Then he added, "Max, the Primordial Race has summoned you. An envoy is waiting outside for you."
Max frowned. "Another summon?"
The Voidwalker Ancestor nodded with a sigh. "Things have taken a turn for the worse across the Divine Realm."
"The devils?" Max asked, frowning again.

The Voidwalker Ancestor nodded. "That last attack you heard about wasn’t the only one. It looks like the devils have found a way into our universe, and because of that, there’ve already been several attacks across the Divine Realm. I think another war might be about to break out between the devils and the people of this universe."
Max and Freya both turned solemn hearing that.

"Max, go ahead and report to the Primordial Race," the Voidwalker Ancestor said calmly. "I believe they’ve already planned something for the growth of all the top geniuses in the Divine Realm. Don’t waste this chance."

Max nodded solemnly. Now that he understood the devils had truly invaded their universe, he knew a war could break out at any moment. He hadn’t forgotten the scene on Orion, where the war between the devils and the Primordials had once played out. Something like that could easily happen again in the Divine Realm.
"Go on," Freya said, smiling.
Max nodded, but he hesitated over something. "About mother and father..."

"Don’t worry about them," Freya cut in. "Now that I’ve come to the Four Sacred Clans, I’m not leaving anytime soon. My team will join me here in a few days too. After that, I’ll do everything I can to free the members of the Voidwalker Clan from the seal. Once that’s done, we’ll have an army ready to move against the elves."
She sighed. "But it’ll take time. I don’t think the four clans are in any mood to break the seal on our Voidwalker Clan right now."
Max understood.

"In the meantime, I want you to push your strength up as fast as you can," Freya said solemnly. "At your current level, thinking about waging war against the elves is basically suicide. You know that, right?"
Max nodded in understanding.
Freya then stepped forward and hugged him. "Now go, Maxy. Next time you come back to the Four Sacred Clans, it’ll be time to wipe those elves off the Divine Realm."
Max hugged her back tightly.
A moment later, they let go of each other.
Max looked at Freya. "I’ll see you soon."
With that, he turned and headed toward the exit of the Voidwalker Clan.
Once Max was gone, the Voidwalker Ancestor turned to Freya, his expression calm. "Do you really intend to wage war against the elves?"
Freya nodded, her expression turning cold. "Not just wage war. I want to wipe out every single one of them from the Divine Realm."
An aura of slaughter radiated off her body in that moment.
The Voidwalker Ancestor looked at her for a long moment, then said calmly, "Well, anything’s possible when you’re a Voidwalker."
Meanwhile, Max appeared outside the gate of the Voidwalker Clan and saw a figure waiting for him. It was Sarvion, the same envoy who’d picked him up from the Black Dragon Clan.
"How should I address you?" Max asked, walking over. "Sarvion, Sir Sarvion, or something else you’d prefer?"
Sarvion smiled politely. "Just call me Sarvion."

As he said it, he tapped Max on the shoulder, and the world around Max changed. This time, Max could see they were flying through some kind of space vortex. Only a few seconds later, they arrived at the Primordial Ancestral Domain.
"That was fast," Max muttered before turning to Sarvion. "How’d you do that? Is that some cosmic path or law you’ve comprehended?"

Sarvion smiled. "No laws or cosmic paths involved. Once you’re as strong as me, you can cut through space to travel long distances. And for people carrying Primordial Race bloodline, it’s even easier."
He added, "Since you already have a Tier 4 bloodline from our race, it’s only a matter of time before you can do this too."
Max nodded lightly as they started walking. "How’s the situation in the Divine Realm? I heard another war might break out between the devils and our world."

Sarvion’s expression turned solemn. "The situation isn’t looking good. The devils have somehow found a way into our universe after all these years. If I’m not wrong, things are only going to get worse from here."

Max’s expression hardened. He thought for a moment before asking, "About the Black Dragon Clan, they’re just a third-rate force, but since they’re the first force I joined in the Divine Realm, I care about them a lot. Can the Primordial Race send some protectors to look after the Black Dragon Clan?"

Sarvion answered without looking back. "You don’t need to worry about the Black Dragon Clan. Now that you’ve become a Primordial, every force you’re connected to falls under the Primordial Race, which means they’re under our protection at all times."
Max nodded, relieved to hear that.
A moment later, Max arrived at a hall where the other top geniuses were already standing, waiting.

Is that some cosmic path or law you’ve comprehended?"
Sarvion smiled.
"No laws or cosmic paths involved.
Once you’re as strong as me, you can cut through space to travel long distances.
And for people carrying Primordial Race bloodline, it’s even easier."
He added, "Since you already have a Tier 4 bloodline from our race, it’s only a matter of time before you can do this too."
Max nodded lightly as they started walking.
"How’s the situation in the Divine Realm?
I heard another war might break out between the devils and our world."
Sarvion’s expression turned solemn.
"The situation isn’t looking good.
The devils have somehow found a way into our universe after all these years.
If I’m not wrong, things are only going to get worse from here."
Max’s expression hardened.
He thought for a moment before asking, "About the Black Dragon Clan, they’re just a third-rate force, but since they’re the first force I joined in the Divine Realm, I care about them a lot.
Can the Primordial Race send some protectors to look after the Black Dragon Clan?"
Sarvion answered without looking back.
"You don’t need to worry about the Black Dragon Clan.
Now that you’ve become a Primordial, every force you’re connected to falls under the Primordial Race, which means they’re under our protection at all times."
Max nodded, relieved to hear that.
A moment later, Max arrived at a hall where the other top geniuses were already standing, waiting.

chapters.title: Chapter 1990: A Week of Time!
paragraphs: "So, everyone is here," Max said as his gaze moved across the hall.

The others had already gathered inside the wide chamber, and even Aurelian had appeared among them. His presence made Max’s eyes pause for a brief moment, but he did not say anything about it. The atmosphere in the hall was already strange enough without him adding more tension.
Orion leaned back against the wall and grinned the moment he saw Max. "You sure took your sweet time getting here."
Max smiled a little awkwardly. "I was in seclusion. I did not even know I had been summoned."
"It is good that you still arrived in time," Rosaline said, her expression unusually solemn.

Max nodded to her, then looked around the hall once more. Aside from the top geniuses, he did not see any Primordials present. There were no elders, no envoys, and no guards standing nearby. When he glanced behind him, he also noticed that Sarvion had already disappeared without a sound.
"Does anyone know what this summons is about?" Max asked, his curiosity growing.
Damian frowned. "No one has told us anything. We have already been waiting here for a full day, yet no one has appeared to explain the situation."
"A whole day?" Max’s frown deepened when he heard that.
Ervin crossed his arms and spoke in a calm voice. "From what we were told, we were supposed to wait for only a few hours while some preparation was being arranged for us."
The group exchanged glances after hearing that, and the uneasiness in the hall became even heavier.

Morgana let out a light sneer. "I think this is nonsense. The Primordials are clearly trying to hide something from us. It is suspicious enough that they summoned us here without explanation, but making us wait this long without showing themselves makes it even more suspicious."
Revona, who had been quietly leaning against a wall until now, finally opened her eyes and spoke. "You are all too impatient. Calm down and wait as instructed. What is the hurry?"
Kaiden, standing beside her, nodded. "I think Revona is right. Let us wait a few more hours before anyone does anything foolish."
"Fine, we will wait," Max said with a shrug.
He walked to a corner of the hall and sat down against the wall. The Primordials had summoned the ten of them, but they had not even prepared chairs or tables for them.
That small detail made the situation feel even stranger, as though the summons had been issued in a hurry or the Primordials simply had no intention of making them comfortable.
Another day passed like that.
By then, even Revona and Ervin, who were usually far calmer than the others, had begun to show signs of impatience.
Then, without warning, a massive rumble tore through the hall.
The entire chamber shook.
Orion instantly sprang to his feet, his grin vanishing as he entered a defensive stance. "What was that?"
Another rumble followed almost immediately, louder and deeper than the first.
Max stood up as well, his expression turning serious. "Is that a battle?"
Rakan’s eyes widened slightly. "Who would dare attack the Primordials?"
Damian’s face turned cold. "Devils?"
A third rumble echoed across the Primordial Ancestral Domain, and this time, the walls themselves trembled as if the impact had come from somewhere close.
Ervin had already started moving toward the exit. "Let us go see what is happening."
Damian followed him without hesitation.
"Let us go," Max said as his aura stirred, and he flew out with them.

Revona, Morgana, Kaiden, Orion, Rakan, Rosaline, Aurelian, and the others followed soon after. None of them knew what was happening outside, but all of them understood one thing clearly. If someone had truly attacked the Primordial Race inside their own ancestral domain, then the situation was far more serious than a delayed summons.
When they arrived outside the Primordial Ancestral Domain, they saw two groups facing each other across the sky.
On one side stood the Primordials.

At their front were the four Primarchs, their auras vast and terrifying even while restrained. Behind them stood many other powerful Primordials, each one carrying a pressure far beyond what ordinary Divine Realm experts could release.
On the other side stood a group of beings that looked somewhat similar to demons, yet were clearly not ordinary demons.

Their bodies were taller and more muscular than most demons, and strange tattoos covered them from head to toe. Those tattoos resembled Infernal Demon Tattoos, but they were more ancient, more savage, and far more oppressive. The markings seemed to grow from the two glowing horns on top of their heads, spreading downward across their faces, necks, chests, arms, and legs like living brands of destruction.
Max’s eyes narrowed.
They were devils.

The one standing at the front of the devils was not an old warlord covered in scars, nor was he a brutish monster releasing endless killing intent. Instead, he looked young. His face was handsome in a cruel and vicious way, and his body was wrapped in a calm confidence that made him seem even more dangerous than the devils behind him.
"So, what will it be?" the young devil asked, his voice carrying clearly across the sky. "A war that wipes out your entire universe, or will you meet our demands?"
The Primordials became quiet after hearing him.

They were not truly silent, however. Max could feel faint fluctuations of divine transmission passing between the four Primarchs and the other high-ranking Primordials. Clearly, they were discussing the matter privately while keeping their expressions calm on the surface.
After a moment, one of the four Primarchs stepped forward.
"Varok," he said in a steady voice, "we need some time to consider this matter. How about this? We will hold a meeting one week from today, and we will discuss your terms then. What do you say?"
Varok, the young devil, sneered.
He did not answer immediately. Instead, his gaze moved across the faces of the Primordials one by one, as if he was memorizing their expressions.

"You Primordials are always like this," he said. "Stalling for time again and again. Last time, the war ended peacefully because of an unforeseen variable, but I am quite sure this time will not end the same way."
His sneer deepened.
"Anyway, take your time if you want. Just do not think one week will change anything. If it even matters at all."
The moment he finished speaking, the space around the devils twisted.
Then all of them vanished.
The sky fell silent.

chapters.title: Chapter 1991: Lesser Beings!
paragraphs: Only after the devils disappeared did the four Primarchs let out faint sighs.
Arvantos, one of the Primarchs, glanced behind him and said, "You children can come out now."
Max, Damian, Ervin, and the others stepped out from where they had been standing. Their expressions were dark because none of them had missed the conversation between the devils and the Primordials.
"Were those devils?" Orion asked with a frown.
"Are they declaring war on us?" Ervin asked.
Damian’s eyes were cold. "What demands were they talking about?"
The others began asking questions as well, and in only a few breaths, Arvantos was surrounded by the confusion and pressure of the top geniuses.
Only Max and Revona remained silent.
Max was thinking about the sudden appearance of the devils, while Revona watched Arvantos with a calm gaze that suggested she might already know more than the rest of them.
"I will explain everything," Arvantos said. "Give me a moment."
He then turned toward the other three Primarchs.
"I will return after I brief them. It is time they knew the truth."
The other three Primarchs nodded. Soon after, they vanished along with the rest of the Primordials, leaving only Arvantos and the ten geniuses behind.
"Follow me," Arvantos said.
Without waiting for further questions, he turned and walked back into the Primordial Ancestral Domain.

The ten geniuses followed him into a different hall. Unlike the previous chamber where they had been forced to wait without explanation, this hall was solemn and ancient. Strange symbols covered the walls, and a massive star map floated above the center of the room. Countless points of light moved within it, some bright, some dim, and some surrounded by faint crimson marks.
Arvantos stopped beneath the star map and turned to face them.
"What do you all know about the last war between the races?" he asked.
Orion blinked. "Nothing?"
Revona spoke right after him. "That we almost lost."
Rakan frowned as if trying to recall something. "I heard some elders mention that it happened on a planet called Orion, or something like that."

Arvantos nodded slowly. "The last time that war happened, we very nearly lost everything. It shook the entire universe. Both the Divine Realm and the Mortal Realm were pushed to the edge of destruction because of those devils."
He sighed, and for the first time, the ten geniuses saw a trace of exhaustion on the face of a Primarch.
"It was only because of a miracle that the last war ended peacefully."
Max looked at him and asked, "What caused the war? What do the devils actually want from our universe?"
Arvantos looked at Max and smiled faintly.
"That is a good question."
He turned his gaze toward the whole group.
"Before I explain that, I must first tell you something about what exists beyond our universe."
The moment Arvantos said those words, the expressions of the ten geniuses changed.
Beyond their universe.

None of them had ever seriously thought about such a thing before. Some had been born in the Divine Realm, while others had climbed up from the Mortal Realm, but all of them had grown up believing that their universe was the highest stage they could reach.

They knew the Divine Realm was vast beyond imagination, and they knew the Mortal Realm contained countless worlds, but the idea that something existed beyond the universe itself was enough to shake even their powerful minds.
In that instant, every one of them focused fully on Arvantos.
Whatever he was about to say next would not only explain the devils.
It might also change their understanding of the entire world they lived in.
Arvantos looked at the ten geniuses for a moment before he began speaking.
"Our Primordial Race is not the only first race beyond this universe. In fact, apart from us Primordials, there are four other races that exist outside our universe."
The hall fell into silence.
"Four other races..." Orion muttered, his expression slowly changing.

The ten geniuses were visibly shocked. Until this moment, most of them had only known about devils through old records, ancient warnings, and the sudden confrontation they had just witnessed outside the Primordial Ancestral Domain. They had never imagined that beyond their own universe, there were not only devils, but four completely different first races standing on a similar level as the Primordial Race.
Arvantos did not look surprised by their reaction.
To these young geniuses, the Divine Realm was already unimaginably vast. The Mortal Realm below it contained countless worlds, planets, star fields, and civilizations.

For most cultivators, even the Divine Realm alone was too large to fully explore in a lifetime. Yet now, Arvantos had casually told them that their entire universe was not the only one, and that beyond its boundaries existed other universes ruled by other first races.
That truth was enough to overturn the understanding they had carried since birth.

Arvantos continued in a calm but serious voice. "Demons and elves also came from special racial origins, but they are not on the same level as the five first races. Their relationship to those higher races is somewhat similar to the relationship between humans and Primordials. In a certain sense, they are lesser beings."
He did not soften his words at all.

The moment he said this, several geniuses became quiet. Max’s eyes moved slightly, especially because of his connection to the elves through his mother’s side and the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline.
However, he did not interrupt Arvantos. He could tell that Arvantos was not speaking with contempt for the sake of contempt. He was explaining the cosmic hierarchy as the Primordials understood it.

"To put it more clearly," Arvantos said, "demons and elves may be powerful races within certain worlds, realms, and civilizations, but their racial foundation does not place them at the peak of existence. Their strongest members may become terrifying experts, and their bloodlines may possess unique powers, but their origin is still not equal to that of the first races. The first races are different. They were not merely born as inhabitants of a universe. Their existence is tied to the structure, laws, and ancient order beyond ordinary worlds."
The expressions of the ten geniuses became even more serious.

chapters.title: Chapter 1992: Five Races!
paragraphs: Arvantos then said, "I will explain the details about demons and elves later. For now, you only need to understand the five first races. Aside from us Primordials, there is the Devil Race, the Spirit Race, the Angel Race, and lastly, the Dragon Race."
The names echoed through the hall.
Devil Race.
Spirit Race.
Angel Race.
Dragon Race.

To the ten geniuses, each name carried an invisible pressure. The Devil Race had already appeared before them, arrogant enough to stand in front of the four Primarchs and threaten the entire universe. If the Devil Race was only one of the other four first races, then it was difficult to imagine how powerful the remaining three could be.

Arvantos raised his hand, and the star map above the hall shifted. Four enormous shadows appeared around the image of their universe. One was dark and crimson, burning with the aura of slaughter and conquest.

One was pale green and silver, filled with life, nature, and spiritual light. One was bright and vast, surrounded by rings of sacred radiance. The last was immense and ancient, carrying the faint outline of coiling dragons whose bodies seemed large enough to wrap around stars.
"Among those four races," Arvantos continued, "the Angel Race and the Dragon Race are the most threatening to us."
Everyone immediately focused on him.

"During the last war, the Devil Race was the one that directly invaded our universe, but the situation could have been much worse. At that time, the Angel Race and the Dragon Race were locked in a conflict of their own. Their attention was elsewhere, and they had no reason to spend their forces on us. That was our fortune."
His tone became heavier.
"If the Angel Race and the Dragon Race had entered the war at the same time as the Devil Race, then we would have surely lost. There is no need to dress it up with pride. That is the truth."
The hall became still.
No one mocked him. No one questioned him. No one thought he was exaggerating.
Arvantos was a Primarch. If someone like him was willing to say that the Primordial Race would have lost, then the threat of the Angel Race and Dragon Race had to be almost unimaginable.
Max’s gaze sharpened slightly.
The Dragon Race caught his attention more than the others.

His Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline was already one of his strongest foundations. It had given him dragon transformation, terrifying defense, chaotic dragon force, and the power of the Black Dragon Cataclysm Breath.

But now, hearing Arvantos speak of a Dragon Race beyond their universe made him wonder whether his Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline was somehow connected to that race, or whether it came from another branch entirely.
For now, he kept the question to himself.
Everyone remained silent for a while after hearing about the other four first races.
Then Max asked curiously, "Is the Spirit Race the same race that spirits came from?"
Arvantos nodded. "Yes, it is the same Spirit Race you are thinking of, but not in the simple way most people understand spirits."

He looked at Max and explained further, "The spirits you know within our universe are often incomplete manifestations of spiritual energy, nature, laws, memories, or special environments. Some are born from treasures, some from natural lands, some from ancient battlefields, and some from the lingering will of powerful beings. They may have intelligence, emotion, and even cultivation, but they are not the true first race."
Arvantos raised his hand, and the spirit-like shadow on the star map became clearer.

"The true Spirit Race beyond our universe exists in humanoid form. They have flesh, soul, bloodline, and spiritual origin. However, unlike ordinary races, their bodies are naturally close to the laws of nature and the pure forces of existence. They are born with an affinity toward life, elemental laws, soul energy, and natural order. That is why many ancient records describe them as a race blessed by gods."
He paused briefly, then corrected himself in a calmer tone.

"Of course, whether gods truly blessed them or whether it is only the blessing of nature is something no one can say with certainty. But among the five first races, the Spirit Race is indeed the one most closely aligned with balance, life, and natural law."
Ervin’s eyes brightened slightly. "Then they are not hostile?"

"Not usually," Arvantos said. "The Spirit Race is considered the most peaceful among the five first races. They do not like invasion, conquest, or meaningless slaughter. They prefer to remain within their own universe, protect their sacred lands, and avoid wars unless their survival or core interests are threatened."
His voice then turned colder.
"The Devil Race is the complete opposite."
The atmosphere shifted again.

"The Devil Race is the most hated race among the five. Their society is built around conquest, domination, bloodline hierarchy, and endless expansion. To them, invading another universe is not a moral question. It is only a matter of whether the benefits are worth the cost. They devour resources, enslave worlds, corrupt races, and turn conquered territories into war engines for future invasions."
Damian’s expression turned grim.

Arvantos looked at the young geniuses and continued, "If only the Devil Race wants to invade our universe, the situation will be dangerous, but not hopeless. Our Primordial Race, together with the top forces of the Divine Realm, can still resist them if we move properly. The true problem is whether the Angel Race and Dragon Race become involved."
Rosaline frowned. "Why would they join?"

"Because war between universes does not remain simple for long," Arvantos answered. "If the Devil Race gains something from invading us, the other races will not sit still. If we weaken too much while fighting the devils, others may see an opportunity. If the hidden secret they seek truly exists here, then every first race will eventually turn its eyes toward us."
His expression became solemn.
"So, while the devils are the ones standing at our gate right now, they may not remain our only enemy."
A heavy silence filled the hall.
After a moment, Damian asked, "Then what do the devils actually want from our universe?"
Arvantos sighed.
"That is a long story."

He looked toward the star map above them. With a wave of his hand, the image expanded again, revealing their universe at the center and four other vast cosmic forms surrounding it from different directions.

Dragon Race.

The Devil Race had already appeared before them, arrogant enough to stand in front of the four Primarchs and threaten the entire universe.
If the Devil Race was only one of the other four first races, then it was difficult to imagine how powerful the remaining three could be.
Arvantos raised his hand, and the star map above the hall shifted.
Four enormous shadows appeared around the image of their universe.
One was dark and crimson, burning with the aura of slaughter and conquest.
One was pale green and silver, filled with life, nature, and spiritual light.
One was bright and vast, surrounded by rings of sacred radiance.
The last was immense and ancient, carrying the faint outline of coiling dragons whose bodies seemed large enough to wrap around stars.
"Among those four races," Arvantos continued, "the Angel Race and the Dragon Race are the most threatening to us."
Everyone immediately focused on him.
"During the last war, the Devil Race was the one that directly invaded our universe, but the situation could have been much worse.
At that time, the Angel Race and the Dragon Race were locked in a conflict of their own.
Their attention was elsewhere, and they had no reason to spend their forces on us.
That was our fortune."
His tone became heavier.
"If the Angel Race and the Dragon Race had entered the war at the same time as the Devil Race, then we would have surely lost.
There is no need to dress it up with pride.
That is the truth."
The hall became still.
No one mocked him.
No one questioned him.
No one thought he was exaggerating.
Arvantos was a Primarch.
If someone like him was willing to say that the Primordial Race would have lost, then the threat of the Angel Race and Dragon Race had to be almost unimaginable.
Max’s gaze sharpened slightly.
The Dragon Race caught his attention more than the others.
His Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline was already one of his strongest foundations.
It had given him dragon transformation, terrifying defense, chaotic dragon force, and the power of the Black Dragon Cataclysm Breath.

But now, hearing Arvantos speak of a Dragon Race beyond their universe made him wonder whether his Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline was somehow connected to that race, or whether it came from another branch entirely.
For now, he kept the question to himself.
Everyone remained silent for a while after hearing about the other four first races.
Then Max asked curiously, "Is the Spirit Race the same race that spirits came from?"
Arvantos nodded.
"Yes, it is the same Spirit Race you are thinking of, but not in the simple way most people understand spirits."
He looked at Max and explained further, "The spirits you know within our universe are often incomplete manifestations of spiritual energy, nature, laws, memories, or special environments.
Some are born from treasures, some from natural lands, some from ancient battlefields, and some from the lingering will of powerful beings.
They may have intelligence, emotion, and even cultivation, but they are not the true first race."
Arvantos raised his hand, and the spirit-like shadow on the star map became clearer.
"The true Spirit Race beyond our universe exists in humanoid form.
They have flesh, soul, bloodline, and spiritual origin.
However, unlike ordinary races, their bodies are naturally close to the laws of nature and the pure forces of existence.
They are born with an affinity toward life, elemental laws, soul energy, and natural order.
That is why many ancient records describe them as a race blessed by gods."
He paused briefly, then corrected himself in a calmer tone.
"Of course, whether gods truly blessed them or whether it is only the blessing of nature is something no one can say with certainty.
But among the five first races, the Spirit Race is indeed the one most closely aligned with balance, life, and natural law."
Ervin’s eyes brightened slightly.
"Then they are not hostile?"
"Not usually," Arvantos said.
"The Spirit Race is considered the most peaceful among the five first races.
They do not like invasion, conquest, or meaningless slaughter.
They prefer to remain within their own universe, protect their sacred lands, and avoid wars unless their survival or core interests are threatened."
His voice then turned colder.
"The Devil Race is the complete opposite."
The atmosphere shifted again.
"The Devil Race is the most hated race among the five.
Their society is built around conquest, domination, bloodline hierarchy, and endless expansion.
To them, invading another universe is not a moral question.
It is only a matter of whether the benefits are worth the cost.
They devour resources, enslave worlds, corrupt races, and turn conquered territories into war engines for future invasions."
Damian’s expression turned grim.
Arvantos looked at the young geniuses and continued, "If only the Devil Race wants to invade our universe, the situation will be dangerous, but not hopeless.
Our Primordial Race, together with the top forces of the Divine Realm, can still resist them if we move properly.
The true problem is whether the Angel Race and Dragon Race become involved."
Rosaline frowned.
"Why would they join?"
"Because war between universes does not remain simple for long," Arvantos answered.
"If the Devil Race gains something from invading us, the other races will not sit still.
If we weaken too much while fighting the devils, others may see an opportunity.
If the hidden secret they seek truly exists here, then every first race will eventually turn its eyes toward us."
His expression became solemn.
"So, while the devils are the ones standing at our gate right now, they may not remain our only enemy."
A heavy silence filled the hall.
After a moment, Damian asked, "Then what do the devils actually want from our universe?"
Arvantos sighed.
"That is a long story."
He looked toward the star map above them.
With a wave of his hand, the image expanded again, revealing their universe at the center and four other vast cosmic forms surrounding it from different directions.

chapters.title: Chapter 1993: Primal Treasure!
paragraphs: "You should first understand the structure of the five universes," Arvantos said. "Each of the five first races exists within its own universe. We Primordials belong to this universe. The Devil Race has its own universe. The Spirit Race has its own universe. The Angel Race and Dragon Race also each occupy their own universe. In other words, apart from ours, there are four other universes outside."
The ten geniuses stared at the star map without blinking.

Arvantos continued, "The arrangement of these five universes is unusual. Our universe is positioned at the center, while the other four universes surround it. This arrangement has existed since ancient times. No one knows whether it was formed naturally or arranged by an existence beyond our understanding."
The central universe on the star map glowed faintly.

"Because of this structure, the other four races have always believed that our universe hides something special. More specifically, they believe our universe contains the entrance to a god-like realm."
"A god-like realm?" Orion asked, his voice filled with disbelief.
Arvantos nodded. "A realm beyond the five universes. A place that may contain opportunities to break through the final barrier and step into the True God Realm."
The eyes of all ten geniuses changed.
True God Realm.
Even for them, that was a realm that sounded distant and almost mythical.

Arvantos explained, "You should understand that even among the first races, reaching the peak is not the same as transcending all limitations. The so-called True God Realm is believed to be a level beyond the normal ceiling of the five universes. It is said that those who enter that realm may no longer be bound by the laws of their birth universe. They may stand above ordinary fate, lifespan, law, and cosmic restriction."
He shook his head slightly.
"But belief is not proof."
Ervin looked at him with curiosity. "Does such a place really exist in our universe?"
Arvantos sighed. "We do not know."
That answer made everyone frown.

He continued, "We have searched our entire universe for countless years. The Primordial Race searched. The ancient sacred clans searched. Other first-rate forces also searched in secret. We examined forbidden regions, ancient ruins, collapsed star realms, sealed worlds, cosmic rifts, and places where the laws behaved strangely. Yet we never found anything that could truly be called the entrance to a god realm."
His gaze became distant.

"Even during the last war, when the enemy tried to force their way toward the place they believed to be the entrance, we investigated that location thoroughly after the war ended. There was nothing there. No gate. No hidden realm. No divine passage. Nothing that could explain why the devils had been so obsessed with it."
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.

Arvantos continued, "However, that belief was enough to ignite war. The other races wanted to find the entrance first. The Devil Race wanted to seize it by force. The Angel Race and Dragon Race watched from outside, each with their own motives. The Spirit Race remained the most restrained, but even they could not completely ignore a rumor involving the True God Realm."
His voice grew heavier.
"That was the reason the great war broke out hundreds of thousands of years ago. A war that pushed both the Divine Realm and Mortal Realm to the edge of destruction."
The hall became quiet again.

Arvantos then added, "By now, I suspect the other races may have also realized that our universe may not contain the entrance they once imagined. At the very least, if it does exist, it is not something that can be found through ordinary searching or brute force. But that does not mean they will leave us alone."
Damian’s eyes were cold. "Because they already see our universe as a target."

"Exactly," Arvantos said. "Once a race invades another universe, hatred does not disappear simply because the original goal becomes uncertain. The Devil Race lost warriors during the last war. We killed many of their experts. They killed many of ours. Blood debts were formed, territories were ruined, and both sides remembered the humiliation. Even if the entrance to the God Realm is only a false legend, the devils still have reasons to return."
His expression became grim.
"And among the Devil Race, there is one being we must be especially wary of."
Max looked at him.
Arvantos said, "Devil Emperor Abaddon."
The name alone seemed to make the atmosphere in the hall colder.

"One of the leaders of the Devil Race," Arvantos continued. "A ruthless conqueror who cares nothing for life outside his own ambition. He is not the kind of ruler who invades only because of a legend. If he wants something, he will move armies to obtain it. If a world resists, he will slaughter it. If a universe blocks his path, he will try to burn through that universe until nothing remains."
His gaze swept across the ten geniuses.
"If Abaddon is behind this invasion, then we cannot assume the devils are only testing us. He may be preparing for something much larger."
The pressure in the hall became suffocating.

Arvantos looked back at the star map. "With the Devil Race making a move, and with the Angel Race and Dragon Race watching from beyond the boundaries, the long-term situation does not look good for us if war truly begins again."
Max remained silent for a moment before asking, "How did the devils enter our universe from theirs? And why now? It has been peaceful for almost a hundred thousand years. What changed?"
Arvantos turned to him.
"Our universe shares boundaries with the other four universes. That boundary is called the Wall of Eternity."
The star map changed again.

A vast translucent barrier appeared around the central universe. It was not a simple wall made of stone, metal, or energy. It looked like a cosmic membrane formed from countless layers of law, space, time, fate, and origin. It separated the five universes from one another while still allowing them to exist within the same greater cosmic structure.

"As the name suggests, the Wall of Eternity is almost eternal," Arvantos said. "Its durability is worthy of that name. Under normal circumstances, it cannot be broken by armies, ordinary treasures, or even most supreme experts. It is not only a physical barrier. It is a law boundary that prevents the universes from collapsing into one another."
He raised his hand, and a tiny point of darkness appeared on one side of the barrier.
"But almost impossible does not mean completely impossible."
Everyone stared at the point of darkness.

"With enough power, and with the help of a treasure at the level of a Primal Treasure, even the Wall of Eternity can be pierced. Not destroyed. Not shattered. Only pierced enough to create a temporary or narrow passage."
Orion swallowed. "A Primal Treasure can do that?"

Arvantos nodded. "A true Primal Treasure is not merely a powerful weapon. Each one was born from a source older than the current order of the five universes. They carry authority that can affect the structure of reality itself. If used properly, one of them can change the flow of a war. If used recklessly, it can destroy entire star regions."
He looked at the dark point on the wall.

"If I am not wrong, the devils possess one of the five Primal Treasures. They must have spent the last hundred thousand years storing energy inside it. They waited, accumulated, prepared, and concealed their movements until that treasure finally held enough power to pierce a small hole through the Wall of Eternity."
His voice became heavier with every word.
"And through that hole, the devils have invaded our universe."

chapters.title: Chapter 1994 - 500 Years of Time!
paragraphs: "So, what is the plan?" Max asked at that moment, his eyes still fixed on Arvantos. "Are we just going to let the devils invade our universe?"
The question made the hall grow quieter.

The other geniuses also looked toward Arvantos. None of them said anything, but their expressions showed that they wanted the same answer. They had just learned that the devils had pierced the Wall of Eternity, entered their universe, and even dared to stand before the Primordials to make demands. If the situation was already that serious, then waiting, negotiating, and discussing terms sounded far too passive.
Arvantos turned toward Max.
"The situation is not that simple," he said in a steady voice. "One fortunate thing about this crisis is also the very thing the devils managed to damage. I am talking about the Wall of Eternity."

The star map above the hall shifted once again, and the image of the central universe reappeared. Around it, the enormous translucent barrier shimmered with countless layers of law, space, time, and origin. On one side of that barrier was a tiny dark opening, so small that it almost looked insignificant compared to the vastness of the wall.

"The devils used one of the five Primal Treasures to pierce a hole through the Wall of Eternity," Arvantos continued. "However, piercing it is not the same as breaking it. The Wall of Eternity is still standing, and because of that, it remains our greatest safeguard."
He raised his hand toward the tiny opening in the star map.

"Right now, the hole is extremely small. It is barely stable enough to let a limited number of beings enter our universe. The stronger a being is, the greater the pressure they place on the opening. If someone above the current limit tries to cross, the passage may collapse, and the Wall of Eternity may crush them before they can fully enter."
Damian’s eyes narrowed. "What is the current limit?"

"At most, beings around the Divine King Realm can pass through," Arvantos replied. "Even then, they cannot pass in large numbers. From what we can tell, only a few hundred devils have entered so far. That number is dangerous, but it is not enough to launch a full invasion against the entire Divine Realm."
The tense atmosphere eased slightly, though no one truly relaxed.

A few hundred devils at the Divine King Realm were terrifying enough to destroy weaker star realms, but against the entire Divine Realm and the Primordial Race, that force alone would not be enough to bring about total war.

Arvantos continued, "If the devils want to send a true army, they will need to widen the hole and make the passage stable enough for stronger existences to cross. That will not be easy. Even with a Primal Treasure, the Wall of Eternity cannot be opened quickly. Based on our current judgment, it may take them around five hundred years to create a large enough breach for a proper invasion army."
He sighed softly.

"Five hundred years is not much, especially for beings at our level. But it is still time. Time to prepare. Time to gather forces. Time to strengthen the younger generation. Time to investigate their methods and search for a way to seal the breach before it grows."
The ten geniuses became silent after hearing this.

Five hundred years sounded like an enormous amount of time to mortals, but to cultivators in the Divine Realm, it was frighteningly short. Some elders spent longer than that in a single seclusion. Some inheritances took thousands of years to mature. For a universe that might have to prepare for a war of survival, five hundred years was only a brief pause before the storm.
Revona, who had been quiet until then, finally asked, "What are the devils’ conditions?"
Arvantos looked at her.

Revona continued calmly, "From what I understood, they also do not want to start a war immediately. If they were confident in attacking right now, they would not have bothered making demands. They are looking for something else."
Arvantos nodded. "Your judgment is correct."
His gaze moved across the group.

"It is not easy for the devils to start a war against our universe right now. As I said, only a small group has crossed through the opening. We do not know when another group will be able to enter, and we do not know how much energy their Primal Treasure must accumulate before the passage stabilizes again. If they attack recklessly now, the few devils already inside our universe may be wiped out before reinforcements can arrive."
Orion frowned. "Then why not just wipe them out?"
"Because doing so may start the very war we are trying to delay," Arvantos replied.
The hall grew quiet again.
Arvantos’s expression became colder. "The most troublesome part is not the few hundred devils. It is the young devil you saw earlier. His name is Varok, and he is the son of Devil Emperor Abaddon."
The expressions of the geniuses changed.

They had already heard Arvantos describe Abaddon as one of the leaders of the Devil Race, a ruthless conqueror who would slaughter entire worlds to obtain what he wanted. If Varok was his son, then killing him would not be a simple military decision. It would become a direct provocation against one of the most dangerous beings beyond their universe.

Arvantos said, "If we kill Varok here, Abaddon will not treat it as the loss of a small scouting force. He will treat it as humiliation and blood debt. He may abandon caution and pour everything he has into forcing the breach open, even if doing so damages his own side. A ruler like him will not allow his son to be killed in another universe without consequence."
Kaiden frowned. "So both sides are restrained."

"Exactly," Arvantos said. "The devils cannot start a full war right away because their forces inside our universe are too limited. We cannot simply kill all of them because doing so may force Abaddon to retaliate before we are ready. In a way, neither side truly wants an immediate war."
Max’s eyes darkened slightly.
That kind of balance was unstable.
It was not peace.
It was only two enemies standing at the edge of a blade, each waiting for the other to make the wrong move.

chapters.title: Chapter 1995: Pearl of Abyss!
paragraphs: Revona asked again, "Then what do the devils want in exchange for delaying the war?"
Arvantos’s expression became ugly.
"They want permission to establish a force in the Divine Realm."
The hall instantly became colder.

Arvantos continued, "They also want independent freedom to move throughout the Divine Realm, interact with other forces, and conduct their own affairs, provided they do not openly slaughter our people or destroy our territories."
The ten geniuses frowned almost at the same time.
That condition was far too much.

Letting devils enter the Divine Realm was already dangerous. Allowing them to create their own force and move freely among the sects, clans, empires, and hidden organizations of the Divine Realm was even worse. The devils might not need to slaughter anyone openly. They could tempt ambitious cultivators, corrupt weaker factions, manipulate internal disputes, buy information, plant spies, and slowly create chaos from within.
Max spoke in a solemn voice. "They could corrupt our human forces in no time."

"That is our concern as well," Arvantos said with a sigh. "Many Divine Realm forces look noble on the surface, but greed exists everywhere. There will always be clans hungry for power, sects desperate for forbidden techniques, rulers who want to break through, and traitors willing to sell their own universe for personal gain. The devils understand this. That is why their demand is dangerous."
Morgana sneered. "Then refusing sounds obvious."
"It would be obvious if Varok were only an ordinary envoy," Arvantos said.
Max’s gaze sharpened. "Why not imprison or seal Varok somewhere?"
Everyone looked toward him.

Max remained calm as he continued, "That way, Devil Emperor Abaddon would not know his son is dead, and we would still have around five hundred years to prepare for war. If Varok is the main reason we cannot act, then keeping him alive but sealed should solve the immediate problem."
For a moment, no one spoke.
It was a ruthless suggestion, but no one could deny that it was practical.
Arvantos looked at Max for a few seconds before shaking his head.
"It is not that simple."
Max narrowed his eyes. "Because of Abaddon?"
"Partly," Arvantos said. "But more importantly, because of what Varok carries."

He raised his hand again, and the star map changed. A dark pearl appeared above the image of the devils. It looked small, but the moment its image formed, the space around it seemed to sink inward, as though even the projection of the treasure carried an aura of endless abyss.
"Varok possesses one of the five Primal Treasures," Arvantos said. "It is called the Pearl of Abyss."
The name caused a strange pressure to settle over the hall.

Arvantos’s voice became solemn. "The Pearl of Abyss is not a normal treasure. It contains a power that even we do not fully understand. It can distort space, hide fate traces, open abyssal passages, protect its bearer, and release destructive power far beyond Varok’s own cultivation. If forced into a desperate situation, Varok may activate it."
Damian frowned. "What would happen then?"
"That is exactly the problem," Arvantos replied. "We do not know."
The answer made everyone’s expression darken.

Arvantos continued, "A Primal Treasure is too unpredictable. Each one possesses abilities that surpass ordinary laws. If Varok activates the Pearl of Abyss in the middle of our universe, it may create another passage. It may summon something from the devil universe. It may collapse a star realm into abyssal corruption. It may even allow him to escape and inform Abaddon that we tried to trap him."
He looked at Max. "So sealing him sounds good in theory, but if the Pearl of Abyss reacts before we complete the seal, the consequences may be far worse than letting him remain under observation."
Max remained silent.

Arvantos then explained further, "There are five Primal Treasures in existence, at least according to what we know. We Primordials possess one. The devils possess two. One is the Pearl of Abyss in Varok’s hands, and the other remains in the devil universe, where they are using it to pierce the Wall of Eternity. The fourth is in the possession of the leader of the Angel Race. As for the fifth, its whereabouts are still unknown."
His gaze moved slowly across the ten geniuses.

"You must understand what that means. The devils did not send Varok here merely as a messenger. They sent him with a Primal Treasure because they wanted him to be untouchable, or at least dangerous enough that we would hesitate before acting against him."
The hall became oppressively silent.
The devils were not simply making demands.
They were using Varok as bait, shield, envoy, and threat all at once.
If the Primordials killed him, Abaddon would have a reason to start war.
If they imprisoned him, the Pearl of Abyss might cause a disaster.
If they agreed to his terms, devils would gain a foothold in the Divine Realm.
If they refused outright, the devils might escalate the situation while the Wall of Eternity continued weakening.
Arvantos sighed again, and for the first time, the ten geniuses could clearly see the weight carried by the Primarchs.

"That is why we are in a bind. We cannot trust the devils. We cannot allow them to move freely. We cannot kill Varok carelessly. We cannot ignore the hole in the Wall of Eternity. And we cannot assume five hundred years will be enough."
He looked at them with a solemn expression.
"This is why we summoned all of you."
Max’s eyes sharpened slightly.

Arvantos continued, "The older generation will handle negotiations, defense lines, and the Wall of Eternity. But the future war will not be decided by old strength alone. If the invasion truly expands, your generation will become the blade of this universe."
His voice grew deeper.
"And before that day comes, all of you must become strong enough to survive the battlefield that is coming."
After hearing Arvantos’s words, the ten geniuses fell into a heavy silence.
The pressure on their shoulders seemed to increase a hundredfold in an instant.

chapters.title: Chapter 1996: Training Chamber!
paragraphs: Before this, their desire to grow stronger had been personal. Some wanted to stand at the peak of the Divine Realm. Some wanted to surpass their rivals. Some wanted to prove their bloodlines, inheritances, and talents. Some simply wanted to become strong enough that no one could decide their fate for them.
But now, that desire had changed.
This was no longer only about pride, ambition, or reputation.
Their entire universe was at stake.

If the devils truly widened the hole in the Wall of Eternity, then the war that had nearly destroyed the Divine Realm and Mortal Realm hundreds of thousands of years ago might begin again. If the Angel Race or the Dragon Race moved while the devils invaded, the situation could become even worse.
The ten geniuses standing in this hall were no longer just young talents being nurtured for future glory. They were now part of the universe’s preparation for survival.
Max felt the weight of that truth more clearly than most.

He had already seen too many strange things happen around him. The Voidwalker Clan’s buried history had surfaced. The First Progenitor had spoken to him and warned him about Anover. The devils had appeared in the Divine Realm soon after that warning.
Now Arvantos was telling them that the devils possessed two Primal Treasures, that Varok carried the Pearl of Abyss, and that the Wall of Eternity might fully crack open in about five hundred years.
Five hundred years.
To others, that might sound like a long time.
To Max, it sounded like a countdown.
Arvantos looked at the faces of the ten geniuses and seemed to understand what they were feeling. A faint smile appeared on his face, though the solemnity in his eyes did not fully disappear.

"You do not need to worry too much right now," he said. "The burden of the universe will not be placed on your shoulders today. The older generation will handle the immediate negotiations, the defense lines, the monitoring of the Wall of Eternity, and the meeting with the devils. What you need to do is use the time given to you properly."
His gaze swept across Max, Revona, Damian, Ervin, Morgana, Kaiden, Orion, Rosaline, Rakan, Aurelian, and the others.

"For the next week, all of you will remain inside the Primordial Ancestral Domain until the meeting with the devils ends. During this time, none of you are to leave unless I personally allow it. The Divine Realm may look calm on the surface, but once news of the devils spreads among the top forces, many things will begin moving in the dark. Some people will panic. Some will prepare. Some will scheme. Some may even try to contact the devils for their own benefit."
His voice became deeper.
"You are all too important to be allowed to wander outside without protection right now."
Morgana raised an eyebrow slightly, but she did not argue.

Arvantos continued, "I have great plans for all of you. The Primordial Race has resources, places, and inheritances that are normally not opened even to our own younger generation without strict qualifications. However, the situation has changed. If war is coming, then old rules must give way to survival."
The ten geniuses immediately became more attentive.

Arvantos then said, "Sarvion will take you to the training chambers of the Primordial Race. Those chambers were built to stimulate Primordial bloodline potential, sharpen law comprehension, strengthen bodies, and draw out hidden abilities. Since all of you have already obtained Primordial Bloodline, you may be able to awaken abilities that are still sleeping inside you."
Max’s eyes shifted slightly.
Awaken abilities of the Primordial Bloodline.

His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline had already increased his base strength by ten times, brought him closer to the laws of the world, and strengthened his Pseudo Cosmic Paths. Yet he had always felt that he had not truly unlocked everything hidden inside it.

Compared to his other powers, the Primordial Bloodline felt broad and fundamental, but also strangely incomplete, as though it had given him a foundation first and was waiting for the right environment to reveal more.
A training chamber made by the Primordial Race might be exactly what he needed.
As Arvantos finished speaking, the door of the hall opened.
Sarvion entered calmly.

He looked the same as before, dignified and unreadable, with an aura that seemed restrained yet impossible to ignore. His gaze moved across the ten geniuses, stopping briefly on Max before continuing.
"Let us go," Sarvion said.
Without waiting for anyone to respond, he turned and walked out of the hall.
The ten geniuses followed him.

Max walked with the others, but his thoughts remained heavy. The conversation with Arvantos kept replaying in his mind. The five first races. The Wall of Eternity. The Devil Emperor Abaddon. Varok. The Pearl of Abyss. The Primal Treasures. The possibility that their universe sat at the center of all the others because of some hidden entrance to a god-like realm.
And beneath all of that, one unfinished warning continued echoing quietly.
’Watch out for Anover...’
Max did not know where Anover fit into this.

He did not know whether it was connected to Abaddon, the devils, the Primal Treasures, or something beyond even the five universes. But he had a feeling that the warning was not separate from what was happening now.
Something that could instill fear into the first inheritor of the Dimensional Keeper Legacy wouldn’t be something weak.
Sarvion led them through the Primordial Ancestral Domain.

The path they walked was very different from the halls where they had waited earlier. Those places had been grand, but this route felt older and more secluded. The walls were no longer smooth and polished.
They were made of dark-gold stone filled with natural patterns that looked like veins, stars, and ancient law marks fused together.

Every few steps, Max saw statues of Primordial experts standing along the corridor. Some had humanoid forms. Some had half-transformed bodies. Some looked so ancient and strange that Max could not even tell whether they had once been human-shaped at all.
The deeper they went, the denser the aura became.
It was not energy alone.
It was something heavier, more primitive, and closer to origin.

chapters.title: Chapter 1997: A Piece of Good News!
paragraphs: Max felt his Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline stir inside him as they continued walking. It did not surge violently, but it grew warmer, as though recognizing the place they were approaching.
His laws also became more sensitive. Space, flame, lightning, soul, body, and even his Emotion Severing Path seemed to sharpen slightly under the pressure of the surrounding environment.
The others felt it too.

Orion, who had been restless earlier, grew quiet. Damian’s face became serious. Ervin looked around with intense curiosity. Revona remained calm, but her eyes were no longer as indifferent as before. Even Morgana stopped making sharp remarks as they walked deeper into the ancestral grounds.
After some time, Sarvion stopped before a massive bronze-gold gate.

The gate was so tall that it looked as though it had been built for giants. Countless ancient symbols covered its surface, and at the center of the gate was a circular mark that seemed to contain many layered worlds inside it. The moment Max looked at that mark, his Primordial Bloodline pulsed once.
Sarvion turned back to them.

"This is one of the core training facilities of the Primordial Race," he said. "Normally, even the direct disciples of the Primarchs cannot enter this place casually. The chambers inside will respond differently to each of you. Do not resist the pressure. Do not force a result. Let your bloodline, laws, body, and soul adapt naturally."
He paused briefly before adding, "If your Primordial Bloodline contains dormant abilities, this place will try to awaken them. Whether you succeed or not depends on your own foundation."
Orion grinned again, though his expression carried tension this time. "That sounds dangerous."
Sarvion looked at him calmly. "It is."
Orion’s grin stiffened slightly.
Sarvion placed one hand on the gate.
The bronze-gold symbols lit up one by one.
A deep sound spread through the corridor as the massive gate slowly opened, revealing a vast space beyond it.
Max stepped inside with the others.
The moment he crossed the threshold, the world changed.
At least, that was how it felt to him.

The training room did not look like a normal chamber. From Max’s perspective, it felt more like an entire sealed realm built inside the Primordial Ancestral Domain. The ceiling was so high that it disappeared into a dim golden mist.

The floor beneath his feet was made of smooth dark stone, but countless lines of light flowed through it like molten law veins. In the distance, enormous pillars rose into the mist, and every pillar carried a different aura.

Some burned with primordial flame. Some crackled with ancient lightning. Some released crushing gravity. Some distorted space. Some gave off a soul pressure so dense that even looking at them made Max’s mind tighten.
At the center of the room stood ten circular platforms.

Each platform was surrounded by runes, and above each one floated a pale golden sphere. Those spheres pulsed slowly, like hearts beating in silence. Every pulse released waves of pressure that entered Max’s body and brushed against his Primordial Bloodline.
Max’s eyes narrowed.
The room was testing them already.
He could feel it clearly.
The pressure did not attack him directly. Instead, it passed over him layer by layer, as if measuring his bones, blood, soul, laws, and hidden powers.

His Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline reacted with a faint growl. His Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline released a soft glow. His Voidwalker bloodline remained quiet but alert. His five Divine Veins pulsed one after another. His Dimensional Keeper Legacy watched silently from the depths of his foundation.
Then his Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline finally responded.
A deep, ancient warmth spread through Max’s body.
For a brief moment, Max felt as if the laws of the training room had moved closer to him. The pressure on his shoulders became heavier, but it also felt clearer.
The lines on the floor, the runes around the platforms, the pillars in the distance, and the golden spheres above them all seemed to reveal tiny details that he would not have noticed before.
’So this place is designed to draw out the bloodline’s deeper potential,’ Max thought.
Sarvion’s voice echoed through the training room.

"Choose a platform and sit. Once the chamber activates fully, each of you will be isolated in your own training space. What you see afterward may not be what the others see. The Primordial training chambers do not train everyone in the same way."
Max looked toward the nearest platform.
The golden sphere above it pulsed.
For some reason, he felt it calling to him.

He walked forward and stepped onto the platform. The runes around it lit up beneath his feet, and a circle of golden light rose around him. The sounds of the others faded slightly, as if distance had suddenly stretched between them.
Max sat cross-legged at the center of the platform.
The moment he closed his eyes, the pressure around him changed.
The training room vanished from his senses.
A vast primordial space opened around him, filled with golden mist, ancient law fragments, and a power that seemed to come from the earliest age of the universe.
Max took a slow breath.
His Primordial Bloodline began to awaken further.
At the same time, in the hall they had left behind, another Primordial appeared before Arvantos.
His expression was solemn.
"All the major forces have been informed, including the Four Sacred Clans," the Primordial said. "They will gather here by tonight."
Arvantos nodded lightly. "Good."

The Primordial continued, "Also, only the Wall of Eternity on the side of the Devil Universe has been weakened because of the hole. The boundaries connected to the Spirit Universe, Angel Universe, and Dragon Universe show no sign of damage."
"That is one piece of good news, at least," Arvantos said.
His expression remained grave.
The other three universes had not moved yet.
But Arvantos knew very well that once the devils began stirring the situation, the others would not remain blind forever.
After a moment, both figures vanished from the hall.
The Primordial Ancestral Domain grew quiet again.
Inside the training facility, Max sat alone within his isolated space, unaware of Arvantos’s conversation.
The golden mist around him thickened.
The dormant power inside his Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline began to rise.

Every pulse released waves of pressure that entered Max’s body and brushed against his Primordial Bloodline.
Max’s eyes narrowed.
The room was testing them already.
He could feel it clearly.
The pressure did not attack him directly.
Instead, it passed over him layer by layer, as if measuring his bones, blood, soul, laws, and hidden powers.
His Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline reacted with a faint growl.
His Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline released a soft glow.
His Voidwalker bloodline remained quiet but alert.
His five Divine Veins pulsed one after another.
His Dimensional Keeper Legacy watched silently from the depths of his foundation.
Then his Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline finally responded.
A deep, ancient warmth spread through Max’s body.
For a brief moment, Max felt as if the laws of the training room had moved closer to him.
The pressure on his shoulders became heavier, but it also felt clearer.
The lines on the floor, the runes around the platforms, the pillars in the distance, and the golden spheres above them all seemed to reveal tiny details that he would not have noticed before.
’So this place is designed to draw out the bloodline’s deeper potential,’ Max thought.
Sarvion’s voice echoed through the training room.
"Choose a platform and sit.
Once the chamber activates fully, each of you will be isolated in your own training space.
What you see afterward may not be what the others see.
The Primordial training chambers do not train everyone in the same way."
Max looked toward the nearest platform.
The golden sphere above it pulsed.
For some reason, he felt it calling to him.
He walked forward and stepped onto the platform.
The runes around it lit up beneath his feet, and a circle of golden light rose around him.
The sounds of the others faded slightly, as if distance had suddenly stretched between them.
Max sat cross-legged at the center of the platform.
The moment he closed his eyes, the pressure around him changed.
The training room vanished from his senses.
A vast primordial space opened around him, filled with golden mist, ancient law fragments, and a power that seemed to come from the earliest age of the universe.
Max took a slow breath.
His Primordial Bloodline began to awaken further.
At the same time, in the hall they had left behind, another Primordial appeared before Arvantos.
His expression was solemn.
"All the major forces have been informed, including the Four Sacred Clans," the Primordial said.
"They will gather here by tonight."
Arvantos nodded lightly.
"Good."
The Primordial continued, "Also, only the Wall of Eternity on the side of the Devil Universe has been weakened because of the hole.
The boundaries connected to the Spirit Universe, Angel Universe, and Dragon Universe show no sign of damage."
"That is one piece of good news, at least," Arvantos said.
His expression remained grave.
The other three universes had not moved yet.
But Arvantos knew very well that once the devils began stirring the situation, the others would not remain blind forever.
After a moment, both figures vanished from the hall.
The Primordial Ancestral Domain grew quiet again.
Inside the training facility, Max sat alone within his isolated space, unaware of Arvantos’s conversation.
The golden mist around him thickened.
The dormant power inside his Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline began to rise.

chapters.title: Chapter 1998: Forceful Awakening!
paragraphs: The awakening of a Primordial Bloodline ability was never meant to be a quick process.
For most members of the Primordial Race, awakening a true bloodline ability required decades of slow adaptation. Some needed centuries.

A Primordial had to let the bloodline settle into the body, fuse with the soul, nourish the bones, refine the organs, and gradually change the way their laws interacted with the world. Only after the bloodline became a natural part of their existence would a hidden ability begin to surface.
But Max and the others did not have decades.
They did not even have years.

The devils had already entered their universe, the Wall of Eternity had already been pierced, Varok was walking around with the Pearl of Abyss, and the meeting between the Primordials and the devils would take place in a week.
Because of that, the Primordial Race had chosen a method that was rarely used unless the situation was urgent.
The training facility had been activated at the highest level.
Level Ten Order.

At this level, the chamber no longer guided the bloodline gently. It no longer waited for the body to adapt naturally. Instead, it flooded the cultivator with concentrated primordial source energy and forced the dormant ability within the Primordial Bloodline to awaken ahead of time.
It was a crude method.
It was dangerous.
It was not recommended even among the Primordial Race.

Although the method worked, it often left behind unstable bloodline foundations. Some Primordials suffered torn meridians. Some experienced soul backlash. Some lost control of their bloodline for years afterward. Some even suffered bloodline combustion, where the dormant power ignited violently inside their bodies and burned them from within before stabilizing.
Yet this method had been used before in ancient wars.
When time was short and survival mattered more than perfection, the Primordial Race had always been willing to take risks.
Now, the same method was being used on the ten geniuses.
Inside his isolated training space, Max sat cross-legged within the golden primordial mist.
Time passed strangely here.
The first day was silent.

The golden mist seeped into his body layer by layer, and his Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline responded like a sleeping ancient beast slowly opening its eyes. The energy did not merely enter his veins. It examined them. It pressed against them. It searched for something hidden within the deepest part of his bloodline origin.
On the second day, the pressure increased.

The primordial source energy became heavier and far more aggressive. It entered Max’s blood, bones, soul, and laws at the same time, trying to force the bloodline ability to appear. His five Divine Veins pulsed one after another, helping his body stabilize the impact.

The Vein of Resilience reduced the damage caused by the pressure. The Vein of Vitality repaired the tiny cracks that appeared inside his body. The Vein of Origin anchored his foundation, preventing the primordial force from scattering through him uncontrollably.
On the third day, the first signs of bloodline combustion appeared.
Golden flames suddenly ignited inside Max’s veins.
They were not external flames.
They burned from within his blood.

A sharp heat spread through his body, and for a brief moment, Max felt as if every drop of blood inside him had turned into molten gold. His skin flushed with light, his bones released faint cracking sounds, and ancient primordial runes surfaced briefly across his arms, chest, neck, and face before sinking back into his flesh.
Max opened his eyes slightly.
’So this is the danger Sarvion mentioned.’

He had already realized that the chamber was not training him gently. It was forcing his Primordial Bloodline to reveal something that should have taken years to awaken naturally. The process was effective, but it was also brutal.
The golden flames inside his bloodline tried to burn open the hidden ability, and if his body had been weaker, his bloodline might have collapsed before the ability even appeared.
Fortunately, Max’s body was not normal.
His foundation had been strengthened too many times.

His Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline gave him a terrifying physical body and monstrous vitality. His five Divine Veins reinforced different aspects of his existence. His Dimensional Sovereign Body had already transformed the nature of his physique.

His Voidwalker inheritance had deepened his dimensional foundation. And more importantly, his Unholy Trinity Body seemed capable of containing different kinds of powers without allowing them to destroy one another.
That was the strangest part.
Inside Max, too many powers existed together.

Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline, Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline, Voidwalker bloodline, Dimensional Keeper Legacy, Divine King Punishment, Emotion Severing Path, Devouring Flames, Dimensional Sovereign Body, Dimension of Soul, and his Divine Veins should have made his body a chaotic battlefield.

But the Unholy Trinity Body acted like a terrifying vessel that could hold them all. It did not make every conflict disappear, but it prevented those powers from tearing his body apart whenever they awakened, clashed, or evolved.
Because of that, Max endured the bloodline combustion.
It hurt.
The golden fire burning inside his veins was not something he could ignore, but it did not cripple him. It burned through his blood, and his body repaired the damage just as quickly.

It surged toward his soul, and his Dimension of Soul swallowed much of the impact. It tried to disrupt his law foundation, and his Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline drew the laws closer instead, turning part of the damage into nourishment.
By the fourth day, the other geniuses had already begun awakening their bloodline abilities.

Max could not see them clearly because each platform had isolated its own training space, but he could still sense several violent fluctuations through the chamber. One aura erupted with a crushing force that seemed to distort gravity.

Another released a storm of primordial lightning. Another carried a freezing pressure that slowed the movement of laws. Another burned with a pale golden radiance that made the entire chamber tremble faintly.
They were awakening faster than him.
Not because their foundations were better.
But because their Primordial Bloodlines were lower in level.
Their bloodlines were easier to force open.

The abilities sleeping inside them were powerful, but not as deeply buried as the one inside Max. The lower the level of the Primordial Bloodline, the easier it was for the Level Ten Order to tear open the sealed ability.
That was why some of the others awakened on the second day, and several more awakened on the third and fourth days.
But their success came with a price.
